title: chore: refresh model metadata from LiteLLM 1.108.1
body:
## Summary

Refresh DSPy's bundled metadata from LiteLLM **1.108.0 → 1.108.1** using `python -I -S scripts/update_model_metadata.py 1.108.1`, and fix DSPy's dimension-specific pricing threshold selection exposed by this update. No dependency changes.

Catalog: **4,242 → 4,256 entries; 14 added, zero removed, 25 changed**. Adds Bedrock Claude Platform entries. Existing Gemini/Vertex entries gain audio/cache service-tier rates, long-context flex rates and image priority prices; two image-model deprecation dates are removed. Family rules and license are unchanged. Changed numeric prices are finite and nonnegative.

LiteLLM remains the sole metadata source. Prices are advisory, not an independent provider-billing audit. New metadata does not add support for unmodelled billing dimensions: generated-media costs still return unknown, and DSPy does not start using cache-audio or batch fields merely because they are present.

## Provenance and security

- Release: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/releases/tag/v1.108.1; exact tag commit `93f52b591ee2c91617a8c6975f047f4ad722d7e3`.
- Reviewed release notes and new incident-discussion updates before fetching the candidate. **Forbidden 1.107.0 was excluded and never downloaded.**
- Exact non-yanked PyPI wheel URL is in `provenance.json`; SHA-256 `cffb9e312baa9f229bdfb94df75c99a321a594e23ec1b26214bc10d5f8e5a23b` verified before extraction.
- Extracted JSON is byte-identical to official tagged source. License matches both tagged source and the current bundled license. Snapshot SHA-256: `a8098ad1968af56fde2076cf859b5dc91037246310135b26748a500fc0656454`.
- Wheel inspected as ZIP data only, never installed, imported or executed. No `.pth`, `cook.py`, `sitecustomize.py`, `usercustomize.py` or `purelib` payload paths. This is a scoped data/provenance review, not a full wheel security audit or cryptographic build-provenance assurance.

## Verification

- Daily metadata tests on current main: **53 passed**; final candidate: **57 passed**.
- Forced-local `python -m pytest tests/clients tests/adapters -q` after review fix: **1566 passed, 18 skipped** (includes metadata tests).
- Applicable pre-commit hooks, including types, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Existing test environment statically inspected before use; pre-existing LiteLLM 1.96.0, not candidate code. No paid/live provider calls locally.

## Greptile follow-up: independent pricing thresholds

Confirmed the reported integration bug: audio-only long-context fields introduced a threshold that DSPy applied to unrelated text rates. With the actual 1.108.1 snapshot, Vertex `gemini-3-flash-preview` at 200001 input/5 output tokens returned unknown before the fix; after it estimates $0.1000155. No generated data was overridden.

Threshold selection now belongs to each billed dimension, duration and service tier. Missing cache/reasoning rates fall back to the corresponding ordinary dimension's independently selected rate; priority never falls back to standard. A controlled-fixture regression covers both sides of 200000 tokens, distinct text/audio thresholds, default/priority isolation and cache/reasoning fallback. All four cases failed before and pass after.

title: fix(rlm): render REPL code and output as plain text in prompts
body:
### Problem

RLM renders its REPL history (the model's code and whatever that code printed) into every action and extract prompt. Adapters expand custom-type markers they find in prompt text into content parts. So a marker inside REPL history became real content in the next prompt:

- `print(photo)` for a `dspy.Image` put the image itself into the root model's prompt. RLM's design assumes the root model sees variables only as text.
- A marker written by hand in code or output became whatever parts it described, including path-based parts that are resolved while the request is built.

### Change

```{ .diff file="dspy/primitives/repl_types.py" }
         text = f"=== Step {index + 1} ===\n{reasoning_line}Code:\n{code_block}\n{self.format_output(self.output, max_output_chars)}"
// @annotation Applied to the finished entry text, after truncation, so no marker pair can survive or be formed by cutting the output.
+        return text.replace(CUSTOM_TYPE_START_IDENTIFIER, "[CUSTOM-TYPE-START]").replace(
+            CUSTOM_TYPE_END_IDENTIFIER, "[CUSTOM-TYPE-END]"
+        )
// @endannotation
```

`REPLHistory` serializes through `REPLEntry.format` for every adapter, so this covers action prompts and the max-iterations extract step. REPL history is now always text. Not affected:

- inputs passed to RLM
- `llm_query` prompts
- tool results and outputs

### Proof

- `test_repl_code_and_output_stay_text_in_the_next_prompt` (LocalInterpreter and Deno) prints a hand-written path-based marker and a real `dspy.Image` marker, then checks the next root request.
  - Before: `{'document', 'image', 'text'}` parts.
  - After: only text, with the inert identifiers.
- Full suite on `fd1dfc6aa` plus this change, without LiteLLM: 3496 passed. The 4 failures also fail on main (`test_lm15_subtree_updater` ×3, `test_usage_tracker_in_parallel`).

### Notes

- **Unmerged History stack:** the History stack (#10387 and its corrections) renders replayed REPL events in `format_repl_event`, outside `REPLEntry.format`, and will need the same rule there.
- **Marker forgery elsewhere:** markers in other untrusted text (string inputs, tool results) are a separate question, tracked internally.

title: [B] feat(rlm): images in RLM's REPL: to_pil, Pillow in the sandbox, llm_query lists
body:
**Draft for review.** Stacked on **[A] #10809** → H #10827 → S #10812 → main 2a7acc6d (S→H→A→B; no merges yet). Commits (cherry-picked with `-x`, no conflicts):
1. `feat(rlm): images in RLM's REPL: to_pil, Pillow in the sandbox, llm_query lists`
2. `feat(rlm): Pyodide packages for the sandbox: PythonInterpreter(sandbox_packages=...), Pillow by default`
3. `test: stub _plan with its sandbox_packages argument in the download-retry test` (#10817's stub, for `_plan(deno_dir, packages)`)
4. `test(rlm): image-valued extraction fallback stays a text preview in replay` (12 public cases from the History review: three adapters × live/JSON-restored History × sync/async; this is their first stage where an Image input reaches the REPL)

### Problem

With [A], RLM's REPL holds real `dspy.Image`s: as inputs, as tool arguments and results, and in `SUBMIT`. The code still can't look at them:

```python
# inside dspy.RLM's REPL, photo: dspy.Image   (executed on [A], Local and Deno)
photo.to_pil()                              # AttributeError: no to_pil
llm_query(["Read the text in this image.", photo])
# → TypeError: Object of type Image is not JSON serializable
```

And Pyodide's sandbox has no Pillow, so cropping in code is impossible under the default interpreter. #10790 (Flex libraries) would have provided Pillow, but it is out of 3.5.

### Change

- **`dspy.Image.to_pil()`** decodes an embedded image (`ImportError` without Pillow; `ValueError` for a remote URL). `dspy.Image(pil_image)` already goes the other way.
- **Pyodide packages for the sandbox: `PythonInterpreter(sandbox_packages=("pillow",))`.** It names packages Pyodide ships (by the names in [its package list](https://pyodide.org/en/0.29.4/usage/packages-in-pyodide.html)) that a sandbox with dspy gets, with their dependencies from Pyodide's lock file. They're sha256-pinned and fetched once when the bundle is built, with no network at runtime. The default, Pillow (11.3.0 for Pyodide 0.29.4), is what `to_pil()` needs. Whether the host has Pillow doesn't matter: Pillow isn't a dspy dependency, and the sandbox never uses the host's copy.

```python
# numpy as well as Pillow
dspy.RLM(sig, interpreter_factory=functools.partial(dspy.PythonInterpreter, sandbox_packages=["pillow", "numpy"]))
# no packages: a smaller bundle (34.1 vs 38.6 MB) that starts slightly faster
dspy.configure(interpreter_factory=functools.partial(dspy.PythonInterpreter, sandbox_packages=[]))
```

  - **Without Pillow,** images still pass through the REPL, `llm_query`, tools and `SUBMIT`; only `to_pil()` raises, with an `ImportError` naming the parameter.
  - **Passing it through the factory** gives nested RLMs and `InterpreterPool` the same packages.
  - **No environment variable.** Unlike `DSPY_SANDBOX_CACHE`, this isn't a deployment constraint, and `dspy.configure` already sets it globally.

```{ .diff file="dspy/primitives/sandbox_bundle.py" }
// @annotation The old check made sandbox capability follow host packages: plain `pip install dspy` got no Pillow, while dev installs, CI and our tests did.
-    if "pillow" in lock and importlib.util.find_spec("PIL") is not None:
-        shipped.append("pillow")  # what dspy.Image converts to and from (Image.to_pil), when this environment has it
+    shipped += packages
// @endannotation
```

```{ .diff file="dspy/primitives/sandbox_bundle.py" }
// @annotation RLM runs without a bundle when it can't build one (offline, say) and only logs a warning. A misspelled package must not take that path, so unknown names raise ValueError outside the guard.
+        unknown = [name for name in packages if name not in _guarded(_pyodide_lock, deno_dir)]
+        if unknown:
+            raise ValueError(
// @endannotation
```

  The names are normalized and sorted, then become part of the per-process bundle plan cache key, the bundle digest (its wheel list) and the build-failure key. Each set gets its own cached bundle, whatever the order or spelling, and a failed build of one doesn't block another.
  - **Relation to #10790** (out of 3.5): its `libraries=[module]` adds your own modules through the host's installed distributions. If it lands later, it can feed the Pyodide packages those libraries need into this same list, rather than a second package mechanism.
- **`llm_query` and `llm_query_batched` take lists** of strings and DSPy values, sent as one user message with the LM's generation defaults:

```text
sandbox: llm_query(["Read this label", crop])
  sandbox_guest.bind wraps llm_query like SUBMIT     → the prompt crosses on the session's wire, in [A]'s session envelope
host: llm_query(prompt)
  read_wire(prompt)                                   → ["Read this label", dspy.Image]
  str → TextPart; a value → #10737's _tool_result_content → ImagePart / JSON text
  lm(build_request(lm, Prompt([Message.user(parts)])))
```

```{ .diff file="dspy/predict/rlm.py" }
+    for item in prompt:
// @annotation Unlike the old [3/3], a string never goes through marker expansion, so a marker written into one stays text instead of becoming media or naming a host file.
+        content = item if isinstance(item, str) else _tool_result_content(item)
+        parts += [TextPart(text=content)] if isinstance(content, str) else content
// @endannotation
```

- A string prompt is unchanged. A plain callable `sub_lm` keeps string prompts and raises a clear `TypeError` for lists.
- The list crosses on [A]'s wire, not as prompt-marker text (the old [3/3]). There's no second representation.

### Proof: executed

- **Restacked head (`94c049d6`, replayed unchanged onto A `7ffc25d2`):** the production tree equals the reviewed #10825 head merged with main 2a7acc6d, plus H's one-line `REPLEntry.max_output_chars = 10_000` default (`dspy/` tree `c44b83f9`), plus exactly A's review fixes (nested `SandboxSerializable` in user models, kept only where the ordinary dump has its str, so a user's serializer that reads one still gets its str; callable tools' `__call__` return hints; see #10809). Credential-free full suite: 3753 passed; the only failures are 3 `lm15_subtree_updater` tests that fail locally on main too. Public boundary probe on Local and Deno: printed images, code markers and a forged host-file marker stay text, now and on History replay (live and JSON-restored); `SUBMIT` returns a typed `dspy.Image`; `llm_query([text, image])` reaches the sub-LM as text + image. A fresh matched V* run on this stack tip follows. Earlier V* scores stay labeled with their own heads (most recently #10825's 85599c8d). The evidence below was gathered on the earlier heads, before the restack.

- **Live** (`gpt-6-sol` on Azure, Responses route, default `PythonInterpreter`, install **without LiteLLM**, at the first pushed head `fcc2cc057`; the later review fix only changes how `SUBMIT`/`llm_query` values are marked). An RLM got a 1600×1000 photo and was asked for the lot number on a small sticker. It returned `4471-Q` and a 220×110 sticker crop as its image output, after this REPL code:
  ```python
  im = photo.to_pil()                      # Pillow inside Pyodide
  print(llm_query(["Describe the image and locate the small sticker...", photo]))
  tight = im.crop((1370, 865, 1590, 975)) # → "LOT 4471-Q / EXP 2027-03"
  print(llm_query(["Transcribe the sticker exactly.", sticker]))
  SUBMIT(lot, {"url": sticker.url})
  ```
  3 sub-LM calls carried image parts.
- **Tests** (Local and Deno): `TestRLMImages` covers:
  - `to_pil` cropping of an image longer than the variable preview
  - the exact parts and LM defaults `llm_query`/`llm_query_batched` send
  - images built in the REPL
  - a forged marker string staying text
  - a callable `sub_lm`
  - JSON with a `__dspy__` key in a prompt list staying JSON text (fails on the first pushed head `fcc2cc057`)

  Plus `to_pil` unit tests, and for the Pillow policy:
  - `PythonInterpreter.provide_dspy` with host Pillow hidden:
    - Pillow (and its dependencies) by default; none with `[]`; numpy added with `["NumPy", "pillow"]`
    - one bundle per set, whatever the order or spelling, each reused
    - `ValueError` for an unknown name; `TypeError` for a string instead of a list

    The default case fails on the first commit, whose plan was empty.
  - a Deno RLM with `sandbox_packages=[]`: `to_pil()` raises the `ImportError`, the image returns through `SUBMIT` unchanged, and the sub-LM gets an image part

  Full suite without LiteLLM at `496927772`: 3654 passed, plus the 4 failures that also fail on main. In a venv **without Pillow or LiteLLM**: `test_rlm.py` + `test_python_interpreter.py` 426 passed, 9 skipped (tests that need host Pillow to make images).
- **Public stories without host Pillow** (`496927772`, Pillow and LiteLLM absent, `call` and `acall`; script `pillow_policy_stories.py`):

  | interpreter | `to_pil()` in the REPL | image through `SUBMIT` | sub-LM got an image part |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Deno, default | decodes; reads the right pixel; returns a crop | yes | yes |
  | Deno, `sandbox_packages=[]` | `ImportError` naming the parameter | yes, unchanged | yes |
  | `LocalInterpreter` (host env) | `ImportError` | yes, unchanged | yes |

  Also:
  - **Adding numpy:** `["pillow", "numpy"]` reads the decoded image with `np.asarray(...)`, shape `(4, 6, 3)`.
  - **A typo:** `["nump"]` raises `ValueError` from a plain RLM instead of degrading to a warning.
  - **The host's own `to_pil()`** raises the same `ImportError`.
  - **The cache** holds one bundle per set: 38.6 MB (Pillow), 34.1 MB (none), 52.8 MB (Pillow and numpy).
- **On main's `InterpreterPool` and snapshots** (this diff applied to main `ef7914672` in a scratch tree; not pushed): two pools, default and `sandbox_packages=[]`, alternating twice. Each used its own bundle and its own `.snap` (snapshots are named after the bundle), both were reused, and `PIL` was importable only in the default sandbox.
- **Public robustness probe** (at `fcc2cc057`; 22 scripted cases; DummyLM records what the LM received). 15/22 pass on Local and 13/22 on Deno. Covered: large inputs (no base64 in the root preview), `to_pil`, exact pixels in `llm_query` and batched, sub-agents, typed tools, containers and `Optional`, async, cross-cell persistence, History replay, and Flex. Remaining:
  - c08/c08b/c10: written for the old contract, which reconstructed user models in the sandbox
  - c09/f03: aliased tool arguments, which need [A]'s open decision
  - c12: Deno async tool under `acall`, a pre-existing main bug fixed by #10808
  - c16: nested RLM under Deno gets dicts (inherited `_in_sandbox`)
  - c14/f04: informational

### Runtime cost

- **The Pillow wheel makes every Deno sandbox start slower by default**, including plain RLMs and Flex; `sandbox_packages=[]` avoids it. Each added package adds its own start cost (numpy: +14 MB of bundle). Since #10776, the runner unpacks the dspy bundle when the sandbox starts, before any code runs, and Pillow adds ~4.5 MB to it (34.0 → 38.5 MB). Measured against [A] on the same machine: plain RLM 1.065–1.080 s on [A] vs 1.084–1.127 s here; `SandboxSerializable` input 2.38–2.44 s vs 2.46–2.51 s (3 alternating rounds × 10 calls), so about +0.02–0.05 s per sandbox start. The first bundle build also downloads the 1 MB wheel once.
- **`to_pil()`, `llm_query` lists:** no cost unless called.

### Implementation notes and risks

- **Pillow is required in Pyodide's lock file.** If a future Pyodide upgrade dropped it, the default bundle would fail to build instead of quietly losing Pillow; the Deno tests would catch that at the upgrade.
- **`LocalInterpreter` still uses the host's Pillow**, by design: it runs in your environment.
- **`llm_query` lists need dspy in the REPL**, which RLM loads when an input, output or tool return involves a dspy type, or when code imports dspy. An RLM with none of those can still build an image and pass it, because importing dspy wraps `llm_query`.
- **Your own `dspy.Type` subclasses render as their fields** in `llm_query` lists: per #10776 they cross as plain data, without their `format()`. dspy's `Image`, `Audio` and `File` become content parts.
- **A value inside a non-string item** (say, a dict holding a marker string) still goes through `_tool_result_content`, as tool results do, so `_refuse_host_files` still checks every request for host paths.

### Release note

- RLM's REPL can work with images: `dspy.Image.to_pil()`, and `llm_query`/`llm_query_batched` accept lists of strings and images.
- `PythonInterpreter(sandbox_packages=...)` chooses the packages Pyodide ships that RLM and Flex sandboxes can import. The default is `("pillow",)`, whether or not Pillow is installed on the host, which costs about +0.03 s per sandbox start; `[]` leaves it out.

main 2a7acc6d
└─ S  #10812  REPL code/output stay plain text (unchanged, dc9070221)

Commits (cherry-picked with `-x`, no conflicts):
1. `feat(dspy): one path for custom values into RLM and Flex sandboxes`
2. `fix(rlm): read back only SUBMIT values the REPL encoded; keep each codec's payload bound`
3. `fix(rlm): rebind SUBMIT for code that imports dspy itself`
4. `fix(rlm): rebind SUBMIT only in a REPL whose session is installed` (needed since main's #10777 snapshots preload the guest module)
5. `Align RLM positional tool calls across interpreters` (Local binds positional calls before `Tool` validation; sandbox `HostTool` rejects surplus positional arguments instead of dropping them)
6. `test(rlm): continue from a JSON-restored History after custom inputs` (moved unchanged from #10825, the first stage where custom inputs reach the REPL)
7. `fix(rlm): keep sandbox values a user's model holds; read callable tools' return types from __call__` (Greptile review of this PR, beyond #10825; see below)
8. `fix(rlm): a user's serializer that reads a sandbox value it holds gets its str, as before` (independent review of commit 7)
9. `fix(rlm): keep a user's sandbox value only where the ordinary dump has its str` (independent review of commit 8; replaces its detection)

### Problem

There are two ways to get a custom value into a sandbox:

1. **#10776's wire.** The host and the sandbox each run a `Wire`: `encode` turns a value into JSON, with tagged nodes for dspy's own classes (`dspy.Image`, …) and plain dicts for your models; `decode` rebuilds it on the other side. Flex inputs and outputs, `HostTool` calls and sandboxed LM calls use it.
2. **`SandboxSerializable`** (public since 3.3). A value supplies four methods (`sandbox_setup`, `to_sandbox`, `sandbox_assignment`, `rlm_preview`), and a separate RLM-only injector runs them once for top-level RLM inputs.

RLM's own paths use neither: its inputs, its tool results and `SUBMIT` go through the interpreter's JSON. So the same value behaves differently depending on where it enters. Executed on the base with the public API and scripted actions:

| Public program | Base, `LocalInterpreter` | Base, Deno (default) | This PR, both |
|---|---|---|---|
| RLM input `nums: Numbers` (a `SandboxSerializable`), mutated and summed | `list`, 12 | `list`, 12 | `list`, 12 (unchanged) |
| Flex input `nums: Numbers` | `str` `'NUMBERS_STR'`; none of the four methods run | same | `list` `[3, 8]` |
| RLM tool `-> Numbers` | `TypeError: Object of type Numbers is not JSON serializable` | **silently** `str` `'NUMBERS_STR'` | `list` `[4, 5]` |
| Same tool without a return annotation | same `TypeError` | **silently** `str` | `TypeError: Tool … returned Numbers, which reaches RLM's REPL only when the tool's return annotation names it` |
| Flex tool returning `Numbers` | `str` | `str` | `list` `[4, 5]` |
| RLM input `photo: dspy.Image` | `variables must be JSON-compatible`, before the first LM call | `str` (marker text) | `Image` |
| RLM tool `-> dspy.Image`, result passed to `ocr(image: dspy.Image)` | `TypeError: … Image is not JSON serializable` | `Arg image is invalid: '<<CUSTOM-TYPE…' is not of type 'object'` | `Image`, and the host tool gets an `Image` |
| Flex: `ocr(image=photo)` | host tool gets an `Image` | `Arg image is invalid: '<<CUSTOM-TYPE…'` | host tool gets an `Image` |
| RLM `SUBMIT(same=photo)` for `same: dspy.Image` | `variables must be JSON-compatible` | `ImagePart.data must be a valid base64 string` (the preview cut the base64) | `Image` |

### Change

Every value the interpreter's JSON can't carry crosses on #10776's wire. A `SandboxSerializable` becomes one kind of value on it, not a second mechanism:

```text
host                                              sandbox
RLM input      HostValues.encode ─▶ JSON ─▶ GuestValues.decode  (once per call)
Flex input     same (already)
tool result    same
tool argument  read by the tool's declared types ◀ GuestValues.encode
SUBMIT         HostValues.decode, then RLM's output parsing ◀ GuestValues.encode
```

```{ .diff file="dspy/primitives/sandbox_guest.py" }
+        if isinstance(value, SandboxSerializable):  # its own codec, before any other form its class has
+            return self.encode_codec(value)
```

- **`Wire.encode_codec`** writes a `{"__dspy__": "codec", "setup", "assign", "name", "text" | "base64"}` node from the four methods. Each value's payload gets its own name, which stays bound in the REPL, so an assignment like `{var} = lambda: {data}` keeps working, as with `_raw_<name>` on main. Only `GuestValues` runs it (in the REPL namespace, so the setup's imports stay in scope); the base `Wire.decode_codec`, used on the host, raises. An in-process interpreter (`InMemory`) rebuilds a host value in its namespace.
- **RLM** injects inputs that are or hold a `dspy.Type` or `SandboxSerializable` once, through the session (`_prepare_serializable_vars`), and loads dspy in the REPL when an input, an output annotation or a tool's return annotation involves one. Every out-of-process session runs one prelude line before each execution. Once the REPL has imported dspy (at setup, or later in the code itself), the line rebinds the tools and `SUBMIT`, because `LocalInterpreter` redefines them every time. Before that it does nothing. Side effect: `LocalInterpreter` error line numbers are one higher, for every RLM. The wrapped `SUBMIT` sends each value in an envelope marked with the session's id (`{"__dspy__": "wire", "session", "value"}`), and the host decodes only those (`read_wire`), so plain JSON that happens to have a `__dspy__` key is never mistaken for a wire value, whether or not the REPL loaded dspy.
- **The RLM-only injector and `_TypeValues` are gone.** There's no fallback that runs the four methods directly.
- **`Tool`'s schema check** reads a model or custom type by its fields, keyed by validation name, instead of its prompt rendering. `dspy.Type` keeps its fields in a `round_trip` dump.

What implementers write: nothing new. The 3.3 `DataFrame` example in the docs is unchanged, and the same value now also works as a Flex input and as a tool result.

### Behavior changes and limits (please judge these)

- **RLM tool results need a return annotation to keep a custom type.** A tool that returns a `dspy.Image` or `SandboxSerializable` without saying so now raises `Tool 'x' returned Corpus, which reaches RLM's REPL only when the tool's return annotation names it, e.g. -> Corpus`. Before, Local raised `not JSON serializable` and Deno silently passed `str(value)`. RLM decides from annotations because loading dspy in the REPL costs ~0.5–1.5 s per call (see below), and plain RLMs shouldn't pay that. Flex always loads dspy, so it has no such limit.
- **An interpreter that can't load dspy now raises for these inputs.** Examples: a restricted compiler that rejects the bootstrap, or a Deno sandbox with no cached bundle while offline. They used to run the four methods directly. Release-note item.
- **One-way.** A `SandboxSerializable` that comes back via `SUBMIT` or a tool argument is plain data. There's no inverse method.
- **Code written in the sandbox never runs on the host.** A `SandboxSerializable` defined by sandboxed code and passed to a host tool is refused (`Only the sandbox rebuilds a SandboxSerializable value`); the tool doesn't run and the setup doesn't execute.
- **Your own models and `dspy.Type` subclasses arrive as plain data**, per #10776; their methods stay on the host. dspy's classes arrive as themselves. A `SandboxSerializable` one of your models (or dataclasses) holds crosses in its own form inside that plain data; the model's field serializers, aliases and `exclude=True` still apply.
- **Not in this PR:** host-side validation of aliased tool arguments (the sandbox-side schema check still rejects aliased models, as on #10776). That would wrap raw Flex functions in `dspy.Tool` in #10776's facade and needs its own decision.

### Runtime cost (executed, same machine, scripted actions, no LM)

Median seconds per `RLM.__call__`, after one warm-up call, 2 alternating rounds × 5 calls per tree:

| RLM program | `LocalInterpreter`: base → this PR | Deno: base → this PR |
|---|---|---|
| No custom values (1 cell, 5 cells, or a string tool) | 0.04–0.06 → 0.04–0.06 | 1.06–1.11 → 1.07–1.08 |
| `SandboxSerializable` input | 0.04–0.05 → **0.54–0.55** | 1.09–1.10 → **2.38–2.44** |
| `dspy.Image` input (1 or 5 cells) | fails → 0.52–0.56 | fails → 2.48–2.56 |

Deno no-custom-values and `SandboxSerializable` rows: this PR's tree against the base, 3 alternating rounds × 10 calls. The Local rows and the image rows come from the run with [B] on top, which doesn't change the Local path; on Deno, [B] adds Pillow, measured there. These are wall-clock medians on one orb, not a benchmark suite.

- **Plain RLMs** (no custom values anywhere) take the same path as before and cost the same.
- **The cost is loading dspy in the REPL**, paid once per call, by RLMs whose inputs, outputs or tool results involve a dspy type or `SandboxSerializable`. Extra REPL cells cost nothing measurable (the prelude is one line).
- **`SandboxSerializable` inputs get slower** (+0.5 s Local, +1.5 s Deno), because the old injector didn't need dspy in the REPL. Options if that matters: accept it; decode codec nodes in the bootstrap without importing dspy (same wire format, smaller decoder); or reuse interpreters across calls.

### Proof: executed

- **Review fixes on this PR (`9c1ff864`, commit 7), production beyond #10825 + main:**
  - *Nested `SandboxSerializable` in a user's model became its `str`.* `HostValues.encode_object` dumped the whole model to plain data first. The dump now keeps such values themselves (through the serialization context for model fields, the fallback for other values) and the wire sends them in their own form. Pydantic's own semantics stay: field serializers, `by_alias=False`, `exclude=True`.
  - *A callable tool object with a quoted, postponed return annotation (`async def __call__(self) -> 'dspy.Image'`) was rejected.* `_tool_returns` now reads hints from `__call__`, as `Tool` does for arguments.
  - *Commits 8–9 (`dc46b324`, `7ffc25d2`):* commit 7's placeholder changed what a wrap field serializer that reads the value receives (`handler(value).upper()`, `str(handler(value)).upper()`, `len(handler(value))`). Commit 8 detected some reads; commit 9 replaces that. The host now dumps the value twice: as before (each `SandboxSerializable` as its str), and with a fresh random placeholder per value. The result is the ordinary dump everywhere, except where the ordinary dump has exactly a value's str and the other dump has that value's placeholder unchanged; there the value crosses in its own form. So every serializer's output is what it writes from its ordinary input, and in a model that mixes a serializer-read value with an untouched one, the untouched one is still rebuilt. Cost: a user value that holds a `SandboxSerializable` is dumped twice, and its serializers run twice. Test `test_a_users_serializer_that_reads_a_sandbox_value_gets_its_str` (mixed model, `str(handler(value)).upper()`) fails on `dc46b324` and passes here. The reviewer's suites pass here: 8 wrap cases, 24 read controls (uppercase, length, mixed × input/tool result × Local/Deno × sync/async; the first 16 pass on `c11e9cde`, fail on `dc46b324`), and the original 28.
  - New tests (fail on `c11e9cde`, pass here, Local and Deno): `test_a_users_model_crosses_as_its_own_dump_with_the_sandbox_values_it_holds` (input and tool result, serializer/exclude controls) and a callable-object case in `test_tools_with_quoted_postponed_return_annotations_return_images`. The independent reviewer's 28 public probes (model input, model tool, serializer model and list control × Local/Deno × sync/async; callable, async callable and function control) went from 20 fail / 8 pass to 28 pass.
- **Stack tip:** #10810 replayed unchanged on top (`94c049d6`); its `dspy/` tree is `c44b83f9` (the reviewed #10825 head merged with main 2a7acc6d, plus H's one-line `REPLEntry.max_output_chars = 10_000` default) plus exactly commits 7–9's production diff. Credential-free full suite at the stack tip: 3753 passed; the only failures are 3 `lm15_subtree_updater` tests that fail locally on main too. The evidence below was gathered on the earlier heads, before the restack.

- **Tests.** New public-API tests on `LocalInterpreter` and Deno: `TestSandboxValues` in `tests/predict/test_rlm.py`, plus two Flex tests in `tests/flex/test_flex_interpreter.py`. They cover:
  - inputs rebuilt once, with changes kept across executions (text, 1.2 MB and binary payloads)
  - tool results with and without annotations
  - images as inputs, tool arguments and results, and `SUBMIT`, across two executions
  - explicit `SandboxSerializable` precedence over the dspy-type default
  - REPL edge cases (a shadowed tool name, `from __future__`, quoted postponed annotations)
  - the in-process and no-bridge interpreters
  - Flex inputs and tool results
  - the host refusing sandbox-made values

  On the base, 9 of these fail and the 3 compatibility ones pass (inputs rebuilt, in-process). The four old tests that asserted the injector's generated code are replaced.

Also code that imports dspy itself and `SUBMIT`s an image in a later execution (fails on Local at `9f6981672`). The reviewer's public probe (8/8) and boundary probe (8/8) pass at this head on Local and Deno, with LiteLLM imports blocked. title: fix(dspy): await async tools under RLM.acall in PythonInterpreter
body:
**Problem.** `RLM.acall` with an `async def` tool fails on the default `PythonInterpreter` (Deno/Pyodide). The REPL sees `RuntimeError: This event loop is already running`, and Python warns `coroutine ... was never awaited`. The same program works with sync `RLM(...)`, and with `LocalInterpreter` on both paths.

```python
async def lookup(sku: str) -> str: ...
rlm = dspy.RLM("sku -> answer", tools=[lookup])  # default PythonInterpreter
await rlm.acall(sku="A1")                         # REPL code calls lookup(sku=sku) → "This event loop is already running"
```

**Cause.** Under `acall`, the REPL code runs on the caller's event-loop thread. `PythonInterpreter`'s `_await_in_sync` then calls `loop.run_until_complete(...)` on that running loop, which asyncio always rejects.

**Fix.** `PythonInterpreter` now uses `LocalInterpreter`'s existing `_await_in_sync` and deletes its own copy. Both interpreters now share one implementation:
- No running loop: `asyncio.run`, as before.
- Running loop: `asyncio.run` on a separate thread that copies the caller's contextvars, and blocks until the result arrives.

Sync calls are unchanged.

**Proof (executed, without LiteLLM installed).**
- **Regression test:** `TestRLMWithDummyLM::test_acall_awaits_async_tools_e2e`. It covers an async tool result under `acall`, a contextvar set by the caller being visible in the tool, and an async tool's `KeyError` reaching REPL code as `RuntimeError`. It fails before this change and passes after.
- **Public-API matrix:** {async tool, sync tool, async tool that raises} × {`rlm(...)`, `await rlm.acall(...)` with another task running on the loop} × {`PythonInterpreter`, `LocalInterpreter`}.
  - Before: 2 of 12 fail, both Deno + `acall`.
  - After: 12/12 pass, with no un-awaited coroutine warnings and no lingering threads.
- **Same check on open stacks:** applied to #10776 (`84a0084ba`) and to the integrated History + images head (`9ca8890e5`), with the same before/after matrix result. The full suite on each shows only the 4 failures that also fail on main (3 in `test_lm15_subtree_updater`, plus `test_usage_tracker_in_parallel`).

**Scope and caveats.**
- `acall` still runs the REPL code itself synchronously on the loop thread, for both interpreters, so the loop stays blocked during a code cell. This fix doesn't change that.
- An async tool now runs on its own short-lived loop. Objects bound to the caller's loop (for example an `aiohttp` session created there) can't be awaited inside it. This matches `LocalInterpreter`.

Written with Amp in a session directed by @isaacbmiller.

title: fix(dspy): accept XMLAdapter field closed before the next field on the same line
body:
Since #10402, a multiline text field in XMLAdapter only ends at a closing tag that is followed by a newline. A response like

```
<answer>
Paris
</answer><count>2</count>
```

now fails with `Missing closing tag for answer` (3.4.1 parsed it), so the default adapter falls back to JSONAdapter or raises, and a StreamListener on `answer` never ends.

This lets the closing tag also end the field when a tag follows on the same line. The existing sibling-boundary check still decides, so a literal `</answer>` followed by non-field markup stays in the value.

Tests: parse cases for the same-line forms, a guard for the literal case, and a streaming test over chunk sizes 1/7/1000. The new tests fail on main and pass with the change; the full suite passes.

AI disclosure: this came from a sweep for issues, not from normal usage. I used Claude Code to build a differential harness (format then parse round trips, streaming vs one-shot parsing, and 3.4.1 vs main), to narrow the root cause, write the fix and tests, and open this PR at my request. The repro was checked on both 3.4.1 and main. title: Validate ensemble size at compile time
body:
Fixes #10752.

`Ensemble(size=N)` currently accepts a negative `N` or an `N` larger than the number of programs, and only fails later inside `random.sample` when the compiled program is invoked, which hides the configuration error behind a low-level traceback.

This validates the size in `compile()`, where the set of programs is known:

- negative sizes raise `ValueError` at compile time;
- sizes larger than `len(programs)` raise `ValueError` at compile time;
- `size=None` and `size=0` keep their existing semantics (use every program).

Regression tests cover the two invalid configurations and the `size=0` behavior.

```
pytest tests/teleprompt/test_ensemble.py -q
8 passed
```

title: Let PythonInterpreter sandboxes import dspy
body:
Merge train, part 1 of 3: #10801 → #10776 → #10777. This one goes first.

`PythonInterpreter.provide_dspy()` makes `import dspy` work inside the Pyodide sandbox, with the same dspy source the host runs. Nothing calls it yet: #10776 moves Flex and RLM onto it. I split this out of #10776 because it's packaging rather than dspy logic, and it reads better on its own.

The sandbox has no network, so the host builds a zip of dspy and everything its installed metadata says it needs, at any depth. Packages Pyodide ships come from Pyodide's own builds, checked against the hashes in Pyodide's lock file, and the others are copied from this environment if they're pure Python. As with the standard library archive from #10775, a Deno run that executes no sandboxed code byte-compiles it once into the sandbox cache, and the runner unpacks it into site-packages before any code runs. With the cache off (`DSPY_SANDBOX_CACHE=0`), each process builds its own in a temporary directory, removed when it exits.

Worth a closer look:

- Which files get bundled. From an install, its RECORD says. From a git checkout, it's what git tracks plus Python files git doesn't ignore, so a `.env` or credentials next to the source never go in. Outside git, only Python source and the package data pyproject.toml declares.
- The bundle's name is a hash of its files' sizes and modification times, so editing a dspy file makes a new bundle on the next start. Only the three most recently used bundles are kept, and an older one is removed only after nothing has used it for an hour, since other processes may be building or using bundles at the same time.
- The first build downloads Pyodide's wheels from jsDelivr, unless Deno's cache already has them. Offline before that, `provide_dspy()` raises `SandboxBundleError`.
- Pyodide can't start threads, so with the bundle installed the runner replaces `ThreadPoolExecutor` with one that runs each call right away. dspy's parallel helpers then run one call after another in the sandbox.

title: Deprecate TwoStepAdapter in DSPy 3.5
body:
## Problem
Implements [CMP-1400](https://linear.app/cmpnd/issue/CMP-1400): deprecate `dspy.TwoStepAdapter` in **3.5**, remove in **3.6**. #10628 fixed a history compatibility bug; it did not deprecate the adapter.

Warn on construction (`DeprecationWarning`, `stacklevel=2`), add class/API/guide notices, and retain all inference behavior and exports. Public-API regression: `dspy.TwoStepAdapter(dspy.utils.DummyLM([{"answer": "x"}]))` now emits one caller-located warning naming both versions and replacements; it emitted none before. Existing sync/async `dspy.Predict` tests still pass.

The adapter sits between `Predict`/`Signature` and the LM; its extraction stage still uses `ChatAdapter`. Recommend `dspy.JSONAdapter()` for models supporting structured outputs (automatically negotiated), otherwise the current default `dspy.XMLAdapter()`. Neither retains a separate extraction LM. Migration changes prompting/extraction; warnings-as-errors users will need to migrate or filter the warning. No provider, optimizer, or inference changes.

title: Add InterpreterPool to start interpreters ahead of need
body:
Merge train, part 2 of 2: #10776 → #10777. Merge after #10776. Until it's in, this diff includes it too, and [this compare](https://github.com/michaelisaac-dev/dspy-contributions/compare/flex-native-dspy...interpreter-pool) shows only this part.

A Flex forward spends most of its time starting its sandbox and importing dspy. This makes both cheap.

- Sandboxes that use dspy start from a memory snapshot of one that has already imported it, instead of installing the bundle and importing dspy themselves. DSPy records the snapshot next to the bundle, once per dspy source.
- `InterpreterPool` is an `interpreter_factory` that keeps interpreters started and hands each one out once. Every call still gets a fresh interpreter that has run no code.

```python
pool = dspy.InterpreterPool(size=2)
program = dspy.Flex(MySignature, interpreter_factory=pool)
```

With a dummy LM, medians of 8 runs in fresh processes. #10776 alone imports dspy in every sandbox, which makes a forward about three times slower than main. This brings it back to main's time, and a pool makes it several times faster.

| | main | #10776 alone | this PR | this PR, pool of 2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Flex forward | 0.25s | 0.83s | 0.26s | 0.06s |
| RLM call | 0.25s | 0.36s | 0.24s | 0.04s |
| RLM call with a dspy sub-agent | 0.25s | 0.84s | 0.26s | 0.06s |

I went with a snapshot because after #10776 importing dspy is most of what's left of the start time, and a snapshot taken right after that import skips it. The pool is opt-in because every idle interpreter holds about 400 MB. Each snapshot takes about 50 MB in `~/.dspy_cache/sandbox`. With the sandbox cache turned off there is no snapshot, and each sandbox imports dspy itself.

Worth a closer look:

- A snapshot holds the memory of the bundle's compiled extension modules but not their code. So the runner loads them before Python starts, in the snapshot build and in every restore, so they land where the snapshot's memory expects them. It records where they landed, and a sandbox that finds they landed elsewhere refuses the snapshot. The host then starts it the usual way, and the next process builds a new snapshot.
- Two less obvious details. The sandbox's locale is fixed to `C.UTF-8`, since the host's would change what the runtime allocates. And a restored sandbox reseeds Python's `random`, or every sandbox restored from one snapshot would draw the same numbers.
- The snapshot uses Pyodide's `_makeSnapshot` and `_loadSnapshot`, which Pyodide marks private. Pyodide is pinned to 0.29.4, so they can't change under us, but a Pyodide upgrade should recheck them.

title: Run the real dspy inside Flex and RLM sandboxes
body:
Merge train, part 1 of 2: #10776 → #10777. This one goes first.

Flex and RLM sandboxes used a small stand-in for dspy whose predictors were built and run on the host. Sandboxed code could only use what the stand-in copied, and every new feature needed more bridging. This removes the stand-in. Sandboxed code now imports the real dspy, from the same source the host runs.

It's easiest to review by commit. "let PythonInterpreter sandboxes import dspy" gets dspy into the sandbox, "run the real dspy inside Flex and RLM sandboxes" moves Flex and RLM onto it, and "keep custom types on the host" replaces how types crossed (more on that below). The rest are fixes from review.

The sandbox has no network, so `PythonInterpreter.provide_dspy()` has the host build a zip of dspy and everything its installed metadata says it needs. Packages Pyodide ships come from Pyodide's own builds, checked against the hashes in its lock file, and the others are copied from this environment if they're pure Python. As with the standard library archive from #10775, a Deno run that executes no sandboxed code byte-compiles it once into the sandbox cache, and the runner unpacks it before any code runs. With the cache off (`DSPY_SANDBOX_CACHE=0`), each process builds its own in a temporary directory, removed when it exits.

Only what has to stay on the host goes there:

- Every LM call, through one tool. The host builds the request from its own LM, rejects routing and credential options, and counts the call. The model, credentials, cache and budget stay on the host.
- Every predictor call's formatting and parsing. The sandbox sends the signature, demos and inputs, and the host's own adapter formats them, calls the metered LM and parses the answer, as it would without a sandbox.
- Provided tools. They show up in the sandbox as real `dspy.Tool`s with their descriptions.
- Nested interpreters. An RLM built in the sandbox gets a fresh interpreter from the same factory.
- The trace, so `program_trace` metrics still see the inner predictor calls.

The rule I ended up with: the host owns the custom types, as it did with the stand-in, and the sandbox only holds plain data. Earlier versions copied user types into the sandbox, first their source, then their shape, and the sandbox validated, defaulted, prompted and parsed with that copy. Review kept finding ways a copy differs from the real class (aliases, `exclude=True`, factory defaults, config, keyword-only fields...), one at a time. So now nothing about what a type means is decided in the sandbox:

- A value of a custom type is plain data there: the JSON its type writes for a round trip, like a dict of a model's fields. Generated code reads it that way and returns such data where the signature names the type, and the host reads it back as the real type, so the user's validators and defaults apply there.
- The sandbox knows the type by name only, so code there can name it, as in a signature. Its values can't be built there, and its methods stay on the host.
- Every predictor call is formatted and parsed on the host by the host's own adapter, which sees the real types.
- Other values cross in one JSON form that carries their types (tuples, bytes, datetimes, dspy's own types), and an object of dspy's that comes back unchanged is the host's own object again.

Real classes for the user's types in the sandbox, for types whose module can be shipped there, would come later, on top of #10790.

Types only go one way: the host never builds a class from anything the sandbox sends, so sandboxed code can't get a class of its own to run there.

Worth a closer look:

- `facade.py` is the host side and `sandbox_guest.py` the sandbox side. Most of the diff is those two and their tests. For types, start at `Wire`, `HostValues` and `HostType`.
- A field marked `exclude=True` doesn't cross, as it isn't in the type's JSON. A value that comes back from the sandbox is read from its JSON, so such a field takes its default, as with pydantic's own round trip.
- An in-process interpreter shares the host's memory, so nothing crosses there and its code gets the real objects. Code optimized against one may not run on another, as the docs already say.
- A type the sandboxed code defines itself is unknown to the host. Only that field is plain text on the host, and the sandbox parses it back into the type.
- Since the host formats every predictor call, signatures cross with their fields' settings too (description, prefix, the name an adapter writes a reasoning field as). The adapter's callbacks fire on the host, and an LM it holds itself, like a TwoStepAdapter's extraction model, is metered like the main one.
- Which files go into the bundle. From an install, its RECORD says. From a git checkout, it's what git tracks plus Python files git doesn't ignore, so a `.env` next to the source never goes in. Adding, removing or editing a file makes a new bundle on the next start.
- Pyodide can't start threads, so the runner swaps `ThreadPoolExecutor` for one that runs each call right away. dspy's parallel helpers run one call after another in the sandbox.
- Every call from the sandbox runs the host LM's sync path, an async one too. The bridge is synchronous, so the caller's loop waits while the sandbox runs, and an async engine run on a loop of its own would lose the connections it keeps. An LM that only implements async can't serve a sandbox, which the stand-in couldn't either.
- `max_predictor_calls` now counts LM calls, since predictor calls happen inside the sandbox.
- It's slower until #10777, because each sandbox now imports dspy. A Flex forward on `PythonInterpreter` takes about 0.83s, against 0.25s on main, and on `LocalInterpreter` 0.24s against 0.03s. #10777 brings it back to main's time with snapshots, and a pool makes it faster than main.

LocalInterpreter also stops leaking its worker's `from __future__ import annotations` into submitted code.

title: Start Pyodide from a precompiled standard library
body:
Merge train, part 1 of 3: #10775 → #10776 → #10777. This one goes first.

Pyodide compiles every standard library module it imports each time it starts, and that is most of the time a `PythonInterpreter` takes to boot. Now the first interpreter on a machine byte-compiles Pyodide's standard library once into `~/.dspy_cache/sandbox`, and every interpreter after that starts from it. The build runs in its own Deno process that executes no sandboxed code and can only write that one file. Sandboxes get read access to it and lose that access once Pyodide has started.

Starting an interpreter and running its first execute goes from about 0.75s to 0.22s. With a dummy LM, a Flex forward goes from 0.80s to 0.25s and an RLM call from 0.80s to 0.25s.

If the cache can't be written, interpreters start the old way. To not write it at all, pass `PythonInterpreter(sandbox_cache=False)`, or set `DSPY_SANDBOX_CACHE=0` for every interpreter, including the ones Flex and RLM make. Write paths that overlap the cache are rejected, like the other runtime files.

The cache's Pyodide release is read from the version runner.js imports, so upgrading Pyodide stays a one-line change there.

title: Make openai an optional dependency
body:
Merge train, part 1 of 4: #10774 → #10775 → #10776 → #10777. This one goes first.

dspy only uses the OpenAI SDK for hosted embeddings in `Embedder`, OpenAI fine-tuning and a Databricks deploy helper. But `Embedder` imported it eagerly, so every `import dspy` paid for it. This moves it to a new `openai` extra and has `Embedder` import it lazily. `import dspy` goes from about 0.42s to 0.21s on my machine.

openai was also the only reason jiter got installed, and streaming uses jiter for partial JSON. pydantic-core ships the same parser as `from_json(..., allow_partial="trailing-strings")`, so streaming now uses that and jiter isn't needed.

It also fixes `gepa[dspy]`, which names an extra that gepa doesn't define.

This is the first of a small stack. The next PRs speed up `PythonInterpreter` startup and let Flex and RLM sandboxes run the real dspy.

title: fix(dspy): support class-based signatures in Flex
body:
`dspy.Flex` doesn't handle class-based signatures well. When you pass one to Flex, the starting code turns it into a string signature, so field descriptions and constraints never reach the prompt. Code running in the sandbox can't use class-based signatures at all, because the sandbox's `dspy` has no `InputField` or `OutputField` and its `Signature` is a function.

This PR fixes both.

- The sandbox shim gets a `Signature` class that can be subclassed, plus `InputField` and `OutputField`. A class signature crosses to the host as a string signature plus each field's kwargs, and the host rebuilds the fields from them.
- If the Flex signature has descriptions or constraints, the starting code declares it as a class instead of a string.
- The optimizer prompt no longer says class-based signatures are unavailable.

title: Update vendored lm15 to 2.0.0 with canonical token accounting
body:
## Summary

Import [lm15 v2.0.0](https://github.com/lm15-dev/lm15-python/releases/tag/v2.0.0) and retain the eleven temporary downstream patches already shipped with DSPy's 1.5.0 snapshot. [Upstream comparison](https://github.com/lm15-dev/lm15-python/compare/v1.5.0...v2.0.0).

2.0 makes usage provider-independent: input includes cache reads/writes and provider tool input; output includes reasoning; total is input + output. DSPy must remove its old Anthropic/Gemini/xAI compensations, or history and cost estimates double-count tokens. Old `dspy-lm15-result-v1` records become cache misses rather than being deserialized with different meanings. The next call may therefore incur a provider charge; current-format caching is unchanged.

Exact upstream release: `b6c9159b965d0aac8fca919b87f7e943a61ce953`. Contract: `cfc3edc0d31127ecab55240f866dd3c54df7f07b`. Tested/imported source: [`d8ab7e3088ea8f3b07fabcf7ccfe578ad8b4f1d2`](https://github.com/cmpnd-ai/lm15-python/commit/d8ab7e3088ea8f3b07fabcf7ccfe578ad8b4f1d2). Subtree split: `d8d539d7f921502cbd102f8281e9e3a905f8844f`. Imported only through `scripts/update_vendored_lm15.py`; no hand edits inside the subtree. Pristine fork main is exactly the release. Committed provenance lists the ordered patch IDs.

The [source patch record](https://github.com/cmpnd-ai/lm15-python/blob/d8ab7e3088ea8f3b07fabcf7ccfe578ad8b4f1d2/DOWNSTREAM_PATCHES.md) preserves each motivation and regression: bound-model enforcement; rate-limited renewal; coherent managed credential/account/endpoint snapshots; retained transports; login exports; terminal input draining; sibling routes/cancellation/verification; deadline errors; dispatch admission; selected identities/cloud settings; and billed usage on malformed OpenAI replies. Patch 11 was added to DSPy's previous snapshot on October 23 and is retained here using the new canonical usage readers, including separate-reasoning policy. Source contribution branch: `cmpnd-ai:fix/managed-request-snapshots-2.0.0`. Upstream PR creation was denied by GitHub integration permissions; the branch is published but **not submitted or merged upstream**.

## Public DSPy reproduction (offline)

Run this with the PR checkout installed, or with `PYTHONPATH=.`. No API keys, external requests or paid inference are needed. The fake replaces only provider HTTP transport; DSPy routing, lm15 parsing, public LM calls, history, cost calculation and caching remain real. Prices are deliberately synthetic fixtures, not assertions about the changing LiteLLM catalog.

```python
import json
from unittest.mock import patch

import dspy
from dspy.lm15 import RouterConfig
from dspy._vendor.lm15.testing import FakeResponse, FakeTransport

cases = {
    "anthropic": {"model": "test", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "ok"}],
        "stop_reason": "end_turn", "usage": {"input_tokens": 100, "output_tokens": 30,
        "cache_read_input_tokens": 40, "cache_creation_input_tokens": 20}},
    "gemini": {"modelVersion": "test", "candidates": [{"content": {"role": "model", "parts": [{"text": "ok"}]},
        "finishReason": "STOP"}], "usageMetadata": {"promptTokenCount": 100, "candidatesTokenCount": 30,
        "thoughtsTokenCount": 10, "toolUsePromptTokenCount": 5, "totalTokenCount": 145}},
}
for provider in ("xai", "openai"):
    cases[provider] = {"model": "test", "choices": [{"message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "ok"},
        "finish_reason": "stop"}], "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 100, "completion_tokens": 30,
        "total_tokens": 140 if provider == "xai" else 130,
        "completion_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 10}}}
rates = {"input_cost_per_token": 2e-6, "output_cost_per_token": 7e-6,
         "cache_read_input_token_cost": 1e-6, "cache_creation_input_token_cost": 3e-6,
         "output_cost_per_reasoning_token": 11e-6}
dspy.configure_cache(enable_disk_cache=False, enable_memory_cache=True)
for provider, body in cases.items():
    transport = FakeTransport([FakeResponse(status=200, body=json.dumps(body).encode())])
    with patch("dspy.clients.execution.RouterConfig", side_effect=lambda **kw: RouterConfig(**kw, transport=transport)), \
         patch("dspy.clients.model_metadata._data", {f"{provider}/test": rates}):
        lm = dspy.LM(f"{provider}/test", engine="lm15", api_key="fake", cache=True)
        assert lm("accounting") == ["ok"]
        cold = lm.history[-1]
        u = cold["usage"]
        print(provider, u["prompt_tokens"], u["completion_tokens"], u["total_tokens"], f'{cold["cost"]:.6f}')
        assert lm("accounting") == ["ok"]
        assert len(transport.requests) == 1
        assert lm.history[-1]["usage"] == {}
        lm.close()
```

Expected and observed output on this PR (prompt, completion, total, USD):

```text
anthropic 160 30 190 0.000510
gemini 105 40 145 0.000530
xai 100 40 140 0.000520
openai 100 30 130 0.000450
```

The identical repro on the raw 2.0 import before DSPy compatibility fixes gave Anthropic `220 30 250 0.000630`, Gemini `105 50 145 0.000600`, xAI `100 50 140 0.000590`; OpenAI was unchanged. On previous main (lm15 1.5), Anthropic/xAI/OpenAI match the final output; Gemini reported `100 40 145 0.000520`, omitting the five provider tool-input tokens that 2.0 now accounts for. Retained tests exercise the same four routes synchronously and asynchronously, cache reuse, both sides of the 200k pricing boundary and safe old-cache misses.

## Verification and limitations

- Before compatibility fixes: 8 accounting failures, 39 controls passed. Initial patch replay also failed four existing public error-accounting tests because patch 11 was missing; restored it rather than weakening assertions.
- `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True python -m pytest tests/clients tests/adapters tests/test_vendored_lm15.py tests/predict/test_rlm.py tests/utils/test_exceptions.py -q`: **1719 passed, 60 skipped** on the final head. Includes optional LiteLLM conversion and streaming, native errors/retries, sync/async, adapters and caching.
- Patched source: **3859 passed, 9 skipped**, only the two previously approved reserved-IP connect-timeout exceptions (this orb receives a response from 192.0.2.1). Exact-release upstream CI and both exact-tip fork CI runs passed. Strict conformance, all pinned contract-harness directions, generated signatures and type checks pass (32 user programs, zero new findings).
- Built sdist and then wheel from sdist; installed the wheel with `--no-deps` in an isolated validation environment. Copied bundled-package tests outside the checkout: `python -I -m pytest ...`: **6 passed** after the pricing-export review fix. Public exports, package version, provenance and license included.
- Vendor tree equals the recorded source split; license unchanged. Applicable pre-commit including ty and `git diff --check` pass. Simplicity review: arithmetic and serialization changes stay in their DSPy owners; no new configuration, provider allowlist or compatibility wrapper.
- This is a major lm15 API update: custom engines constructing Usage must now include cached/reasoning tokens in totals. Invalid old Usage serializations can fail validation. `InferencePricing.estimate` now accepts a Usage object. Those raw lm15 APIs are not DSPy's metadata pricing engine. Gemini Live WebSocket usage changes are source-tested, not claimed exercised through `dspy.LM`; no live-provider accuracy/billing claims.
- LiteLLM metadata is unchanged at reviewed 1.106.6. The forbidden 1.107.0 artifact was never downloaded, installed or executed. No new metadata PR is needed.

## Greptile review follow-up

Greptile's first review caught that the bundled package does not re-export `PricingTier` or `InferencePricing`, so my initial claim that they were already publicly available was incorrect. Confirmed the explicit import failed on the initial installed wheel, then exported the original classes from DSPy's facade (no vendor edits or wrappers). The same installed-wheel regression now passes; focused metadata/package checks: **57 passed**. This self-contained public repro also produces `0.000392`:

pricing = InferencePricing(tiers=(PricingTier(
    above_input_tokens=100, input_per_million=2, output_per_million=7,
    cache_read_per_million=0.5, cache_write_per_million=4,

              cache_read_tokens=40, cache_write_tokens=20, reasoning_tokens=10)

title: fix(dspy): keep falsy and list interpreter values in the RLM trajectory
body:
## 📝 Changes Description

`RLM._process_execution_result` formats the value the interpreter returns with `str(result) if result else ""`, so anything falsy is treated as "nothing was returned". The interpreter returns the value of the last expression though, so `0`, `False`, `0.0`, `{}` and `[]` are real results, and the next turn is told the cell printed nothing.

The list branch above it is just as lossy: a list is a value, but it was joined with newlines, so `[1, 2, 3]` was shown to the model as

```
1
2
3
```

which reads like three lines of output instead of one list.

After the change only `None` and an empty string still produce the "(no output - did you forget to print?)" hint. Everything else goes through `str()`:

| interpreter result | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `0` | `(no output ...)` | `0` |
| `False` | `(no output ...)` | `False` |
| `{}` | `(no output ...)` | `{}` |
| `[]` | `(no output ...)` | `[]` |
| `[1, 2, 3]` | `1\n2\n3` | `[1, 2, 3]` |
| `""` / `None` | `(no output ...)` | `(no output ...)` |

The mixed list case stays readable as before, since `str()` of a list of strings still gives back a Python list literal. If a caller really wants the old multi-line look for a large list, that looks like a separate formatting decision; I kept this patch to the bug in the issue.

Fixes #10693

## ✅ Contributor Checklist

- [x] Pre-Commit checks are passing (locally and remotely)
  - `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` on both touched files report exactly the same two findings the files already had on `25162c4` (`B004` in `rlm.py`, `RUF043` in the test file), nothing new
- [x] Title of your PR / MR corresponds to the required format
- [x] Commit message follows required format {label}(dspy): {message}

Tests: 8 new cases in `TestRLMFormatting` (6 parametrized falsy values, an empty list, a non-empty list). Without the source change all 8 fail; with it `tests/predict/test_rlm.py` goes from 1 failed / 146 passed to 1 failed / 154 passed. The single failure `TestRLMSubAgents::test_interpreter_that_rejects_the_shim_as_syntax_error_runs_without_sub_agents` fails identically on the unmodified commit. `tests/predict` overall: 619 passed, 1 failed (that same one), 148 skipped.

## ⚠️ Warnings

None. This only touches how a result is rendered into the trajectory; no code path that decides *whether* to continue the loop was changed.

title: [1/3] feat(dspy): send custom-type tool results as content blocks
body:
**Stack:** **[1/3] #10737** → [2/3] #10738 → [3/3] #10736. This PR doesn't depend on #10776 and can merge on its own. Head `d417d35c1`, rebased on main `3f708b1aa` with no code change since the runs below (at `e8d0be34a`).

### Problem

In 3.5, tools are called natively by default (`XMLAdapter(use_native_function_calling=True)`). The adapter `json.dumps` each tool result into the `tool` message, so a tool that returns a `dspy.Image` sends the model JSON-escaped base64 text instead of an image. The same happens to `dspy.File` and to any `dspy.Type` whose `format()` returns content parts.

```python
def screenshot(page: str) -> dspy.Image: ...            # renders an admin "Orders" page

dspy.ReAct("question -> answer", tools=[screenshot])(question="Which order is on hold, why, and its total?")
# main:      "I couldn't reliably read the order details from the dashboard screenshot…"
# this PR:   "Order ZX-4172 is on hold because of an address mismatch. Its total is $1,240.00."
```

### Change

Tool results now get the marker-to-content-parts expansion that input fields already had. The adapter then puts each media part where the route can carry it.

```diff
 dspy.ReAct.forward
   tool(...) -> dspy.Image                      # kept as-is in ToolCallResults / History
   Predict -> Adapter.__call__                  # adapters/base.py
     format() -> format_conversation_history
       Message.tool([tool_result(id,
-        json.dumps(value)                      # escaped base64 text
+        _tool_result_content(value)            # (ImagePart,) or text + parts
       )])
     build_request(lm, prompt, lm_kwargs)
+    _place_tool_result_media(request, lm, lm_kwargs)
     lm(request)
```

- **Routes that carry media in tool results** (OpenAI Responses, Anthropic, Gemini 3, xAI images): the media stays inside `ToolResultPart`.
- **Routes whose tool rows are text-only** (OpenAI Chat, which is `dspy.LM("openai/…")`'s default `model_type`, plus Gemini 2.5, Groq, OpenRouter and Azure Chat): the adapter moves the media into a user message right after the tool results. pydantic-ai, Goose and Cline do the same.
  ```text
  tool: ToolResultPart(call_1, "[image attached in the next message]")
  user: "Attachments from tool call call_1 (screenshot):", ImagePart
  ```

Relocation is the adapter rewriting the native lm15 request. It is **not** an engine fallback and doesn't need LiteLLM.

### How `supported_tool_result_media` is derived

1. **Source of truth: lm15's per-route compat policy.** Each dialect preset sets `tool_result_media` to `"native"` (image + document), `"images"` or `"reject"`, and each value cites a live receipt in `_vendor/lm15/compat.py`. Chat presets can override by model prefix (`for_model`). Gemini has no preset field; it uses `gemini_level_class(model)`, where the Gemini 3 class is native and 2.5 rejects.
2. **DSPy exposes it per LM.** `capabilities._capabilities` resolves the LM's route: provider and dialect come from the model string and `model_type`, or from a declared provider's own compat object. `_TOOL_RESULT_MEDIA_ADMITS` then maps the policy into `lm.supported_tool_result_media`. A custom engine (`dspy.LM(engine=…)` or a `BaseLM` subclass) declares the attribute itself, and an undeclared one is `set()`.
3. **The adapter checks each request.** `tool_result_media(lm, lm_kwargs, request)` returns the route's set only if this request will really run natively. It returns `set()` when `engine="auto"` would hand the request to LiteLLM, which happens for unmapped provider options, client settings lm15 can't carry, or a plan lm15 refuses. `_place_tool_result_media` then moves every media part that isn't in the set.

Evaluated at this head in an install without LiteLLM:

| `dspy.LM(…)` | Route policy | Kept in the tool result |
|---|---|---|
| `"openai/gpt-6-sol"` (default `model_type="chat"`) | OpenAI Chat preset `openai`: `reject` | nothing, all moved |
| `"openai/gpt-6-sol", model_type="responses"` | Responses: `native` | image, document |
| `"anthropic/claude-opus-5-5"` | Messages: `native` | image, document |
| `"gemini/gemini-3-pro-preview"` / `"gemini/gemini-2.5-flash"` | Gemini level class | image, document / nothing |
| `"xai/grok-4.7"` | Chat preset `xai`: `images` | image (a PDF is moved) |
| custom engine without a declaration | unknown | nothing (safe on every route) |

**LiteLLM is optional, and no claim here depends on it.** If lm15 can't resolve a model (for example `moonshotai/…`), or the LM has client settings like `api_version`, every call needs `dspy[litellm]`, with or without images. When LiteLLM is installed and selected, its capability set is empty, so media is moved for that route too.

### Proof: executed

All runs used `gpt-6-sol` on Azure (`api_base` + `api_key`, which runs natively on lm15) with the public API and the default adapter, at this PR's rebased head. Every "This PR" row was re-run in an install **without LiteLLM**, where any LiteLLM fallback would raise `ImportError`. "main" means an isolated install of `b8485dde4`.

| Tool returns | Route | This PR | main |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dspy.Image` screenshot (above) | Chat (moved to user message) | "ZX-4172, address mismatch, $1,240.00" | "couldn't read the screenshot" |
| same | Responses (native) | same correct answer | "can't reliably identify…" |
| `dspy.File` PDF invoice | Responses | "$4,812.60 due Nov 14, 2026" | "PDF is image-only…" (pre-rebase run) |
| `dict` with nested `[dspy.Image, dspy.Image]` | Chat + Responses | "Wash cold 30°C, do not tumble dry, made in Portugal" | "can't verify… from the available listing" (Responses, pre-rebase run) |
| user-defined `Chart(dspy.Type)`, caption + image | Chat + Responses | "September, $88k" | "can't read the chart" (pre-rebase run) |

### Benchmark: V* Bench, executed

V* asks questions about small objects in high-resolution photos (191 official questions, letter-match scorer). Zooming in is the core operation, and that is what this PR unblocks: `dspy.ReAct(sig, tools=[zoom])`, where `zoom(left, top, right, bottom) -> dspy.Image` returns a crop of the full-resolution photo. On main those crops reach the model as base64 text.

| Same model and questions (`gpt-6-sol`, n=191) | Overall | Attribute | Spatial |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dspy.Predict` on the full image | 87.43 | 84.35 | 92.11 |
| **`dspy.ReAct` + `zoom` (this PR)** | **92.15** | **91.30** | **93.42** |

- **Paired against direct:** ReAct fixed 14 questions and broke 5. Exact McNemar p = 0.064, from one run each.
- **Zoom usage:** ReAct zoomed on 58 of 191 questions.
- **Published baselines (other models and settings, not matched):** GPT-4V 55.0, GPT-4o 66.0, SEAL 75.4, DeepEyes-7B 90.1, o3 95.7.

Harness, per-question results and sources: https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/pull/10736#issuecomment-6639664713

### Implementation notes and risks

- **The relocation lives in the adapter, after `build_request`.** A raw `lm(Request)` is never rewritten. The cost is that `tool_result_media()` has to predict which backend will run the request, so it mirrors `execution._select_engine` (a request headed to LiteLLM gets no media). That puts engine selection logic in two places, and they could drift apart.
- **Gemini's policy comes from a model-name table** (`gemini_level_class`). A Gemini model the table doesn't list gets relocation, which is safe, because Gemini 2.5 rejects media inside `functionResponse` with HTTP 400.
- **Only types whose `format()` returns parts expand.** Structured types such as `Score` and `BoundingBox` stay JSON.
- **Markers are trusted.** A plain string tool result that contains a custom-type marker now expands into media on native routes too, as text-mode tool results and input fields already did on main. Fixing that marker trust boundary is tracked separately.

### What this enables

[2/3] and [3/3] move `dspy.Type` values into and out of the real-dspy sandbox from #10776. [2/3] also forwards `supported_tool_result_media` to the sandbox's LM, so a ReAct built in a Flex or RLM sandbox places tool-result media the same way. That was verified live: native on Responses, moved on Chat.

title: [3/3] feat(dspy): pass dspy.Type values to RLM llm_query and sub-agents
body:
**Stack:** #10737 (merged) · base `isaac/rlm-images-base` (History corrections + main + #10776; see #10738) → [2/3] #10738 → **[3/3] #10736** (GitHub stack #10807). Review only the last commit, `feat(rlm): show images to llm_query and llm_query_batched` (`9ca8890e5`).

### Problem

After [2/3], REPL code holds real `dspy.Image`s, but `llm_query` takes only strings:

```python
# inside dspy.RLM's REPL, photo: dspy.Image   (executed on [2/3], Deno and LocalInterpreter)
llm_query(["Read the text in this image.", photo])
# → TypeError: Object of type Image is not JSON serializable
```

Sub-agents already work without this PR. #10776 runs the real `dspy.Predict` in the sandbox, so `dspy.Predict("image: dspy.Image -> text")(image=photo)` sends the image natively. The old [3/3]'s facade changes for sub-agents are gone.

### Change

```text
sandbox: llm_query(["Read this label", crop])
  bind(prompts=("llm_query", "llm_query_batched"))    # sandbox_guest, rebound before each REPL execution
    list items → prompt_text(item)                   # a dspy type → its prompt rendering (custom-type marker)
host: llm_query(prompt)
  _llm_query_content(prompt) → parts_from_text(...)  → [TextPart, ImagePart]
  lm(build_request(lm, Prompt([Message.user(parts)])))   # LM defaults apply, as for a string prompt
```

- A string prompt still goes to the LM as plain text. Only list prompts become multimodal.
- `llm_query_batched` takes a list of such prompts.
- A plain callable `sub_lm` can't build a request, so it keeps string prompts and raises a clear `TypeError` for lists.
- RLM's instructions say `llm_query` accepts lists. The prompt snapshot is updated to match.

### Proof: executed

The live runs used `gpt-6-sol` on Azure with the public API and the default `PythonInterpreter` (Deno), in an isolated install **without LiteLLM**, rerun at head `9ca8890e5`, the stack with History fix `f28a8c875`.

| Program | Result |
|---|---|
| Expense audit: `llm_query_batched([[prompt, receipt] for receipt in receipts])` over 6 receipt photos, then sums in Python | $342.24, and the 3 merchants over $50. Both exact. |
| Parcel triage: a sandbox sub-agent `dspy.Predict` (`photo: dspy.Image` → carrier, fragile) per label photo | Fragile parcels `[0, 2]` and `{UPS: 2, FedEx: 1, DHL: 1}`. Both exact. |

The robustness matrix in #10738 also checks that `llm_query` and `llm_query_batched` deliver the exact pixels, with no base64 in text parts, on Local and Deno, on sync and async paths, and across REPL cells. It checks that a forged marker in a string prompt stays text.

Tests, on Deno and LocalInterpreter:
- `test_llm_query_and_sub_agents_receive_and_return_images` checks the exact content parts the sub-LM receives from `llm_query` and `llm_query_batched` (text, image, and a `Score` tool result as JSON). It also checks that the LM's temperature and max tokens apply, and that a sub-agent gets the image and returns a `dspy.Image`.
- `test_llm_query_takes_images_made_in_the_first_cell` covers an image built in the same cell that imports dspy.
- `test_llm_query_refuses_host_files_named_in_markers` is the security regression below.

### Benchmark: V* Bench

With this stack, `dspy.RLM` can run V*, where the REPL hands the image to `llm_query([question, image])`. On main, every RLM run crashes before the first LM call (root cause in #10738).

| `gpt-6-sol`, 191 questions, single runs | direct | ReAct + zoom | RLM |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Integrated stack** `f5add6b40`, without LiteLLM | 89.53 | 93.19 | 89.53 |
| Old architecture `6c2ea61dc` (not this code) | 87.43 | 92.15 | 90.58 |

- On the integrated stack, RLM called `llm_query` with the image on 191/191 questions and never cropped. It had 0 errors.
- RLM vs direct: 6 fixed, 6 broken.
- Published baselines, with other models and settings, so not matched: GPT-4o 66.0, SEAL 75.4, DeepEyes-7B 90.1, o3 95.7.

RLM's main model never sees pixels, so it either forwards the whole image or crops blind. The stack makes the program possible. Making RLM crop well is a program-design question.

### Implementation notes and risks

- **List items cross as their prompt rendering, a custom-type marker the host expands.** So a string item that contains a forged marker also becomes media, as in adapter-rendered text. That marker trust boundary is tracked in CMP-1674.
- **Host files are refused.** A review reproduced that a forged marker with a `path` part made the host read a host file into the request. `llm_query` now applies #10776's host-file check (`PermissionError`), as sandboxed LM calls already did. No dspy type emits `path` parts.
- **The conversion happens in the sandbox.** The interpreter's stub can't JSON-encode a `dspy.Image`, so `sandbox_guest.bind` wraps the host tools the session spec lists as `prompts` (`llm_query`, `llm_query_batched`), and RLM rebinds them before each execution (see [2/3]). A bare `llm_query(image)`, not in a list, still fails with the JSON error.
- **User-defined media types render as their fields.** #10776 sends user `dspy.Type`s into the sandbox as shapes, without `format()`, so a user type whose `format()` returns an image renders as JSON text in an `llm_query` list. dspy's own `Image`, `Audio` and `File` are real classes there and become content parts. Keeping user types' identity would need type tags or a host render step, which this rebuild deliberately removed.
- **`llm_query_batched` passes string prompts through unchecked**, as before, so an empty string in a batch doesn't fail the whole batch.
- **RLM's max-iterations fallback can't produce images.** That extract step regenerates outputs as text, so image outputs need `SUBMIT`.

This PR makes the docs easier for search engines and AI tools to read and date. It does not depend on #10730, but the two work together.

Page dates
- Each page shows a "last updated" date. The build reads the date of the page's last git commit and adds it to the page's front matter as `revision_date`. Zensical's theme already shows that field.

- `build_docs.py release` removes `sitemap.xml` and `sitemap.xml.gz` from snapshots, so only Current publishes a sitemap. This applies to new snapshots only. Existing snapshots still have their sitemaps. #10730 adds a `noindex` header to snapshot paths.

This PR changes the hosting files that `docs/scripts/publish_versioned_docs.py` writes to the deployment repo, `krypticmouse/dspy-docs`. The publish workflow rewrites these files on every run, so the change has to go here.
