title: [6/6] Make LiteLLM optional; retain compatibility fallback
body:
## 6/6 — Make LiteLLM optional; retain compatibility fallback

Stack: #10709 → #10712 → #10713 → #10652 → #10708 → **#10719**.
Base: #10708. Review the parent-relative diff; nothing is merged. Maxime Rivest's #10401 retained the compatibility engine, and this PR now does too, following maintainer clarification.

### Call paths

```text
pip install dspy                 native lm15 + custom engines; no required LiteLLM
pip install "dspy[litellm]"      also enables optional LiteLLM compatibility

engine="auto"                   native first; compatibility selected before inference
engine="lm15"                   strict native; unsupported mappings raise
engine="litellm"                explicit optional compatibility

Provider failures never trigger a backend switch.
All engines keep the canonical Request/Response contract.
```

### Changes in this PR

- Remove LiteLLM from required dependencies, retaining the `[litellm]` extra and its retry-helper dependency, tenacity. Native imports/calls do not load LiteLLM. Missing compatibility dependencies produce an actionable installation error.
- Retain the compatibility engines, error translation, logging helpers, and text-completion mode. Their execution/engine implementations match PR5. Automatic fallback handles unsupported routes, client options and representational refusals before provider I/O; strict native selection, declared-provider representation refusals and native prompt-cache requests retain their safeguards.
- Preserve native gateway environment overrides, native Azure endpoint selection, the XAI key alias, and OpenRouter `models`/`route="fallback"` controls. Compatibility routing of a registered provider preserves its declared destination, credential and static headers.
- Hosted embeddings move from LiteLLM to OpenAI SDK clients for OpenAI, Azure and compatible endpoints. Batching, caching, call-time overrides, float32 results and callable backends remain. **Embedding fallback is not restored by installing the extra**; other providers need a callable.
- Replace the proxy test dependency with an isolated stdlib HTTP fixture. Keep core CI LiteLLM-free; a separate Python 3.12 installed-wheel check installs the extra and exercises compatibility and registered-provider routing. The removed `run_tests.yml` fastuuid/PyO3 workarounds remain unnecessary in jobs that do not select the extra.
- Restore `docs/Pipfile` and `docs/Pipfile.lock` unchanged from PR5. Their deletion was unnecessary documentation cleanup, unrelated to making the runtime dependency optional.
- Update installation, migration, caching, deployment, custom-engine and API documentation. Keep historical attribution and LiteLLM-derived model-catalog provenance/offline controls; catalog metadata does not establish native support.
- Import the source-owned malformed-reply billed-usage fix from [cmpnd-ai/lm15-python#3](https://github.com/cmpnd-ai/lm15-python/pull/3), with exact vendor provenance. Malformed completed native replies retain valid billed usage while still failing, without successful history/cache entries or manufactured retries.
- Keep bounded application-owned Cohere retrieval and text-only Bedrock Nova recipes. The Nova recipe pins the tested LiteLLM 1.96.0 through the optional extra; a custom engine is no longer described as its only integration mechanism. Neither recipe is an accepted release-gate exception.

### Boundaries and release gates

This PR does not introduce `Request`/`Response`, `Prompt`, or one public call per adapter candidate; those are earlier layers. It does not remove custom engines, callable embeddings, provider declarations, DSPy retries/caching/history, or static metadata.

Compatibility restoration is **not a claim of native feature parity**:

- Native Chat audio/files remain unsupported. Optional compatibility carries Chat audio/file blocks; the new tests verify their wire representation against loopback HTTP, not live `gpt-audio-mini` inference. Earlier live comparisons showed that switching that model to Responses did not fix audio support. The prepared native fix remains unimported.
- Native Anthropic citation enablement/provenance/location fidelity remains unresolved. Prepared integration preserves `Document.citations=True`, but source contract approval and ratification are required before importing it.
- Explicit candidate seeds advance and Claude thinking controls retain their earlier-layer fixes. **Repeated-input billing remains open: 624 versus 156 tokens** in the measured four-candidate comparison. Distinct seeds do not guarantee distinct text.
- OpenRouter fallback controls survive native sync/async Predict serialization; no live outage/fallback transition was induced. Earlier live privacy controls were preserved through predictor config, and PDF extraction worked through Responses.
- Native Bedrock Nova/Converse and Cohere embedding parity are not implemented. Optional LM compatibility changes the mitigation options, but does not establish native support or live AWS/Cohere behavior. The earlier Nova custom-engine recipe had 25 locally verified SigV4-signed requests; its evidence is not evidence for built-in Nova execution.

The stack is **not release-ready** while native contract/parity, billing and exception decisions remain open. No source-contract publication, native audio/citation import, merge or release is included.

### Verification

Latest compatibility restoration at [ea92dfd66](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/commit/ea92dfd662ad87ebbcec9fc22a7722ae2277e6d1):

- Full core: **3,243 passed, 299 skipped, 2 xfailed**, using `pytest -q -m 'not extra and not deno' -n 4 --dist worksteal tests/` in a scrubbed environment (LiteLLM 1.96.0 installed).
- Clean Python 3.12 installed wheel, outside the checkout, with LiteLLM absent: **93 passed, 22 optional skips** across vendoring, native calls, missing-extra hints and compatibility controls.
- After installing that wheel's `[litellm]` extra with LiteLLM 1.106.5: **70 tests passed** for optional compatibility and registered-provider routing. Sync/async loopback checks cover explicit and automatic selection, candidate seeds, cache/usage, disabled timeout routing, audio/file wire preservation, Chat streaming, public error types and declared endpoint/credential preservation. Native 401/429 failures make no compatibility request. Text/Responses/Cohere Predict checks use the real SDK's mock-response mode, not live providers.
- Fresh-process imports remain lazy with the extra installed; restored logging helpers work. Pipenv files compare byte-for-byte with PR5. Targeted Ruff, repository fix-only Ruff, configured `ty check` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Current docs build passes with six existing missing-page warnings; the revised migration section was rendered and inspected. No new live-provider parity claim.
- Current-head CI and Greptile must be read from GitHub; previous reviews do not automatically cover this head.

Earlier retained evidence is scoped to its original revision:

- Azure authentication fix: all 12 new regression cases failed before the fix; SDK 3.40 loopback changed from eight credential refusals/four wrong-credential requests to 12 correct bearer requests. Explicit keys remain explicit and explicit conflicts remain SDK-owned. SDK 2 may infer its own ambient key. Independent checks: 14 tests and 28 constructor-selection/refusal probes, unchanged cache hashes/environment; no live Azure calls.
- Earlier embedding/native integration review: 158 tests, 24,576 endpoint-preprocessing comparisons, six persisted-cache cases, 16 constructor restrictions, failure cleanup and eight OpenRouter cases. These are not newly repeated live checks.
- Earlier fresh extra/Deno run: 3,357 passed, 302 skipped, 2 xfailed. Earlier 1,424-link/anchor check across 12 rendered pages is historical, not a new whole-site claim.

Five embedding simplification rounds reduced the isolated embedding source from 278 to 255 lines while whole-PR churn grew from 10,784 to 10,793. **The under-20% target was not achieved**; those historical metrics precede this compatibility restoration. Independent source fixes and migration recipes are not credited as simplification.

Maintainer-directed, Amp-assisted implementation. Earlier layers preserve Maxime Rivest's authorship and canonical-contract design.

title: Migrate adapters and candidates to canonical requests and responses
body:
## 3/6 — Switch adapters to canonical objects and one public call per candidate

Stack: #10709 → #10712 → **#10713** → #10652 → #10708 → #10719.
Base: #10712. This is the adapter/candidate cutover, not the legacy-execution deletion or LiteLLM removal.

### Call path changed here

```text
Before
  Predict → Adapter.format → OpenAI message dictionaries
    lm(messages=..., n=N) → existing dual-contract execution

After
  Predict → Adapter.format → Prompt(system, lm15 Messages)
    build_request → Request
    for each candidate, sequentially:
      vary explicit seed by candidate index; derive cache rollout identity
      public lm(Request) / await lm.acall(Request)
        existing dual-contract execution
    parse canonical Responses → Prediction
```

### Changes in this PR

- `Adapter.format()` returns `Prompt`; custom `Type.format()` returns canonical parts/string and `parse_lm_response()` receives `Response`. Tools become `FunctionTool` objects via `Tool.as_function_tool()`.
- Each adapter candidate crosses public `lm(...)`/`acall(...)`: callable wrappers, callbacks, sandbox budgets, caching, history and usage observe one call per candidate. Namespaced rollout identities prevent candidate cache collisions; completed candidates survive a later failure.
- Explicit seeds use `seed + zero-based candidate index`. `None` and the first seed are unchanged; distinct seeds do not guarantee distinct outputs. Direct string-call fan-out gets the equivalent fix in #10652.
- Stream consumers read canonical events while listener-facing `chunk.choices[0].delta` remains available. Signed/redacted thinking and text continuation metadata survive canonical marker expansion. Malformed tool arguments are repaired only from correlated original wire strings; a legitimate `partial_json` argument is preserved.
- Migrate TwoStep, native tools, fine-tuning/export consumers, sandbox facade, TypeSafe decisions/BoundingBox and test doubles. Preserve current-main XML defaults.
- Include effective client settings in typed-call cache identity with existing credential/endpoint exclusions; preserve explicit `None` and trusted sandbox defaults.
- Nonstreaming LiteLLM text/Responses helpers inside `streamify` still complete without token chunks.
- Honor explicitly disabled thinking in ChainOfThought instead of forcing a native reasoning request.

### Does not change

- Dual-contract LM execution, direct `messages=`/`forward` integrations and legacy cache readers remain until #10652.
- Both native lm15 and LiteLLM engines remain; PR6 removes LiteLLM.
- No provider-native batching or parallel candidate execution. Separate requests still repeat input-token billing.
- No native Chat audio/file serialization; #10712's workaround is SDK/export-only.

### Review order and remaining release gates

1. `adapters/base.py`: public candidate calls, seed/cache identities and parsing.
2. `adapters/types/base_type.py`: canonical media markers and continuation preservation.
3. `clients/call_result.py` and `lm15_boundary.py`: visible text beside tools, native response retention and provenance-safe repair.
4. Public prediction/streaming tests, then consumer migrations.

Native Anthropic document citation opt-in/provenance is still lost in this candidate. Generated citations are not equivalent. The source and DSPy integration fixes are prepared separately but require contract-first source landing and vendor import; this is a release blocker, not an accepted downgrade. Native Chat audio/files and filename fidelity also remain bounded coverage gates.

Earlier live four-candidate calls used **624 versus 156 prompt tokens**. Seed variation fixes the identical-seed mechanism, not this billing difference. Max's original #10401 already made separate engine requests; the batching loss is not solely caused by this split.

### Verification and simplification

At `57447e9363e67b6986fed2c1e1d12365500a4917`: core suite **3,064 passed, 299 skipped, 2 xfailed** (`pytest -q -m 'not extra and not deno' -n 4 --dist worksteal tests/`); changed-file Ruff and configured type check pass. Independent adversarial probes found no concrete issue in imports, mixed text/tools, literal `partial_json`, continuation preservation, and sync/async candidate seeds. No new live-provider test in this round.

Five simplification rounds retained shared visible-answer extraction, single-pass marker translation, header-helper reuse and provenance-safe repair. PR3-only source shrank by **21 lines**; normalized parent-relative churn was **3,837 versus 3,828**, so **the under-20% target was not achieved**. PR2 overlap and independent bug fixes are excluded from those figures. No assertions were weakened to achieve reductions.

Canonical migration originates in Maxime Rivest's #10401. Public per-candidate dispatch and compatibility fixes are maintainer-directed, Amp-assisted changes; authorship is preserved. Passing checks do not waive the release gates above.

```text
  request_kwargs(Request, model_type)
    lm15 writer (+ temporary Chat media subclass)
    SDK kwargs / text-completion prompt

Predict → Adapter → LM                       ← still the old adapter path
```

- Normalize Chat/Responses function and hosted tools, named/allowed choices, strict output schemas, reasoning dictionaries and prompt-cache policy. Refuse per-tool `strict=True` because the bundled `FunctionTool` cannot represent it; this does not disable strict structured outputs.
- Respect registered-provider dialects and provider-specific reasoning controls. Keep Anthropic thinking budgets/disable controls on its native writer; reject contradictory explicit controls.
- Preserve SDK/export Chat audio and file blocks with `_SDKChatLM`; mark that workaround `TODO(upstream-lm15)` with its removal condition. Fix text-completion token limits, sampling and integer logprobs; reject non-text content in a flattened text prompt.

### Does not change

- No switch to `Prompt`/canonical parts in adapters yet: #10713 wires this builder into adapter calls.
- No removal of `messages=`, `forward`/`aforward`, legacy engines or old cache readers; #10652 owns that removal.
- No native Chat audio support is added. The temporary subclass serves SDK/export serialization, not the native inference writer.
- No LiteLLM removal or universal provider-option passthrough. Unsupported native options can still select the compatibility engine where the existing routing policy permits it.
- No `generate`/`agenerate` API is introduced in this stack.

### Composition with later layers

PR3 owns the `ChainOfThought` default injection: its local update lets explicit Anthropic thinking controls win over an injected low effort. This builder still rejects genuinely contradictory explicit settings. Native media and citation source fixes are prepared separately and remain blocked on contract approval/landing; this PR does not claim that dependency is integrated.

### Verification and provenance

After five simplification attempts, parent-relative churn fell from **784 to 728 lines**: production **447 to 391**, unchanged tests **337**. This is a 7.14% whole-PR reduction, not the under-20%-remaining target. Tool normalization now stays in the builder and reuses existing SDK-object/reference readers rather than adding duplicate helpers. Those existing readers must move to surviving owners when PR4 deletes the legacy modules; no final-stack saving is claimed for that transitional reuse.

On [c23a84708](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/commit/c23a847080043b47d4dd92c2e5efb2e1685761fd), the core suite reports **2,948 passed, 299 skipped, 2 xfailed** (`pytest -m 'not extra and not deno' -n 4 --dist worksteal tests/`). **131 focused tests**, Ruff and repository-configured `ty` also passed. title: fix(PythonInterpreter): inject variables above 64 KiB through the filesystem
body:
`PythonInterpreter` already injects a large variable through the sandbox filesystem (`inject_var` to `/tmp/dspy_vars/<name>.json`, then `json.loads`). `LARGE_VAR_THRESHOLD` was 100 MiB, just under the 128 MiB Pyodide FFI crash, so every realistic multi-megabyte input was inlined as a Python literal in the program passed to `runPythonAsync`.

Inlining copies that literal through the host, the JSON-RPC line, Deno, and Pyodide's parser. On Linux, with a warm interpreter and the payload already resident in the parent, peak process-tree RSS for one `execute` of `len(data)` was about +106 MiB for a 1 MiB string (156 ms) and +440 MiB for an 8 MiB string (1.20 s, ~293 MiB still resident afterward). The same 8 MiB value on the filesystem path was +69 MiB and 152 ms. The growth is in the Deno process. Below ~32 KiB the two paths are within noise, and past 64 KiB the file path is both smaller and faster, so that is the new default.

`large_var_threshold` overrides the cutoff per interpreter (`None` uses the default, `0` files every eligible value, `MAX_INLINE_BYTES` restores 100 MiB). Settings above 100 MiB are rejected so a caller cannot inline into the FFI crash. Dicts with non-string keys stay inlined below that ceiling, because JSON object keys are strings and `{7: text}` would otherwise stop supporting `data[7]`. `RLM` and the other modules that call `PythonInterpreter()` pick this up with no API change.

Tests cover a 2 MiB string taking the file path and round-tripping, a custom cutoff, the 100 MiB restore path, escaped strings, and int-key dicts.

Fixes #10689

title: fix(teleprompt): handle metric_threshold=0.0 in BootstrapFewShot (fixes #10603)
body:
### Summary
Fixes #10603.

When configuring `BootstrapFewShot(metric_threshold=0.0)`, `dspy/teleprompt/bootstrap.py` previously evaluated `if self.metric_threshold:`. In Python, `0.0` is falsy, causing the threshold to be bypassed and falling through to `success = metric_val`.

This led to two critical inversion defects:
1. A demonstration scoring `0.0` was rejected despite satisfying `0.0 >= 0.0` (because `bool(0.0) == False`).
2. A demonstration with a negative score (e.g., `-0.1`) was accepted despite falling below the threshold (because in Python, non-zero floats evaluate to `True`).

title: Add BoundingBox type with automatic Jev image support
body:
## Rebased onto main #10402, #10648, and #10660 have merged. This PR now targets `main` with the six BoundingBox commits plus removal of the one-off validation script; duplicated dependency history is removed. All six patches were unchanged by the rebase, and there is no XMLAdapter diff. Post-rebase client, adapter, signature, predictor, streaming, and ReAnchor tests with Deno: **2,240 passed, 109 skipped, 2 xfailed**. Ruff and `git diff --check` passed. This used main's updated dependency lock and patched uv 0.13.4. Delivery status: [current head](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/commit/f8eb98e5798926a562f2cf8f73716cabea902e5f) removes only the one-off validation script; **30 BoundingBox tests passed**, and no repository references remain. Fresh CI has **26 passing checks** (documentation publishing intentionally skipped), and Greptile gives **5/5** on this head. The XML dependency no longer blocks merging; this PR is unmerged. ## What and why Add `dspy.BoundingBox`, an immutable `dspy.Type` with normalized `top`, `bottom`, `left`, and `right` edges. Invalid/nonfinite/out-of-range or reversed geometry is rejected, never clamped. Boxes serialize as objects and work as inputs and nested/list/optional outputs with Chat, JSON, XML, and TwoStep adapters. Extend the existing automatic Jev decision path for `dspy.LM("typesafe:jev-1.14.0", engine="lm15")` to support boxes and images. No separate public adapter is needed. Signature instructions, inputs, image demonstrations, and output descriptions become native judgments; existing lm15 code owns transport and provider evidence. Text-only states retain their existing structured representation. Native TypeSafe supports individual named boxes alongside bool, Literal choices, and rich Noul/Choice/Score outputs. Thresholds, weights, cuts, instructions, and criteria remain available on decision fields. Literal retains its existing choice semantics; use Score[...] for ordinal scoring. Boxes themselves reject decision calibration overrides. Native list/nested/nullable boxes remain unsupported. Confidence stays provider evidence, separate from geometry; ordinary generated boxes do not acquire TypeSafe calibration. ## API examples ### Image input and a native Jev box Set `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`. Native routing is automatic; no separate adapter is needed. ```python import dspy class Locate(dspy.Signature): photo: dspy.Image = dspy.InputField() visible: bool = dspy.OutputField(desc="Is there a coffee mug in inputs.photo?") mug: dspy.BoundingBox = dspy.OutputField(desc="The coffee mug in inputs.photo.") photo = dspy.Image.from_path("kitchen.jpg") predict = dspy.Predict(Locate) with dspy.context(lm=dspy.LM("typesafe:jev-1.14.0", engine="lm15")): result = predict(photo=photo) if result.visible: print(result.mug.model_dump()) # normalized top, bottom, left, right ``` There is no native “not found” box: ignore geometry when `visible` is false. Add another named `BoundingBox` output for another target; add a named `Image` input for a reference picture and identify it in the output description. Async uses `await predict.acall(...)` in the same context. Pixel edges are `left/right × image width` and `top/bottom × image height`, using the image actually sent.
Generative LMs, lists, and TwoStepAdapter Given an already configured vision-capable `vision_lm` and an `extraction_lm`, the same type works with standard adapters: ```python class Regions(dspy.Signature): photo: dspy.Image = dspy.InputField() boxes: list[dspy.BoundingBox] = dspy.OutputField(desc="All visible coffee mugs.") with dspy.context(lm=vision_lm, adapter=dspy.JSONAdapter()): regions = dspy.Predict(Regions)(photo=photo) # The vision LM describes regions; a second LM extracts typed coordinates. with dspy.context( lm=vision_lm, adapter=dspy.TwoStepAdapter(extraction_model=extraction_lm), ): regions = dspy.Predict(Regions)(photo=photo) ``` Chat, JSON, XML, and TwoStep support nested/list/optional boxes, subject to provider support. Native Jev supports named top-level boxes only. Generated boxes have validated geometry, not native TypeSafe confidence. These adapters were verified through public sync/async `Predict` calls with controlled responses; the general vision-LLM live benchmark was blocked by deployment configuration, so no Jev-versus-vision-LLM quality claim is made.
## Bounding-box comparison benchmarks **Historical live Jev 1.14.0 runs, not new measurements on this head.** The comparison is the earlier explicit-adapter implementation versus the final automatic routing through ordinary `dspy.LM`. Both used the fixed COCO-derived smoke sample, uncached quality calls, and no ground-truth coordinates in model inputs. The automatic-routing results were captured at [the native-state serialization revision](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/commit/ad2fa1468a56d78b7fc38ecbf5f8617744e50a74). | Measurement | Earlier explicit adapter | Automatic Jev routing | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Main integration contracts passed | 22/22 | 22/22 | | Reference/crop follow-up contracts passed | 2/2 | 2/2 | | COCO-derived boxes scored | 18 | 18 | | Mean IoU | 0.762 | 0.766 | | IoU ≥ 0.50 | 15/18 | 15/18 | | IoU ≥ 0.75 | 11/18 | 11/18 | | Reference-image matching IoU | 0.857 | 0.823 | | Flipped phone, full-frame IoU | 0.396 | 0.396 | | Same phone, caller-selected tile IoU | 0.887 | 0.881 | IoU is intersection-over-union against the annotation; larger is better. Contract success means the typed/native integration completed correctly, **not** that localization was accurate. The 18 boxes include flips and repeated images, not 18 independent images. This deliberately selected sample is neither COCO mAP nor a calibration study; the small score difference is not evidence that routing improved model quality. Tiling is one follow-up example, not a general cropping benchmark. Additional live controls exercised landscape/portrait coordinates, multiple named boxes, two-image disambiguation, reference images, absent-target guards, sync/async cache hits, and changed image contents. A cropped rectangle correctly returned `{top: true, bottom: false, left: true, right: false}` for which image edges it continued beyond. An absent green triangle returned `visible=False`; its otherwise-valid box was ignored.
Actual automatic-routing outputs: multiple targets, crop comparison, and a weak result Green is the annotation; pink is the prediction. These are saved outputs from the automatic-routing run above, not generated illustrations. **Two targets in one request:** table IoU **0.670**, television **0.839**. ![One image with table and television boxes](https://ampcode.com/user-content/artifacts/2a5ad9452915477bf1a84536f3668d77e2a17988837cc916ab3ac1c1c252cdae-file.png) **Phone comparison:** full flipped frame **0.396** versus a caller-selected left-half tile, resized, **0.881**. Tile coordinates were mapped back to the original image for comparison.
Full frameSelected tile
**Weak localization:** apple IoU **0.480**. Valid coordinates do not guarantee a good match to the annotated object. ![Apple with low overlap between annotation and prediction](https://ampcode.com/user-content/artifacts/64fe514e83299ea78c258f943540133620b2bf1772d479701941402604da9e8e-file.png) Photo sources: COCO val2017 images [139](https://images.cocodataset.org/val2017/000000000139.jpg), [1296](https://images.cocodataset.org/val2017/000000001296.jpg), and [2149](https://images.cocodataset.org/val2017/000000002149.jpg). COCO records [CC BY-NC 2.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/2.0/) for 139 and [CC BY-SA 2.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0/) for 1296/2149; overlays and the phone flip/crop/resize are benchmark transformations.
## Historical XML validation A/B qualification These results were collected on the [previous stacked head](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/commit/6a392ef5e2d3648c1efc01eea102988ee0b32eae). The merged XML PR contains additional trailing-prose/streaming fixes. The live A/B was not rerun after the main rebase; current-head validation is the test suite above and fresh CI. Reused the [XML thread's frozen fixtures and scorers](https://ampcode.com/threads/T-01a136a7-3a90-73bd-9a3e-7fee3d6dd4f7), with **864 fresh live trajectories**: 240 core and 192 holdout per arm, including XML, Chat and JSON controls. The only source difference between arms was removing `strict=False` from structured-container validation. Core covered six models; holdout covered eight. Cache/retries were off, cmpnd tracing was enabled, and failures remained in denominators. | Cohort | Adapter | Default validation | `strict=False` | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | | Core | XML | 66/80 | 68/80 | | Core | Chat | 73/80 | 70/80 | | Core | JSON | 63/80 | 65/80 | | Holdout | XML | 54/64 | 59/64 | | Holdout | Chat | 62/64 | 61/64 | | Holdout | JSON | 55/64 | 55/64 | **305 live XML parse attempts evaluated under both flags had identical acceptance and typed values**, including dynamic tool/RLM signatures. Separately, **410 historical completions** had identical parser outcomes and task-field scores, and **83/83 deterministic parser/streaming cells** passed in each arm. Historical replay excludes closed-loop tool/RLM execution; the fresh runs exercise those paths. The frozen few-shot scorer's `Example.items` collision was corrected consistently from retained responses (48 corrections, all exact), without regenerating outputs. This is evidence of no observed regression attributable to the flag, not a claim of improved model quality or universal non-regression. Subgroups fluctuated: core plain-description RLM scored 3/4 versus 0/4; the paired parsers agreed on its fresh outputs too. Timing showed no consistent parser-sweep regression, but noisy scaling measurements do not establish performance equivalence. **Strictness caveat:** eight of 50 focused cases changed from rejection to acceptance. Nested XML now coerces text into numeric BoundingBox edges and also overrides explicit `StrictInt`, `StrictBool`, or `ConfigDict(strict=True)` on nested models. Finite/range/ordering/positive-area geometry constraints still reject invalid boxes; JSON-text strict validation remains unchanged in the tested cases. This behavior belongs to #10402, not a separate BoundingBox XML patch. ## Verification - `PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/clients tests/adapters tests/signatures tests/predict tests/teleprompt/reanchor -q --tb=short`: **1,897 passed, 166 skipped, 2 xfailed** after the native-state serialization fix. - Public `Predict` coverage includes sync/async Chat, JSON, XML, TwoStep, and native TypeSafe paths; nested/list/optional boxes, saved demos, validation, mixed judgments, image payloads, evidence, cache hits, and unsupported schemas/overrides. - Mixed native-box tests change thresholds, choice weights, and score cuts against the same cached evidence and verify that calibrated decisions change while boxes stay unchanged. An offline probe also verifies image-only rich Noul/Choice outputs, nested images, and saved/restored image demonstrations. - Literal nested XML is tested through `Predict`, including rejecting a boolean coordinate and preserving numeric-looking strings. XML leaf coercion happens at the adapter boundary; direct box construction remains strict. - Native state uses the shared JSON serializer: public Predict regressions for tuple/date/set inputs and demonstrations fail before the fix and pass afterward, both with images and text-only. - Pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed. - Latest uncached TypeSafe run through automatic routing: **22/22 main integration checks and 2/2 follow-up prediction checks passed**. Eighteen COCO-derived boxes had mean IoU **0.766**, with **15/18 >= 0.5** and **11/18 >= 0.75**. This deliberately varied smoke sample is not COCO mAP or a calibration claim. - Live controls passed for portrait/landscape geometry, multiple named boxes, two-image disambiguation, reference matching (IoU 0.823), absence guards, crop-edge questions, sync/async caching, and changed image contents. Tiled phone refinement reached IoU 0.881. Earlier source and installed-wheel runs also passed 44/44 integration checks before consolidation. - Replayed captured results with injected reference/crop failures: both false-success exits reproduced before the fix; both now exit nonzero and report the failed control. A clean replay still exits zero. - The one-off live validation harness is not included in this PR's final diff. It remains available in the [pre-removal commit](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/commit/41793f063dd80f1db00ff1bd8e0dfcb6828b7313) for reproducing the historical evidence; its results remain linked in this thread. - General vision-LLM live verification remains blocked by the available Azure deployment configuration. Its adapter coverage uses controlled responses. The concise BoundingBox guide was built and visually inspected locally. The exact documentation example passed present/absent cases with controlled native responses, and all 30 bounding-box tests passed. The site build reports eight unrelated missing-page warnings. Implementation and detailed evidence: https://ampcode.com/threads/T-01a144f8-afdf-76d9-a524-f60b382eefe1

title: feat(dspy): ReActV2 show the agent its remaining turn budget each turn
body:
## 📝 Changes Description

This MR/PR contains the following changes:

ReActV2 never tells the model about `max_iters`, so the model hits a forced `submit` with no warning. RLM already shows the model a per-turn `iteration` count (`"3/20"`); this PR adds the same idea to ReActV2.

- Each LM call gets a `turn_budget` input, e.g. `Turn 3 of 10 (7 more after this one).` It follows a per-call `max_iters` override. The forced final call says ``No turns remain. Call `submit` now with your final outputs.``
- One plain line is added to the instructions: the run has a limited number of turns and must end with `submit`.
- Each turn's `turn_budget` is stored in that turn's history event, so replay rebuilds each request exactly as sent. With native function calling, every request is a prefix of the next, so provider prompt caching keeps working. This also fixes a gap on `main`, where turns 2+ dropped the trailing format reminder on replay.
- `show_turn_budget=False` turns it off. While it's on, `turn_budget` is a reserved field name.
- Agents saved with `dump_state` before this change still load with their optimized instructions. Agents pickled before it keep the old behavior.
- Tests cover sync and async, request-prefix stability in native mode, the off switch, the reserved name and the pickle fallback. Docs are updated in `diving-deeper/react.md`.

Motivation: [Budget-Aware Tool-Use Enables Effective Agent Scaling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.17006) (COLM 2026). A per-step budget status let ReAct agents keep improving with larger tool budgets at lower cost. Anthropic's [task budgets](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/task-budgets) use the same pattern.

## ✅ Contributor Checklist

- [x] Pre-Commit checks are passing (locally and remotely)
- [x] Title of your PR / MR corresponds to the required format
- [x] Commit message follows required format {label}(dspy): {message}

## ⚠️ Warnings

- The feature is **on by default**, which changes the prompt for existing ReActV2 users. It hasn't been benchmarked yet.
- In text mode (`use_native_function_calling=False`), requests still aren't full prefixes of each other, because the `tools` list sits in the trailing message and isn't stored in history. That's unchanged from `main`.

This follows merged #10540 and updates bundled **lm15 1.4.0 → 1.5.0**. No lm15 merge is authorized.

- Adds public `dspy.lm15.bounding_box(...)`: TypeSafe Jev 1.14 Box judgments, structured output on other providers, and generated boxes beside measured judgments on token-scoring servers. Boxes have no probability distribution; confidence remains in provider data. Mixed and cached responses retain both box coordinates and other judgments' probabilities.
- Takes upstream's saved cloud-settings fix and provider-name alias handling. The overlapping runtime hunk is removed from our temporary patch stack; its retained sync/async replacement regressions pass against the upstream implementation.
- Replays the remaining managed-auth fixes without rewriting published branches. No new DSPy runtime workaround, hand-edited vendor files, dependency, or license change.

## Provenance and risks

[Upstream comparison](https://github.com/lm15-dev/lm15-python/compare/48ab49d84257873e63329c62712973cd0c838363...6a1814a04565bcabe2a82d7c729b696a102d14ae) · [exact imported source](https://github.com/cmpnd-ai/lm15-python/commit/1c6a5c7a9a87482db2b61817847f4ece04339df2) · [contract pin](https://github.com/lm15-dev/lm15-contract/commit/6dc1c5ccfe8e2e3b0e8b2eece74b5aa3546bb567).

cmpnd `main` is the pristine v1.5.0 release. Ten ordered patch commits remain on `integration/lm15-1.5.0-patches` / `fix/managed-request-snapshots-1.5.0`; [DOWNSTREAM_PATCHES.md](https://github.com/cmpnd-ai/lm15-python/blob/1c6a5c7a9a87482db2b61817847f4ece04339df2/DOWNSTREAM_PATCHES.md) records motivations, regressions and replay adjustments. Upstream PR submission remains permission-denied; branches are published, not claimed submitted/merged. The independently contributed cloud fix is upstream [#21](https://github.com/lm15-dev/lm15-python/pull/21).

TypeSafe images/boxes remain experimental. Boxes require Jev 1.14 (`jev-preview` or `jev-1.14.0`); older models can reject them. Upstream contract decisions D1/D3 (shape recognition and probability semantics) await maintainer ratification. A four-number top/bottom/left/right schema is recognized as a box; boxes alone do not demand probabilities even with `required`. Other providers' coordinates are model output, not rescaled or guaranteed accurate. Existing managed-auth opt-ins, terms/data-use warnings, WebSocket/raw-builder refusals and cancellation limits remain unchanged.

- Public DSPy sync/async regression: **2 box cases fail before; all 4 cases pass after**, including image-only controls, wire encoding, confidence, probabilities and cache reuse.
- Greptile's coverage finding is addressed with retained public DSPy sync/async token-scoring tests: fake wire responses distinguish generated from measured answers, reject box tokenization, verify asymmetric coordinates and independently normalized probabilities, and preserve both through the cache. Focused integration file: **34 passed**.
- Forced-local clients/adapters/bundled/RLM/exceptions/LocalInterpreter: **1,295 passed, 61 skipped**.
- Source: **3,771 passed, 9 skipped**, only the two approved reserved-IP orb connect-timeout failures. Strict conformance, all 18 pinned harness directions, generated signatures and types pass. Focused login/routing/box coverage: **226 passed**.
- [Exact-release CI](https://github.com/lm15-dev/lm15-python/actions/runs/38822533894) and [patched-source CI](https://github.com/cmpnd-ai/lm15-python/actions/runs/38905337102) pass.

[Review](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/pull/10660#issuecomment-6216400328) confirms the coverage finding is resolved. Ready for maintainer review; not merged.

## Runnable DSPy user-facing repros (October 19 follow-up)

This PR was merged on October 19. The verification above records the pre-merge state. At the maintainer's request, the following retained tests were rerun unchanged against the pre-merge main (lm15 1.4.0) and this PR's final head (lm15 1.5.0).

From a DSPy checkout with development dependencies installed:

```bash
LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True python -m pytest \
  tests/clients/test_lm15_rc3_integration.py \
  -k 'typesafe_image_judgments or token_scored_judgments' -v
```

- **Locate a mug in an image through `dspy.LM("typesafe:jev-preview")`.** [Runnable sync/async repro and image-only controls](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/6eec3de7016f7b81e432b61b5af6695cfd12b404/tests/clients/test_lm15_rc3_integration.py#L220-L274): submit a public `dspy.lm15.Request` containing images and `judgments(mug=bounding_box("Locate the mug."), same=yes_no(...))`, with `probabilities="required"`. The result keeps the mug's asymmetric coordinates, yes/no probabilities, and provider confidence through a second cached call. It also checks the real TypeSafe request encoding and experimental image header. **Before:** both box cases fail because `dspy.lm15.bounding_box` is unavailable; both image-only controls pass. **After:** all four cases pass.
- **Keep a generated box beside a measured judgment through `dspy.LM("vllm:m")`.** [Runnable sync/async repro](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/6eec3de7016f7b81e432b61b5af6695cfd12b404/tests/clients/test_lm15_rc3_integration.py#L277-L346): ask for a box and `mug_visible` with required probabilities. The fake server deliberately generates `mug_visible=False` while token scores favor `True`. DSPy must return the measured `True`, its independently normalized probability, and the generated box; only the yes/no question is token-scored. Repeating the request preserves both without another provider request. **Before:** both cases fail at the missing public box helper. **After:** both pass.

**Executed result:** before **4 failed, 2 passed**; after **6 passed**. The identical retained tests were used on both revisions. These are offline public-API integration repros: they exercise real DSPy routing, lm15 encoding/parsing/scoring, and caching, replacing only the provider transport. They do not establish live-provider compatibility or image-localization accuracy; no paid/live requests were made. The before failure demonstrates the feature was absent, not a pre-existing scoring bug. The tests are already included in this PR, so no duplicate test files or follow-up code changes were needed.

title: refactor(lm): remove deprecated entry points and unify engine execution
body:
## 4/6 — Remove the old LM contract and consolidate canonical execution

Stack: #10709 → #10712 → #10713 → **#10652** → #10708 → #10719.
Base: #10713, whose adapters already send canonical requests. This PR is not the whole migration and does not remove LiteLLM.

### Call path after this PR

```text
Adapter → lm(Request)                         ← already migrated by PR3
Direct user → lm("text")                     ← convenience stays list-returning
  BaseLM.__call__ / acall
    prepare
      string input only: build_request
      validate, snapshot, construct cache identity
    execute / aexecute
      cache hit → cached result
      cache miss → select engine
        native lm15 / LiteLLM / custom complete(Request)
        or optional stream(Request) → canonical accumulator
        retry only the eligible engine attempt
      account and cache completed results
    finalize: usage, history, Response or convenience list

Removed: messages= → dictionary execution branch
Removed: custom forward/aforward and legacy-engine shortcuts
```

### Changes in this PR

- Remove deprecated `messages=`, `forward`/`aforward` integration, legacy engines/converters/deprecation machinery, and historical LiteLLM cache readers/fixtures. Old cache entries regenerate; they are not migrated.
- Keep one `Request -> Response` contract for adapters/custom engines and the existing list-returning string convenience. There is no `generate`/`agenerate` API.
- Type `BaseLM` parameters; support sync/async engine pairs and async-only engines. Capability declarations prefer sync when present, otherwise async—not a union.
- Add separate runtime-checkable `StreamingEngine`/`AsyncStreamingEngine` protocols and explicit missing/noncallable-stream errors. Minimal completion protocols stay non-runtime-checkable; callable and coroutine-kind validation remains explicit. Custom engines remain borrowed.
- Preserve custom-engine reconstruction through trusted-state loading; validate constructor/copy connection settings and engine replacements before use. Sync/async caches remain separate.
- Retain completed usage on conversion errors/cancellation without retrying completed generations or caching failures. Keep pricing/cache/history work outside retry regions.
- Retain provider-reported partial usage from failed streams, including eager stream-opening failures and attempts retried before visible output. Completed responses are never charged twice because cleanup also failed.
- Keep the successful response's model name in history and cache after a billed failed attempt; usage-only failed-attempt records contribute billing, not answer metadata.
- Direct `lm("text", n=...)` varies an explicit seed by candidate index, matching PR3's `Predict` policy. Retries reuse the candidate's seed; the original whole-call cache identity and grouped history remain unchanged.
- Preserve SDK citation/cost metadata and text logprob shape; declared gateway pricing namespaces remain authoritative. These LiteLLM compatibility paths remain useful at this layer and are deleted only in PR6.
- Preserve automatic pre-inference native planning and eligible LiteLLM fallback, including SDK-supported Chat media. Provider/network/auth failures do not trigger backend switching.

### Does not change

- Does not introduce the adapter `Prompt`, canonical type rendering, or per-candidate public calls; those are PR3.
- Does not remove LiteLLM, text completions, compatibility fallback or logging helpers. That is #10719.
- Does not fix native Chat audio, native document citations or repeated input billing. SDK media fallback still covers some gaps here but disappears in PR6. Distinct seeds are not a guarantee of distinct output.
- Does not close caller-owned custom engines or require streaming on completion-only engines.

### Review order and simplification

Read `BaseLM.__call__/acall` → `execution.prepare` → `execute/aexecute` → `finalize`, then `LM` pool/copy/persistence ownership. Check failure-lifecycle and public-call tests before legacy file deletions. Request-schema and SDK readers move to surviving owners when legacy modules are deleted.

Five simplification rounds removed duplicate copy/default initialization, a redundant options copy, and redundant attempt state. `_Attempt` retains only its result and retry-blocking flag; both completion and visible output prohibit retries. Pool detachment is shared; cleanup still runs outside the lock. The pool-owner rewrite was rejected because pickle/deepcopy changed sharing and engine reuse.

The isolated refactor removes **32 physical / 27 handwritten source lines**, but increases parent-relative churn **5,837 → 5,917**. It does **not** meet the under-20% target. Seed and billing corrections are separate behavior changes, not counted as simplification.

### Verification and provenance

Final local core run for [9593be7f](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/commit/9593be7f16e1e08a055d1b42fd6cd7f711eb855d): **3,166 passed, 299 skipped, 2 xfailed** (`pytest -q -m 'not extra and not deno' -n 4 --dist worksteal tests/`). Changed-file Ruff and configured type checks pass. An initial restack run failed because PR3 reused a header helper PR4 deletes; the final run includes its relocation to the sole remaining caller, with user-header precedence preserved. Broad clients-directory Ruff additionally reports three unrelated existing findings; they were not changed.

Greptile's previous-head model-name finding reproduced in all four sync/async × streaming/completion cases. The same public regression now passes and checks both first-call history and cached replay while preserving all 16 billed tokens and avoiding extra engine calls. The one-line fix selects model metadata from the first completed result instead of a usage-only failed-attempt entry.

Independent adversarial probes verified sync/async partial billing, no double charge after cleanup failure, retry seeds `[41, 41, 42]`, candidate-count cache separation, copy validation and SDK/schema reader relocation. No additional blockers found. SDK boundary probes were mocked, not live-provider evidence. Native audio/citation source patches are not included; contract/source landing and vendor import remain release gates. See GitHub checks for exact-head CI/review results.

Continues Maxime Rivest's #10401 execution cleanup with his authorship preserved, plus maintainer-directed engine-contract, persistence, accounting and compatibility fixes. Original #10401 remains untouched. Superseded #10650 work is retained in this stack. Amp assisted the continuation.

title: Treat null / empty-dict tool_calls as 'no calls' in ToolCalls validator
body:
Fixes #10612

## What does this PR do?

`dspy.ToolCalls.validate_input` rejected `None` and `{}`, but JSON-mode models write both to mean "no tool calls this turn" (`{"next_thought": "...", "tool_calls": null}`). With `ReActV2` + `JSONAdapter` this surfaced as `AdapterParseError` (counted as `parse_error`) instead of the usual `empty_tool_calls` path that `"tool_calls": []` takes — and on a forced submit it re-raised instead of the standard "no submit call" error.

The validator now normalizes to an empty call list:

- `None` (bare, or as the value of `"tool_calls"`) → `{"tool_calls": []}`
- `{}` (empty dict) → `{"tool_calls": []}`

This matches the native tool-calling path, where the field is `None` when the provider returns no calls and ReActV2's `_coerce_tool_calls` already treats that as "no calls".

## Tests

Added to `tests/adapters/test_tool.py`:
- `dspy.ToolCalls.model_validate(None)` / `({})` / `({"tool_calls": None})` → empty call list
- end-to-end with the issue's deterministic `DummyLM` repro: ReActV2 now raises the standard `empty_tool_calls` error for `"tool_calls": null`, not `AdapterParseError`

title: ci: isolate test dependency caches by job

Core and extra-test jobs currently share the package-build cache key. On Python 3.15 they restore a 19 MB cache, spend minutes preparing missing dependencies, then skip saving because the key was an exact hit. Give each test job its own cache suffix without changing test selection or coverage.

### Real GitHub Actions proof

Compared the unchanged parent run [38317685164](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/actions/runs/38317685164) with three attempts on this exact PR head:
- [Cold attempt 1](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/actions/runs/38407394314/attempts/1): all 22 jobs passed; saved separate Python 3.15 core (471 MB) and extra (666 MB) caches.
- [Warm attempt 2](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/actions/runs/38407394314/attempts/2): all 22 jobs passed; core/extra dependency installation took 2s/2s.
- [Warm attempt 3](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/actions/runs/38407394314/attempts/3): all 22 jobs passed; core/extra dependency installation took 2s/1s.

Before: core/extra installs took 188s/431s. Both warm logs show exact hits on distinct `-test` and `-extra_test` cache keys and build only the local DSPy package, with zero dependency rebuilds. Python 3.15 test results are identical before and after: core 2408 passed, 351 skipped, 2 xfailed; extras 244 passed, 2 skipped. Builds and Python 3.10–3.14 tests passed in all three attempts. First-job-start to last-job-completion elapsed time was 649s before versus 169s and 245s warm; runner and scheduling variability apply. Cold runs still pay dependency-build costs.

title: fix(utils): cache materialized module on lazy-import proxies
body:
## 📝 Changes Description

Since #10520, `_LazyModule._load` takes the per-module lock and calls `importlib.import_module` on every attribute access. #10520 fixed a real circular-import crash by keeping proxies out of `sys.modules`, but it made every access through `get_litellm()` and the module-level `np`, `anyio`, and `jiter` proxies about 20% slower than 3.4.0.

This PR caches the materialized module on the proxy. Later accesses skip the lock and `import_module`:

- Once the module is fully initialized, `_load` stores it on the proxy. It reuses the cached module only while `sys.modules` still holds that same object, so a module that is later replaced or removed is re-resolved as before.
- A module that is still initializing (`__spec__._initializing`, the same flag CPython's `_find_and_load` checks) is not cached. Otherwise, touching the proxy during the module's own import would pin the partial module. Other threads would then read it without the lock, and a module that replaces itself in `sys.modules` would stay bound to the old object.
- Failed imports are not cached, so the next access retries.
- The proxy stays out of `sys.modules`, and the missing-extra stub is unchanged.

Micro-benchmark on Python 3.11, reading `proxy.zeros` on a materialized numpy proxy (best of 7 × 200k reads; a plain `numpy.zeros` read takes 56 ns):

| version | ns per access |
|---|---|
| 3.4.0 | 1575 |
| main | 2051 |
| this PR | 1281 |

Most of the remaining cost is CPython's: on a `ModuleType` subclass, normal attribute lookup fails and builds an `AttributeError` before `__getattr__` runs.

New tests in `tests/utils/test_lazy_import.py` cover three behaviors a cache could break:
- another thread must wait instead of seeing a module still initializing;
- a module that replaces itself during import resolves to the replacement;
- a failed import can be retried.

Each test fails against a naive cache (or, for the retry test, a cache that memoizes the error) and passes with this change.

title: fix(adapters): serialize non-JSON values one at a time in serialize_for_json
body:
## 📝 Changes Description

Since #10555 made `InstructionProposer` GEPA's default, the reflective dataset keeps raw input and output values and the adapter renders them through `serialize_for_json`. If any one value can't be serialized by pydantic, for example a `numpy.int64` read from a pandas row, `serialize_for_json` falls back to `str()` of the **whole** examples list. When that happens:
- every example renders as a Python repr (`'claim_amount': np.int64(1200), 'photo': Image(url=...)`);
- `dspy.Image` inputs reach the reflection LM as repr text instead of image parts;
- custom objects lose their `__str__`.

This PR passes `fallback=str` to the existing `TypeAdapter(...).dump_python(...)` call (supported since pydantic 2.11, DSPy's minimum), so only the value pydantic can't serialize becomes `str(value)`. Values that already serialize go through the same call and render unchanged. A top-level unknown value, or a serializer that raises, still falls back to `str()` of the whole value as before. Other adapters benefit the same way: a container holding a numpy scalar now renders as JSON instead of a repr. Numpy scalars render as JSON strings (`"1200"`), matching 3.4.0's per-value `str()`.

Testing: `test_examples_reach_adapter_as_structured_values` now includes a `numpy.int64` and an object with a custom `__str__` next to a nested `dspy.Image`. It fails on main (no image part). `pytest tests/adapters tests/teleprompt/test_gepa*.py tests/primitives tests/predict` → 1131 passed, 267 skipped. Also checked with a pandas + `dspy.Image` GEPA repro and a live `InstructionProposer` call on gpt-4o.

title: fix(facade): host the dspy facade in in-process interpreters without replacing host dspy
body:
## 📝 Changes Description

Since #10478, the sandbox `dspy` facade shim (`_facade_shim.py`) refuses any interpreter that runs code in the host's memory. `dspy.Flex` installs the facade with no fallback, so every forward on an exec()-based interpreter, including `dspy_interpreters.InProcessInterpreter`, raises `CodeExecutionError: ... the dspy facade needs an isolated interpreter`. RLM falls back to running without sub-agents. 3.4.0 works with these interpreters, but its shim could leave itself in the host's `sys.modules["dspy"]`.

The refusal doesn't remove any capability: in-process code already shares the host's memory. What it actually prevented was the shim replacing the host's `dspy` module. Only an explicit choice reaches an in-process interpreter: the module's `interpreter_factory` or `dspy.settings.interpreter_factory`. The default is `PythonInterpreter`, and `LocalInterpreter` is a fresh subprocess.

This PR:
- makes the shim, when it runs in the host's memory, bind `dspy` through the interpreter namespace's own `__import__` (a per-namespace copy of `__builtins__`) instead of `sys.modules`. Sandboxed `import dspy` gets the shim, `import dspy.<sub>` raises `ModuleNotFoundError` as it does in a real sandbox, and the host's `sys.modules` is untouched. Isolated sandboxes still register the shim in `sys.modules`.
- as a result, RLM gets sub-agents on in-process interpreters instead of logging a warning.
- adds a Flex regression test. It uses a bare exec() interpreter that doesn't save or restore `sys.modules`, plus a host tool that checks `sys.modules["dspy"] is dspy` during the forward. It also flips the RLM and `dspy_interpreters` conformance tests that pinned the refusal.
- documents in flex.md §7 and the Flex API page that an in-process interpreter works but isolates nothing.

Verification:
- The four new or flipped tests fail on main. A naive fix that drops the refusal and always writes `sys.modules` fails the new Flex test.
- `pytest -n auto --deno tests/flex tests/predict/test_rlm.py tests/primitives`: 547 passed, 5 skipped.
- A live gpt-4o run of a decomposed Flex (`Predict` + `ChainOfThought` + host tool) on `InProcessInterpreter` succeeds with the host's `dspy` intact.

title: fix(dspy): parse None for optional list outputs in XMLAdapter
body:
## 📝 Changes Description

This MR/PR contains the following changes:

`XMLAdapter` writes a `None` value of a `list[str] | None` output field as the text `None` (for example in a few-shot demo), but `XMLAdapter.parse` reads that text back as `['None']`. `ChatAdapter` and `JSONAdapter` return `None` for the same value. The same happens for `tuple[str, ...] | None` and `set[str] | None`.

```python
class Extract(dspy.Signature):
    text: str = dspy.InputField()
    emails: list[str] | None = dspy.OutputField()

adapter = dspy.XMLAdapter()
xml = adapter.format_assistant_message_content(Extract, {"emails": None})  # '<emails>\nNone\n</emails>'
adapter.parse(Extract, xml)  # {'emails': ['None']}, expected {'emails': None}
```

Cause: `_elements_to_value` wraps plain text under an array schema into a one-item list, and for a nullable schema it only treats a fully empty element as null.

Fix: in the array branch, when the schema is nullable and the childless element's text is exactly `None`, return `None`. `<emails><item>None</item></emails>` is still `["None"]`, and `str | None` is unchanged.

Related to #10269, which is a different case (empty containers).

AI disclosure: I used an AI coding assistant to help find this (a format-then-parse round-trip check across the adapters) and to draft the fix and test. I reproduced the bug and reviewed the change myself.

JSON-mode models (seen with `DeepSeek-V4-Flash` + `JSONAdapter` on τ-bench retail) use both to mean "no tool calls". ReActV2 then rejected the turn as `parse_error`, and a forced submit with the same reply raised `AdapterParseError` from `forward`.

The fix goes in `ToolCalls` parsing rather than ReActV2's signature. Declaring `tool_calls: dspy.ToolCalls | None` would also accept `null`. But adapters detect the native tool-call field with `field.annotation == ToolCalls`, so an Optional field silently turns off native function calling for every LM that supports it. Parsing empty values in the type fixes every `ToolCalls` output field on the text path and leaves the native path unchanged. `ToolCalls | None` fields still get `None` for `None`.

With this change, `null`/`{}` behave exactly like `[]`: the loop ends with `empty_tool_calls`, and the forced submit runs. If the model still never calls `submit`, ReActV2 raises "no submit call" as before. Text mode can't force a tool choice, which is a separate question.

## Verification

- `test_react_v2_json_null_or_empty_tool_calls_mean_no_tool_calls` (parametrized over `None` and `{}`) drives ReActV2 through `JSONAdapter` with a `DummyLM`. Both cases fail on main with `AdapterParseError` and pass with the fix.
- Extended `test_toolcalls_vague_match` to cover `None`, `{}`, and `[]`; it fails on main.
- `pytest tests/predict/test_react_v2.py tests/adapters/test_tool.py`: 91 passed. `pytest tests/adapters tests/predict tests/signatures`: 1014 passed, 148 skipped.
- `ruff check` passes on the changed files, and CI's `ruff check --fix-only --exit-non-zero-on-fix` is clean. pre-commit hooks pass.
- Live on Azure `DeepSeek-V4-Flash`: a forced-submit reply of `"tool_calls": null` now ends as "after empty_tool_calls: no submit call" instead of `AdapterParseError`.

## AI assistance

Investigated, reproduced, and implemented with Amp (Claude) in a maintainer-directed session. Prompt: "Open one issue and one fix PR for: ReActV2 fails when the model returns `tool_calls: null` (or `{}`) with DeepSeek-V4-Flash + JSONAdapter. Reproduce it, confirm the root cause in code, include a DummyLM repro, decide whether the fix belongs in ReActV2's signature or in how `ToolCalls` parses empty values, and explain the choice."

### Summary
Fixes #10603

### Description
In `BootstrapFewShot`, setting `metric_threshold=0.0` previously evaluated as falsy in `if self.metric_threshold:`, skipping numeric threshold comparison and treating the metric result as a boolean. This caused:

### Changes
- Updated `dspy/teleprompt/bootstrap.py` to check `if self.metric_threshold is not None:`.
- Added unit tests in `tests/teleprompt/test_bootstrap.py` verifying behavior when `metric_threshold=0.0`.

One of the tests fails on Windows (test_saved_state_loads_in_a_fresh_process
in tests/clients/test_custom_engine_contract.py)

title: fix(dspy): render PEP 604 unions like typing.Union in adapter prompts
body:
On Python < 3.14, `get_annotation_name(int | None)` returns `UnionType[int, NoneType]`, while `Optional[int]` returns `Union[int, NoneType]`. So a field typed `int | None` shows up in adapter prompts as "a valid Python UnionType[...]", which isn't a real type expression. On 3.14 both already give `Union[...]`.

Repro (3.10):
```    
from dspy.adapters.utils import get_annotation_name
get_annotation_name(int | None)  # UnionType[int, NoneType]
```

Fix: treat a `types.UnionType` origin like `typing.Union` in `get_annotation_name`, so both spellings render the same on every Python version.

Tests: added a parametrized test for PEP 604 vs typing unions, a ChatAdapter prompt test, and removed the 3.14 version branch in `test_xml_adapter`. `pytest tests/adapters` passes on 3.10.

AI disclosure: I used Grok Bot (an AI assistant) to find this bug and draft the fix and tests. I reproduced it myself on 3.10 and reviewed every changed line. Prompt was roughly: "find a small bug in DSPy and propose a minimal fix with tests".

Note: on Python 3.10–3.13 this changes the rendered prompt text for X | Y annotations (UnionType[...] → Union[...]), so cached or recorded prompts for those signatures may change.

title: fix: reject unknown field names in Example.with_inputs
body:
## Summary

`Example.with_inputs` stores whatever keys it is given without checking that they exist on the example. A single typo silently inverts the input/label split that the whole DSPy training loop depends on:

```python
import dspy

ex = dspy.Example(question="Why?", answer="Because.").with_inputs("queston")  # typo!

ex.inputs().toDict()   # -> {}            program is called with NO inputs
ex.labels().toDict()   # -> {'question': ..., 'answer': ...}
                       #    every field becomes a label, including the input
```

Downstream this means optimizers call the program with empty inputs and the metric compares against everything — far away from the one-character mistake that caused it. The trap also scales: `DataLoader.from_hf(..., input_keys=[...])` propagates a wrong key into **every** example of a dataset (`dspy/datasets/dataloader.py`), and none of it raises.

## Fix

Validate the keys against the example's fields:

```python
unknown = set(keys) - set(self._store)
if unknown:
    raise ValueError(
        f"Unknown input field(s) {sorted(unknown)}. Available fields: "
        f"{sorted(self._store)}. ..."
    )
```

All in-tree callers (`dspy/datasets/*.py`) pass existing fields, verified by the full `tests/primitives/test_example.py` + `tests/datasets/` suites passing.

The guard, regression test, and description were drafted by the tool; the change was reviewed and tested by the author, who is responsible for it.

title: fix(teleprompt): raise a clear error when student predictors have no LM set
body:
Fixes #10546

## Problem

`BetterTogether.compile` documents that every student predictor must have an LM assigned, but `_prepare_student_and_teacher` called `all_predictors_have_lms(student)` and discarded the return value, so nothing was ever validated. Compilation ran all the way to the baseline evaluation and then died inside `launch_lms`:

```
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'launch'
```

This happens even when a global LM is configured, because `Predict` falls back to `settings.lm` only at call time (`dspy/predict/predict.py`), while `launch_lms` reads `pred.lm` directly with no fallback.

## Change

- Add `assert_all_predictors_have_lms(program, role)` in `dspy/teleprompt/bootstrap_finetune.py`, the asserting counterpart of the `all_predictors_have_lms` predicate.
- Call it for the student in `BetterTogether._prepare_student_and_teacher`.

The failure now happens up front, before any evaluation work, and says how to fix it:

```
ValueError: The student program must have a language model set on every
predictor, but these have none: ['self']. Call `student.set_lm(lm)` before
compiling.
```

## Tests

Three tests added to `tests/teleprompt/test_bettertogether.py`:

- `test_compile_requires_student_lms` — raises `AttributeError` without this PR, `ValueError` with it.
- `test_compile_names_the_predictors_missing_an_lm` — the message names only the predictors actually missing an LM.
- `test_compile_accepts_student_with_all_lms_set` — the happy path is unaffected.

title: fix(dspy): preserve callbacks across deepcopy and reset_copy
body:
## Changes Description

Resolves #10547.

### Background & Problem
In `Module.__getstate__`, `callbacks` and `history` are excluded to prevent unpickleable objects during model serialization (preserving the fix for #8599).
However, because `Module` did not define a custom `__deepcopy__`, Python's `copy.deepcopy` fell back to `__getstate__`, dropping `callbacks` across all in-memory copies (`module.deepcopy()` and `module.reset_copy()`).

Consequently, modules such as `BestOfN` and `Refine`—which call `self.module.deepcopy()` in their candidate evaluation loops—inadvertently reset `callbacks` to `[]`, preventing observer callbacks from ever firing during execution.

### Fix
1. **Implemented `Module.__deepcopy__`**:
   - Preserves `callbacks` as `list(value) if value is not None else []` so observer instances remain intact across copied modules while decoupling the container list.
   - Resets `history` to `[]`.
   - Deep-copies other attributes recursively using `memo`.
2. **Updated `BaseModule.deepcopy` fallback**:
   - Handles `callbacks` and `history` consistently when `deepcopy()` is called directly on base modules.
3. **Preserves Serialization Safety**:
   - `Module.__getstate__` continues to omit `callbacks` and `history`, preventing serialization failures with unpickleable callback handlers.
4. **Regression Tests**:
   - Added `test_module_deepcopy_preserves_callbacks` verifying callback preservation across `copy.deepcopy`, `mod.deepcopy()`, `mod.reset_copy()`, and exclusion in `__getstate__` / serialization.
   - Added `test_module_callbacks_fire_in_best_of_n_and_refine` verifying callbacks correctly trigger inside `BestOfN` and `Refine`.

## Contributor Checklist

- [x] Pre-Commit checks are passing (locally and remotely)
- [x] Title of your PR / MR corresponds to the required format
- [x] Commit message follows required format {label}(dspy): {message}

## Warnings

None.

title: fix(adapters): make Tool argument defaults JSON-serializable for function calling
body:
## Summary

`dspy.Tool` copied parameter defaults verbatim into the argument JSON schema, so `Enum` and `date`/`datetime` defaults broke `json.dumps()` in `format_as_litellm_function_call()` with `Object of type Unit is not JSON serializable`. This blocked `Predict(tools=...)` with JSON-mode adapters before the request reached the provider.

Fix: serialize the default via `TypeAdapter(hints[k]).dump_python(default, mode="json")` with a `TypeAdapter(Any)` fallback. String `Enum`s become their value (`"celsius"`), `IntEnum`s stay integers, and dates become ISO-8601 strings (`"2024-01-01"`), matching the existing schema's `type`/`format`.

Fixes #10548

## Verification

Reproduced from the issue:

```python
import enum, json, dspy
class Unit(enum.Enum):
    C = "celsius"; F = "fahrenheit"
def weather(city: str, unit: Unit = Unit.C) -> str:
    """Get the weather."""
    return city
json.dumps(dspy.Tool(weather).format_as_litellm_function_call())  # TypeError before, OK after
import datetime, json, dspy
def foo(d: datetime.date = datetime.date(2024, 1, 1)) -> str: return str(d)
json.dumps(dspy.Tool(foo).format_as_litellm_function_call())  # TypeError before, OK after
```

Also verified `IntEnum`, `datetime`, `str`, `int`, `None`/`Optional` defaults still serialize/validate correctly.

Tests:

|-------|--------|
| `tests/adapters/test_tool.py -k "not async"` | 31 passed (same as base; 7 `async` failures are pre-existing - missing `pytest-asyncio` plugin, unrelated to this change) |
| `ruff check` | All checks passed |

Out of scope: no API change; `format_as_litellm_function_call()` now returns JSON-serializable `default` values as the schema already expects.

- [x] References the issue (`Fixes #10548`)

`ToolCall.execute(functions=[dspy.Tool(...)])` called `tool.func` directly. Pydantic arguments were left as plain dicts, and an async tool came back as a coroutine instead of a result.

title: fix: prevent JSONAdapter streams from spilling into adjacent fields
body:
Fixes #10551.

With JSONAdapter, streamed string fields could include the next JSON key and value even though the final Prediction was correct. Emit decoded string-value increments and finish when the value closes, before adjacent fields can be flushed. Accepted non-string values use JSONAdapter's str coercion; split numbers wait for a delimiter. Typed fields retain their existing handling, including single-chunk Prediction fallback.

Reusable string listeners reset at response boundaries rather than at the field's closing quote, preserving final-Prediction suppression and ignoring nested same-name keys. At terminal events or finalization, buffered repaired/truncated values use the same JSON repair rules as JSONAdapter.

Validation: full existing streaming suite with live-model tests (`pytest tests/streaming --llm_call -q`) — 57 passed using a hosted mimo-v2.6-distill-qwen-9b model. Regression tests stay in the existing test file and exercise exact field content, every streamed prefix, final markers, final Prediction, typed fallback, response reuse, and repaired output. Real HTTP/SSE replay and 648 temporary chunk-boundary/coercion checks pass. Before/after reproductions confirmed the original issue, Greptile's finding, and adversarial review findings; the final Astra recheck found no remaining actionable introduced regression in tested paths.

title: feat(gepa): make InstructionProposer the default instruction proposer
body:
## Changes

GEPA now builds `InstructionProposer()` by default. The proposer uses `dspy.Predict` with a `JSONAdapter` and preserves GEPA's reflection instructions in the `ProposeInstruction` signature.

Reflective examples remain structured dictionaries through `Predict`. The adapter renders histories and multimodal values, including nested images. Custom proposers retain their existing reflective dataset format. The adapter and proposer now have a one-way import dependency.

The built-in proposer supports these options:

- `skills` accepts a single source or a sequence of paths, skill directories, or inline strings. YAML frontmatter is parsed with PyYAML, including multiline descriptions. Invalid metadata and empty skill bodies raise at construction.
- `additional_instructions` adds guidance to every proposal.
- `base_instructions` replaces the reflection instructions while retaining the fields.
- `max_chars` sets an exact character limit after stripping outer whitespace. Pydantic validates the draft and allows one compression attempt if it is too long. An empty or still oversized compression raises `ValidationError`. Validation runs after adapter parsing and also applies to custom adapters. Instructions are never truncated.
- `truncate_history_outputs` shortens long tool and REPL outputs before adapter rendering without mutating the original histories.
- `adapter` selects the adapter used for proposal calls; the default is `JSONAdapter()`.

`max_chars` replaces the earlier word/token options. There is no tokenizer selection or estimated token count. Exceptions propagate to GEPA for proposal failure handling.

`MultiModalInstructionProposer` remains available. Its TODO links to #10591 for a vision-quality comparison before any deprecation decision. Structured system-prompt fields, the proposal journal, lesson distillation, and changes to the Flex code proposer remain out of scope.

The docs describe the new API and omit explicit temperature settings from GPT examples.

## Validation

211 tests passed against the pinned GEPA 0.1.4:

```sh
python3 -m pytest tests/teleprompt/test_gepa.py tests/teleprompt/test_gepa_builtin_instruction_proposer.py tests/teleprompt/test_gepa_instruction_proposer.py tests/flex -q --disable-warnings
```

Coverage includes character limits and failed compression, scalar skill inputs, YAML parsing, structured examples and nested images, history truncation, and custom proposer compatibility. Recorded reflection prompts were updated; student LM records and recorded responses are unchanged.

The dependency lockfile check and `git diff --check` pass. Changed Python files introduce no new Ruff findings. These are mocked-LM behavior checks, not an optimization-quality evaluation.

## Behavior change

The default reflection request changes from the gepa library's raw prompt and backtick extraction to a system message plus structured input fields and JSON output. Optimization results may differ from earlier releases even with the same seed. The reflection instruction paragraphs remain unchanged.

title: fix(dspy): keep boundary whitespace out of ChatAdapter stream chunks
body:
Fixes #10552.

The ChatAdapter/XMLAdapter listener only stripped trailing whitespace from the last token and leading whitespace from the chunk that completes the header. If the provider sends the `\n\n` before the next header with the text, as its own chunk, or sends the leading `\n` after the header in a separate chunk, it ends up in the yielded chunks, so they no longer join to the parsed value.

`_default_handle_stream_chunk` now drops leading whitespace until the first text is yielded and holds trailing whitespace back until more text arrives (it's discarded when the next field header shows up). Whitespace inside the value is unchanged, it just goes out with the following token. JSONAdapter path is untouched.

Added a parametrized test with the splits from the issue plus one with newlines inside the value; 3 of the 4 cases fail on main. `tests/streaming`, `tests/adapters` and `tests/utils` pass locally (two streaming tests that need the litellm proxy binary were skipped).

Prompt (summarized): "Fix #10552: ChatAdapter/XMLAdapter stream chunks include boundary newlines depending on how the provider splits tokens. Keep the chunks joining to the parsed value and add tests with the splits from the issue."
