title: Update vendored lm15 to 1.4.0 with temporary auth fixes
body:
## Summary and origin

Maintainer-requested recurring dependency maintenance with Amp, not an issue sweep. The request is to import stable/RC lm15 releases, replay still-needed source fixes, review DSPy compatibility, and iterate on CI/Greptile. This updates bundled lm15 from 1.0.0rc3 to **1.4.0**, with ten temporary source patches. No automatic merge is authorized for this PR.

[Full upstream comparison](https://github.com/lm15-dev/lm15-python/compare/55fce2e61a04ed3193acfeb8797b7c58d1b55398...48ab49d84257873e63329c62712973cd0c838363) · [increment since the 1.3.0 review](https://github.com/lm15-dev/lm15-python/compare/505eaf5044556b791a62f684a2e75e56861a517a...48ab49d84257873e63329c62712973cd0c838363).

**1.4.0 adds TypeSafe Jev PNG/JPEG judgments.** Typed `dspy.LM("typesafe:jev-latest")` requests can carry local/inline images alongside text and structured data, preserving part order. Image requests send TypeSafe's experimental-image opt-in header. URLs, file IDs, other image formats, audio and video remain refused before transport. No generic chat, system-prompt, streaming or box-question support is implied. Images are beta; the pinned upstream contract explicitly marks mixed-part array semantics as awaiting maintainer ratification. No live provider calls were made here.

## Provenance and retained fixes

- Pristine [v1.4.0 release](https://github.com/lm15-dev/lm15-python/commit/48ab49d84257873e63329c62712973cd0c838363); cmpnd main fast-forwarded to this exact release without patches.
- Exact imported [source tip](https://github.com/cmpnd-ai/lm15-python/commit/05acf78594fe82df81d9cc37b1c88c5ffc99760b), published on `integration/lm15-1.4.0-patches` and `fix/managed-request-snapshots-1.4.0`. Previous branches were not rewritten.
- Exact [contract pin](https://github.com/lm15-dev/lm15-contract/commit/10645e5f6a69d9d7a365bdb62de9abac1f4dcffc). Ordered replay commits, original motivations, regressions and contribution status are recorded in [DOWNSTREAM_PATCHES.md](https://github.com/cmpnd-ai/lm15-python/blob/05acf78594fe82df81d9cc37b1c88c5ffc99760b/DOWNSTREAM_PATCHES.md) and packaged provenance.
- All nine patches remain necessary and replay unchanged: bound-model selection; renewal-429 credential preservation; coherent credential/account/endpoint snapshots and dispatch admission; retained transport/adaptation settings; noncolliding login descriptors; terminal input ownership; connection-pinned route lookup/cancellation/verification; typed late-approval errors; requested-route admission and cancellation independent of blocked executor workers. The upstream increment changes none of those owners.
- A [tenth source patch](https://github.com/cmpnd-ai/lm15-python/commit/359f90953dd90089c306ceb5a69fe10bbb14c483) fixes both October 15 Greptile findings: bound clients and saved-account model catalogs discard config identity overrides; managed cloud requests merge saved project/region settings before explicit router settings. Transports and other execution settings remain intact, caller configs are not mutated, and ordinary routers retain explicit-identity precedence.

The package subtree exactly matches the source tip; no manual vendor edits or license changes. Upstream PR creation was again permission-denied on October 15; follow-up confirmed no PR was created. Source contribution branches are published, not claimed merged upstream. Current DSPy main was merged normally, preserving DSPy-owned compatibility fixes. This increment adds a public-boundary regression test, not a new runtime workaround.

## Existing limitations remain explicit

Meta login still requires `allow_unverified=True`; upstream documents Muse Code-only terms/account risk and Contributor-mode data use. Ordinary DSPy LM construction does not opt into managed Auth. Use `dspy.lm15.login_providers` for descriptors; `providers` remains the implementation package. Managed WebSocket/raw-builder paths fail closed. Logout cannot recall admitted requests. Terminal callback completion may wait for Enter; cancellation releases its reservation but cannot interrupt `input()`, stop executor shutdown waiting for that worker, or undo a completed commit.

## Verification

- Exact pristine [upstream CI](https://github.com/lm15-dev/lm15-python/actions/runs/38660184325) and [patched-source CI](https://github.com/cmpnd-ai/lm15-python/actions/runs/38743753225) pass.
- Local source suite: **3,744 passed, 9 skipped**, with only the two previously approved reserved-IP orb connect-timeout failures. Strict conformance, all 18 pinned harness directions, generated signatures and type checks pass (32 user programs; zero new package findings).
- October 15 review regressions: **10 failed before / 10 passed after**; full login/managed-dispatch coverage **103 passed**. Public connect and sync/async retained cloud adapters cover wrong keys/named identities, logout/replacement, absent/conflicting ambient settings and partial explicit overrides.
- DSPy image-judgment test: **2 failed before / 2 passed after**, using sync/async public LM calls, local PNG + inline JPEG + text/data, transport capture, typed probabilities and cached responses. Fixtures test byte mapping, not provider image decoding.
- Forced-local DSPy clients/adapters/bundled/RLM/exceptions/LocalInterpreter: **1,289 passed, 61 skipped**.
- Fresh sdist-built wheel, copied tests outside checkout with `python -I -m pytest`: **5 passed**. Installed public `dspy.lm15.connect` smoke verifies selected cloud identity/project/region against conflicting overrides, refusal after logout, and exact ten-patch provenance. The initial 1.4.0 wheel also passed image success, text/no-header and four unsupported-media/no-dispatch controls; this follow-up does not change image encoding.
- Source/vendor tree equality, unchanged license, applicable pre-commit and diff checks pass. No live/paid provider calls locally.

LiteLLM metadata remains separate: 1.105.1 is current on main after #10646; today's 13 forced-local metadata tests pass with unchanged hashes.

Final October 15 status: [current head](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/commit/3b48ff1b7406459e319fd654c4f047caa30730f4) has **Greptile 5/5**, all 26 checks passing (publish-current intentionally skipped), and no unresolved review threads. Both October 15 findings are confirmed resolved in the re-review. Ready for maintainer review; unmerged, with no automatic merge authorized.

title: Vendor lm15 with ogg, opus, flac, aac, aiff, webm and mpeg input_audio
body:
`dspy.Audio` renders as a Chat Completions `input_audio` block whose `format` is the file's MIME subtype. The vendored lm15 reads that body into a canonical request before it chooses a provider. That reader accepted only `wav` and `mp3`, so an ogg/opus recording sent to a Gemini model never reached lm15's Gemini request. On the lm15 engine it raised `input_audio.format must be one of ['mp3', 'wav']`; otherwise DSPy fell back to LiteLLM. An `.mp3` file, which DSPy labels `mpeg`, hit the same wall.

This updates the vendored lm15 with `scripts/update_vendored_lm15.py` to cmpnd-ai/lm15-python `b0bffc1` (cmpnd-ai/lm15-python#2), the one-line-table fix on the 1.0.0rc3 line. Each format now reads as its true media type: `ogg`, `opus`, `flac`, `aac`, `aiff`, `webm` and `mpeg` join `wav` and `mp3`. Gemini sends the part as `inlineData` with that type. The OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic builders still refuse audio before the wire. The vendored diff is that table and the provenance record.

`tests/clients/test_lm15_audio_formats.py` runs `dspy.Predict` with an ogg `dspy.Audio` through a fake transport and checks the Gemini `inlineData` part. It fails on the previous vendor and passes now. The full suite passes (2314 passed, 519 skipped, 2 xfailed), and `ruff check` is clean.

Draft until cmpnd-ai/lm15-python#2 lands; if it lands under another SHA, the updater is re-run against it. The format list itself is lm15-dev/lm15-contract#1.

title: Prepare DSPy for Python 3.15
body:
## Summary

This PR adds Python 3.15 support to DSPy. With it, `pip install dspy` and `uv add dspy` both work on 3.15 from wheels, with no Rust toolchain and no build flags, and LM calls run through the bundled lm15 engine. pydantic 2.14.0 (released 2026-10-08) supplies the cp315 pydantic-core wheels this depends on.

## Changes

1. **Raise `requires-python`** from `<3.15` to `<3.16`. DSPy made the same change from `<3.14` to `<3.15` at 3.1.0 for the 3.14 cycle.
2. **Install litellm and gepa only below 3.15.** Both declare `requires-python <3.15`. pip honours that, so without this change `pip install dspy` fails on 3.15: it rejects `gepa==0.1.4`, then falls back to litellm 1.83.7, whose pinned fastuuid and pydantic-core have no cp315 wheels and do not build under PyO3 0.26. uv ignores the cap but still has to build fastuuid from source, which needs Rust and `PYO3_USE_ABI3_FORWARD_COMPATIBILITY=1`.
   - The lm15 engine serves LM calls without litellm. The litellm-only paths already raise DSPy's `require()` install hint.
   - `dspy.GEPA` becomes a stand-in that raises `ImportError` when gepa is absent, so `import dspy` still works.
3. **Declare `jsonschema`.** `dspy/adapters/types/tool.py` imports it, but it only arrived through litellm.
4. **Add 3.15 to the `test`, `extra_test`, and `build_package` matrices** as allowed failures (`continue-on-error`) while 3.15 is a release candidate. `allow-prereleases: true` lets the leg use the 3.15 rc interpreter. The dev extra keeps litellm and gepa on 3.15, so these legs still test the LiteLLM and GEPA paths. Those legs set `PYO3_USE_ABI3_FORWARD_COMPATIBILITY=1` so fastuuid builds.
5. **Widen two exact-3.14 conditions to 3.14 and later.** The `dev` extra selects `litellm[proxy]` only below 3.14, and the LiteLLM proxy test fixture skips only on 3.14 exactly.
6. **Update `uv.lock`.** pydantic goes to 2.14.0 and pydantic-core to 2.50.0. The 3.15 resolve takes pyarrow 26.0.0 because pyarrow 25.0.1 has no cp315 wheel.

## Verification

On CPython 3.15.0rc3 (linux aarch64), installing the built wheel into a fresh venv with no Rust on `PATH` and no pyo3 variable:

| Installer | Install | `Predict` (default engine) | `dspy.GEPA(...)` | `dspy.Embedder("openai/...")` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| pip 26.2.1 | succeeds | works | `ImportError`: gepa is required | `ImportError`: install `dspy[litellm]` |
| uv | succeeds | works | `ImportError`: gepa is required | `ImportError`: install `dspy[litellm]` |

On 3.12, pip still installs litellm and gepa, and `dspy.GEPA` constructs normally.

Test suites through `uv sync` with the dev extras:

| Python | `-m 'not extra and not deno'` | `-m 'extra or deno'` |
|---|---|---|
| 3.15.0rc3 | 2433 passed, 310 skipped, 2 xfailed | 244 passed, 2 skipped |
| 3.12 | 2443 passed, 300 skipped, 2 xfailed | 244 passed, 2 skipped |

The "Dependencies (latest)" check fails on `main` as well (`test_lm_wraps_litellm_errors_with_metadata`), so this PR does not cause it.

## Limits on 3.15 outside DSPy

- **LiteLLM features** (`engine="litellm"`, `Embedder` with a model string, the LiteLLM logging helpers, and providers or client settings lm15 does not route) need litellm. pip cannot install litellm on 3.15 because of its `requires-python <3.15`. uv can, but needs Rust and `PYO3_USE_ABI3_FORWARD_COMPATIBILITY=1` until fastuuid ships cp315 wheels (fastuuid/fastuuid#71), and litellm 1.102.0 and later import `sre_constants`, which Python 3.15 removed. Pin `litellm<1.102` on 3.15 for now.
- **GEPA** needs gepa, which declares `requires-python <3.15`. uv can install it on 3.15; pip cannot.

These lift once litellm and gepa support 3.15. DSPy then needs to drop the `python_version < '3.15'` markers and bump the exact gepa pin.

title: fix(lazy_import): prevent circular import when submodules are imported before lazy parent
body:
##  Changes Description

Fixes #10516

When a package is wrapped in a `_LazyModule` proxy (e.g. `openai`), external callers importing its submodules (e.g. `from openai._models import BaseModel` as done by `litellm`) trigger Python's import machinery to query and attach submodules onto the parent package:
1. Python checks `hasattr(parent, submod_name)`, which triggers `_LazyModule.__getattr__`.
2. Python attaches the loaded submodule via `setattr(parent, submod_name, submod)`, which triggers `_LazyModule.__setattr__`.

Previously, `__setattr__` and `__getattr__` unconditionally called `_load()`, eagerly materializing the entire top-level module while submodules were still mid-execution. In libraries like `litellm` where submodules perform relative imports during module execution, this triggered circular `ImportError`s.

This PR:
- Resolves submodules in `_LazyModule.__getattr__` without prematurely materializing the parent package.
- Allows submodule attachment in `_LazyModule.__setattr__` via `super().__setattr__` without triggering `_load()`.
- Preserves previously attached submodules on the real module upon materialization.

Adds the first tutorial for DSPy's experimental decision types — `Noul`, `Score`, `Choice` — and the `ReAnchor` calibration optimizer. These were introduced in DSPy 3.4.0 but currently have only API reference docs and no tutorial or learn guide.

title: Keep method-named fields in sync between attribute and item access
body:
A field whose name collides with a method -- items, keys, values, get, copy, and so on -- could hold two different values at once. __setattr__ routed any name appearing in dir(type(self)) to a real instance attribute and left _store untouched, so:

    ex = dspy.Example(items=["a"])
    ex.items = ["b"]
    ex["items"]   # ["a"], while the instance attribute held ["b"]

Assignment now writes to _store whenever the field is already stored, so attribute and item access cannot disagree. Names that are not fields keep their previous routing, and private names are unaffected.

Attribute reads are deliberately left alone: making ex.items return the stored value would shadow the mapping API that Example exposes and that callers depend on. Instead the constructor now warns when a field name collides with a method, naming the field and pointing at subscript access, so the reader is told rather than left to discover it.

Fixes #10497

title: Don't fall back to JSONAdapter when a value fails validation
body:
ChatAdapter raises AdapterParseError for two unrelated situations: a response that does not conform to the chat wire format, and a well-formed response whose value fails validation against its field annotation. The JSONAdapter fallback treats both as format failures.

For the second case that costs a second LM call which cannot succeed -- the LM is asked again and returns the same out-of-domain value -- and the specific validation error is replaced by a generic serialization error from JSONAdapter, so the actual cause is lost.

Distinguish the two with an is_format_error flag on AdapterParseError, set to False where parse_value rejects an extracted value, and fall back only for genuine format failures. The flag defaults to True, so any caller that does not classify its failure keeps the previous behaviour. XMLAdapter subclasses ChatAdapter and had the same split, so it is classified the same way.

Fixes #10498

title: fix(rlm)!: accept interpreter factories at call time
body:
## Change
Replace the live-interpreter call-time API from #10022 with a keyword-only, zero-argument factory override:

```python
result = rlm(query=query, interpreter_factory=MyInterpreter)
result = await rlm.acall(query=query, interpreter_factory=MyInterpreter)
```

The call-time factory wins over constructor and context/global settings, creates one fresh session for the whole invocation, and supplies its runtime prompt guidance. RLM shuts down the session on success, failure, or cancellation. Live interpreter instances and positional factory overrides are intentionally rejected. The input name `interpreter_factory` is reserved for runtime configuration. CodeAct and ProgramOfThought retain their APIs.

## 📝 Changes Description

This MR/PR contains the following changes:

Adds `dspy.ChainOfDensity`, an implementation of Chain of Density summarization
(Adams et al., 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.04269). The module produces an
initial entity-sparse summary, then runs `num_steps` densification steps that each
add 1–3 missing salient entities while keeping the target length.

- `ChainOfDensity(num_steps=5, target_length=80, return_intermediate=True, use_chain_of_thought=True)`
  returns `final_summary`, `summaries`, `entities_added`, `entity_density`. Sync and async (`aforward`).
- `ChainOfDensityWithPreference` picks the returned summary via `preferred_step` or a custom
  `selection_fn`, since the paper finds humans prefer mid-chain summaries (step ~3 of 5).
- Exported from `dspy.predict` / `dspy`.
- Tests in `tests/predict/test_chain_of_density.py` using `DummyLM`.

`entity_density` is a rough heuristic (capitalized-token ratio), not NER-based.

title: feat(RLM/Flex): Implement sub-dspy interpreters
body:
`dspy.RLM` can now build dspy sub-agents (`Predict`, `ChainOfThought`, `ReActV2`, nested `RLM`) from its REPL.

- **On by default**: every interpreter RLM creates from its `interpreter_factory` gets the sandbox dspy facade and a sub-agent section in the action prompt. There is no flag to turn it off; `max_llm_calls` bounds what sub-agents spend. A runtime that cannot host the shim (one that executes in the host's memory) runs that call without sub-agents and logs a warning. Nested code-executing sub-agents (e.g. a nested `RLM`) run on the factory the invocation runs on, including a call-time `interpreter_factory=` override. The facade's names (`dspy`, `_dspy*`, `__dspy*`) are reserved for inputs and tools.
- **Facade shared with Flex**: the shim moved from `flex/_sandbox_shim.py` to `dspy/primitives/facade.py` + `_facade_shim.py`. Predictors are built and run on the host; only JSON crosses. The facade refuses an interpreter that runs code in the host's memory (the host process or a fork of it). A code-executing sub-agent (e.g. a nested `RLM`) always runs on the host module's interpreter factory; sandboxed code cannot pass `interpreter_factory`.
- **`SandboxLM`**: every LM call made for sandboxed code (RLM sub-agents, Flex bridged predictors) runs on this proxy. It admits only generation parameters per call (`temperature`, `max_tokens`, `response_format`, ...; never `api_base`, `api_key`, headers, or `model`), mirrors only those defaults, and meters RLM's `max_llm_calls` one slot per requested completion (so `n` cannot multiply it). The budget now covers `llm_query`, `llm_query_batched`, and all sub-agent LM calls; sub-agents resolve `sub_lm` (else `dspy.settings.lm`) per call, like `llm_query`. Flex keeps `max_predictor_calls`.
- **Tests**: mock and Deno RLM tests, `SandboxLM` unit tests, and conformance against dspy-interpreters (test-only `dev` dependency group): an isolated backend runs bridged sub-agents with host tools, an in-process backend runs RLM without them, and the library's `check_interpreter`, `check_rlm`, and `check_flex_facade` pass.

title: Add experimental ReAnchor calibration optimizer for Predict
body:
Stacked on #10463.

`dspy.experimental.ReAnchor` calibrates decision outputs in `Predict` programs against a whole-program metric. It works with TypeSafe and generative LMs, without changing instructions, criteria, or demos.

| Output | Fitted setting | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Noul` / `bool` | `threshold` | Converts P(True) to a Boolean |
| `Score` | `cuts` | Selects `.level`; leaves continuous `.value` unchanged |
| `Choice` / `Literal` | `weights` | Reweights option probabilities to select a value |

```python
from dspy.experimental import ReAnchor

optimizer = ReAnchor(metric=metric)
tuned = optimizer.compile(program, trainset=trainset, valset=valset)
print(optimizer.report)
tuned.save("tuned.json")
```

### Search and acceptance

Candidates come from observed probabilities. Threshold search also tries zero when P(True)=0 is observed. A setting changes only when it improves the training score and passes a fold check: settings selected on the other folds must improve the combined held-out score. This discourages gains confined to small portions of the dataset, but can accept them when they recur across folds.

On generative LMs, ReAnchor can ask native `bool` and `Literal` outputs for probabilities while preserving their Python return types. It keeps this change only when the calibrated output beats the native output under the same fold check.

### Execution and saved state

- `compile` returns a copy; the original program is unchanged.
- Numeric settings live in each predictor’s `fields` and use normal program save/load.
- Identical requests reuse cached answers. Changed upstream decisions can produce new downstream requests; native-output promotion also changes requests. Caching is required by default, but does not guarantee a fixed request count.
- Evidence collection is scoped to the current execution context and its DSPy workers.
- `report` includes training scores, fitted settings, observed evidence summaries, and fold-check results. Optional validation data is scored but never fitted. `log_dir` writes `report.json`.
- The API is experimental. RLM decision outputs are unsupported. Single-option Choice calibration currently raises an error.

### Author-reported Jev results

Calibration-only results from the original PR evaluation; these benchmarks have not been rerun for the subsequent implementation changes.

| Benchmark | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Email triage (1,000 test emails, unseen senders) | 0.692 | 0.749 |
| Trend-report judge (8 test files) | 0.813 | 0.874 |

title: fix(dspy): preserve integer precision when loading pandas data

## 📝 Changes Description

`DataLoader.from_pandas()` uses `iterrows()`, which coerces mixed integer/float rows to floating point. Importing an `int64` identifier such as `9007199254740993` alongside a float column produces `9007199254740992`, silently changing the training example.

import pandas as pd
from dspy.datasets.dataloader import DataLoader

df = pd.DataFrame({"id": [2**53 + 1], "score": [0.5]})
example = DataLoader().from_pandas(df)[0]

title: fix(MIPROv2): honor an explicit seed of 0 in compile()
body:
Fixes #10321

## Problem

`MIPROv2.compile()` resolved the seed with `seed = seed or self.seed`. Because `0` is falsy,
`compile(..., seed=0)` silently fell back to the constructor default (`seed=9`), so the run
used a different seed than the caller asked for.

## Fix

`dspy/teleprompt/mipro_optimizer_v2.py` — one line:

```python
-seed = seed or self.seed
+seed = seed if seed is not None else self.seed
```

The parameter is typed `seed: int | None = None`, so `None` is the only value that should
trigger the fallback.

## Tests

Added `tests/teleprompt/test_mipro_optimizer_v2.py` with two tests that stub out the three
expensive compile stages and assert on the seed those stages actually receive:

- `test_compile_honors_an_explicit_seed_of_zero` — fails on `main` with `assert 9 == 0`, passes with the fix.
- `test_compile_falls_back_to_constructor_seed_when_unset` — passes both before and after, guarding the `seed=None` behavior.

Both also assert `optimizer.rng` matches `random.Random(expected_seed)`.

`pytest tests/teleprompt` → 89 passed locally (Python 3.10, `uv sync --extra dev`).

## AI disclosure

I used Claude (Claude Code) to help trace the seed through `compile()` into
`_bootstrap_fewshot_examples` / `_optimize_prompt_parameters` and to draft the test scaffolding.
I reviewed every line, ran the suite locally, and verified the regression test fails on `main`
and passes with the fix. 

Prompts used, in substance: "find where MIPROv2.compile resolves its seed argument and what it
forwards it to", and "write a pytest regression test that stubs the expensive compile stages and
asserts the forwarded seed value".

title: fix(clients): recursively apply strict JSON schema to oneOf, prefixItems, and items lists
body:
## 📝 Changes Description

### Problem / Motivation
In `dspy/clients/legacy_requests.py::_strict_json_schema`, schemas passed to OpenAI's structured outputs (`strict: True`) are shaped according to strict mode requirements (`additionalProperties: False`, all properties in `required`, `None` defaults stripped).

While `_strict_json_schema` recurses into `anyOf` arrays, it did not recurse into `oneOf` or `prefixItems` (or `items` when given as a list). In Pydantic v2:
- **Discriminated unions** (`Annotated[Union[Cat, Dog], Discriminator(...)]`) emit a `oneOf` array in their JSON Schema.
- **Tuples** (`tuple[SubModel, int]`) emit a `prefixItems` array in their JSON Schema.

Because these array branches were not visited by `_strict_json_schema`, sub-schemas within discriminated unions and tuples were sent to OpenAI without strict mode attributes (`additionalProperties: false` missing, `required` incomplete, `None` defaults retained). As a result, OpenAI's API rejected these models with a 400 Bad Request error. Note that `_close_object_schemas` in the same file already handles `("items", "prefixItems", "anyOf", "oneOf", "allOf")`.

### What changed (Causal Mechanics)
In `dspy/clients/legacy_requests.py::_strict_json_schema`:
- Replaced the single `anyOf` list check with iteration over `("items", "prefixItems", "anyOf", "oneOf")`, ensuring all schema list variants recursively receive strict schema transformations.

### Backwards compatibility
100% backwards-compatible. Standard models and existing schemas retain identical behavior.

### Non-goals
- Does not change how raw user-supplied dictionary schemas are handled (they remain untouched).
- Does not alter Pydantic model definitions or validation rules.

### Tests
Added 6 comprehensive regression tests in `tests/clients/test_lm_schema_conversion.py`:
1. `test_strict_schema_recursively_processes_oneof_branches`: Tests `oneOf` object schemas, ensuring `additionalProperties: False`, all properties required, and `None` defaults dropped.
2. `test_strict_schema_recursively_processes_prefix_items`: Tests `prefixItems` (tuple) schemas with inline objects and defaults.
3. `test_strict_schema_recursively_processes_items_list`: Tests `items` as a schema list.
4. `test_discriminated_union_and_tuple_model_strict_schema`: Tests a real Pydantic v2 model combining both a discriminated union (`oneOf`) and a tuple (`prefixItems`).
5. `test_discriminated_union_response_format_is_sent_strict_on_both_paths`: End-to-end test verifying that both canonical (`_canonical`) and legacy (`chat_to_responses`) paths emit matching strict schemas for discriminated unions.
6. `test_nested_oneof_inside_prefix_items_and_vice_versa`: Tests deep nesting of `oneOf` inside `prefixItems` and vice versa.

- **Falsifiability**: Reverting the 2-line production fix causes 4 tests to immediately fail with `KeyError: 'additionalProperties'`.
- **Test execution receipts**:
  ```shell
  $ uv run pytest tests/clients/test_lm_schema_conversion.py
  ============================= 14 passed in 1.60s ==============================
  ```

## ✅ Contributor Checklist
- [x] Pre-Commit checks are passing (locally and remotely)
- [x] Title of your PR / MR corresponds to the required format
- [x] Commit message follows required format

## ⚠️ Warnings
None.

title: fix(predict): reject ReActV2 input fields named 'history' or 'tools'
body:
## Summary

Fixes #10336.

`ReActV2` validates that a user's signature doesn't declare **output** fields named `history` or `termination_reason` (reserved keys attached to every returned `Prediction`), but it never validates the signature's **input** fields against the internal input names `history` and `tools` that `_make_react_signature` injects.

If a user's task signature declares an input literally named `history` or `tools` — both plausible domain field names, e.g. `history: str -> summary: str` for a support-ticket summarizer — `_make_react_signature` silently overwrites that field with the internal `dspy.History` / `list[dspy.Tool]` definition, and `forward()`/`aforward()` pop `history` out of the caller's kwargs before it can reach the signature. The user's actual input is silently dropped or misinterpreted as conversation history, with no error.

This PR adds a construction-time `ValueError` for input fields named `history` or `tools`, mirroring the existing output-field check from #9853 so both sides fail fast with a clear, actionable message.

## Change

- `dspy/predict/react_v2.py`: add `_RESERVED_INPUT_KEYS = frozenset({"history", "tools"})` and a matching intersection check in `__init__` right after the existing output-field check (+13 lines).
- `tests/predict/test_react_v2.py`: `test_react_v2_rejects_reserved_input_field_names`, parametrized over `history`/`tools`, mirroring the existing `test_react_v2_rejects_reserved_output_field_names` (+6 lines).

## Why this helps

- Before: a user input named `history`/`tools` is silently replaced — the domain input never reaches the model (verified by constructing `dspy.ReActV2(dspy.Signature("history: str -> summary: str"), tools=[])` and observing `input_fields["history"].annotation is dspy.History`).
- After: construction fails immediately with a `ValueError` naming the reserved field(s), matching the established output-field behavior.
- Normal signatures are unaffected: `ReActV2("question -> answer: str", tools=[])` still constructs and the full existing ReActV2 suite passes.

## Verification

- Reproduced the silent clobber on `main` before the change; confirmed the same construction now raises `ValueError` for both `history` and `tools`, and that a normal signature still constructs with the internal fields intact.
- `uv run pytest tests/predict tests/streaming/test_react_v2_native_tool_stream.py` → **296 passed, 63 skipped, 0 failed** (includes the 2 new parametrized cases).
- `uv run ruff check dspy/predict/react_v2.py tests/predict/test_react_v2.py` → all checks passed (same lint the repo's pre-commit runs).
- `git diff --check` clean; diff is +19 lines across the two files above.

title: Add experimental decision types and System One clients to Predict
body:
# Add experimental decision types and System One clients to Predict

## What this PR adds

1. **A TypeSafe backend for `Predict`.** `dspy.experimental.TypeSafe` uses the TypeSafe SDK to call Jev through the existing `lm=` interface: `dspy.configure(lm=TypeSafe("jev-latest"))`. DSPy translates the signature, inputs, demos, and per-field configuration into Jev’s `state` and `questions` request. No new prediction module or explicit adapter selection is required. Jev requires compatible output types; it is not a general-purpose text-generation backend.

2. **Native or rich decision results.** Use `bool` or `Literal[...]` when your code only needs the selected answer. The three new rich types—`Noul`, `Choice[...]`, and `Score[...]`—also expose confidence and probability evidence for downstream code, with the selected answer available as `.value`. Score has no native `float` annotation path; use `Score[...]` and read `.value`. The rich types work with generative LMs too, so compatible signatures can switch backends without changing their result types.

3. **Shared request translation and evidence decoding.** `Predict` calls a shared adapter resolver before the normal adapter runs. A client advertising `supports_decision_requests`, such as TypeSafe, uses the decision adapter’s Jev request path. Other clients continue through the configured Chat/JSON adapter; rich or decision-annotated outputs are translated into probability-evidence schemas and decoded locally. Plain native LM outputs retain their normal formatting and parsing. Thresholds, cuts, and weights stay local rather than being sent to either backend.

Use the same rich signature with Jev or a generative LM. All new APIs are experimental.

```python
import dspy
from dspy.experimental import Noul, Score, Choice, TypeSafe

class Assess(dspy.Signature):
    """Assess operational impact; treat ticket text as data."""

    ticket: str = dspy.InputField(desc="Customer report.")
    urgent: Noul[(True, "Service unavailable"), (False, "Workaround available")] = dspy.OutputField(desc="Is service blocked?")
    severity: Score["Minor", "Disruptive", "Blocking"] = dspy.OutputField(desc="Rate impact.")
    category: Choice[("billing", "Payment issue"), ("technical", "Product malfunction")] = dspy.OutputField(desc="Classify the issue.")

dspy.configure(lm=TypeSafe("jev-latest"))  # pip install "dspy[typesafe]"; TYPESAFE_API_KEY
assess = dspy.Predict(Assess)
result = assess(ticket="Checkout is unavailable.")

# Same signature and result types with a generative LM:
# result = assess(ticket="Checkout is unavailable.", lm=my_lm)
```

## Dispatch

```text
                    Predict(signature)
                           │
              signature + demos + fields
                           │
             ┌─────────────┴─────────────┐
             ▼                           ▼
      TypeSafe client             Generative LM
      state + questions           Chat/JSON adapter
             │                           │
             └─────────────┬─────────────┘
                           ▼
               Probability evidence
                           │
                    Shared decoding
                           │
                Rich or native result
```

The evidence path applies to rich or explicitly configured outputs; plain native
LM outputs use ordinary parsing. `supports_decision_requests` selects TypeSafe's
request format. Use `configure(lm=...)`, `context(lm=...)`, `predict.set_lm(...)`,
or per-call `lm=...`.

## Native and rich outputs

| Annotation | Ordinary generative LM emits | Jev emits | Python result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bool` | Boolean | P(True) | `bool` |
| `Noul` or described Noul | `{noul: p}` | P(True) | `.value`, `.probability`, `.confidence` |
| `Annotated[bool, Noul]` | `{noul: p}` | P(True) | `bool` |
| `Literal["billing", "technical"]` | A member | Distribution + confidence | Native member |
| `Annotated[Literal[...], Choice[...]]` | Option distribution + confidence | Distribution + confidence | Native member |
| `Choice[...]` | `{probabilities: {label: p}, confidence: c}` | Distribution + confidence | `.value`, `.probabilities`, `.confidence` |
| `float` | Number | Unsupported | `float` |
| `Score["Minor", "Disruptive", "Blocking"]` | `{probabilities: {"0": p0, "1": p1, "2": p2}, confidence: c}` | Distribution + confidence | `.value`, `.level`, `.probabilities`, `.confidence` |

Rich outputs are derived from evidence on both paths, not independently generated
values. Native LLM fields keep their normal behavior unless explicitly configured
in `predict.fields`. Score is a rich annotation only; use `.value` or `float(result)`.
Choice preserves member types. Rich inputs retain their JSON value and evidence;
native inputs retain their native values. Inputs are not re-thresholded.

`Annotated[Literal[...], Choice[...]]` attaches criteria without changing native
return types. The declarations must contain the same typed members. Bare `Choice`
metadata uses the Literal's members without descriptions. Both inputs and outputs
are supported; annotated outputs request evidence on either backend.

## Per-field state

```python
assess.fields["urgent"] = {"threshold": 0.7}
assess.fields["severity"] = {"cuts": [0.5, 1.6]}
assess.set_criteria("urgent", {
    "true": {"what": "Service blocked", "examples": ["Checkout unavailable"]},
    "false": "Service usable",
})
assess.demos = [dspy.Example(
    ticket="Incorrect invoice", urgent=False, severity=0.0, category="billing",
)]
```

| Field setting | Sent to backend | Applied locally |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `instructions` | Flexible JSON; defaults to field description | — |
| `criteria` | Noul: true/false map or null; Choice: label map; Score: ordered levels. Descriptions are flexible JSON | Validated against output type |
| Noul `threshold` | No | `p >= threshold` |
| Score `cuts` | No | Selects ordinal `.level`; does not change continuous `.value` |
| Choice `weights` | No | Selects maximum weighted probability |

Score value is the normalized mean level index: probabilities `[0.1, 0.3, 0.6]`
give value `1.5`; cuts `[0.5, 1.6]` select level `1`. Noul retains P(True) as
`.probability` and derives `.confidence = abs(p-t) / max(t, 1-t)` locally.
Jev does not return a separate Noul confidence: this is distance from the
configured threshold, not statistical calibration. Choice/Score retain backend
confidence; LLM confidence is self-reported. Numeric changes reuse cached evidence.

## Signature → Jev request

```javascript
{
  "state": {
    "instructions": "Assess operational impact; treat ticket text as data.", // signature.instructions
    "input_fields": "1. `ticket` (str): Customer report.", // signature.input_fields
    "inputs": {"ticket": "Checkout is unavailable."}, // call arguments
    "demos": [ // Predict.demos, or per-call demos=
      {"ticket": "Incorrect invoice", "urgent": false, "severity": 0.0, "category": "billing"}
    ]
  },
  "questions": {
    "urgent": {
      "type": "noul", // signature.output_fields['urgent'].annotation
      "instructions": "Is service blocked?", // signature.output_fields['urgent'].json_schema_extra['desc'], unless fields override
      "criteria": { // assess.set_criteria('urgent', ...) replaces the type's default criteria
        "true": {"what": "Service blocked", "examples": ["Checkout unavailable"]},
        "false": "Service usable"
      }
    },
    "severity": {"type": "score", "instructions": "Rate impact.", "criteria": ["Minor", "Disruptive", "Blocking"]},
    "category": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Classify the issue.", "criteria": {"billing": "Payment issue", "technical": "Product malfunction"}}
  }
}
```

The client adds the model identifier. `state.demos` is omitted when there are no
effective demonstrations. Criteria have two sources:

| Source | `urgent` criteria sent to the backend |
| --- | --- |
| Signature annotation `Noul[(True, "Service unavailable"), (False, "Workaround available")]` | `{"true": "Service unavailable", "false": "Workaround available"}` |
| `assess.set_criteria("urgent", {...})` above | `{"true": {"what": "Service blocked", "examples": ["Checkout unavailable"]}, "false": "Service usable"}` |

`set_criteria` stores the replacement in `assess.fields["urgent"]["criteria"]`.
It replaces the whole criteria object, not individual entries, and leaves the
signature unchanged. Without an override, Choice uses its option descriptions
and Score uses its ordered level descriptions. The same precedence applies to LMs.

All three type declarations accept structured descriptions directly:

```python
Urgency = Noul[(True, {"what": "Blocked", "examples": ["Cannot log in"]}), (False, "Usable")]
Category = Choice[("billing", {"what": "Payment issue", "not_for": "Login failures"}), ("technical", "Product bug")]
Severity = Score["Minor", {"what": "Major", "examples": ["Cannot log in"]}]
```

These keys are ordinary JSON. Type criteria are immutable internally;
`Type.criteria()` and `predict.get_criteria(field)` return independent copies.
`predict.fields` stores only explicit overrides, not resolved defaults.

## Signature → generative LM request

| Rich type | As an LLM **input**: caller supplies | As an LLM **output**: model generates |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Noul` | `{"value": true, "probability": 0.8, "confidence": 0.6}` | `{"noul": 0.8}` |
| `Choice[...]` | `{"value": "technical", "probabilities": {"billing": 0.2, "technical": 0.8}, "confidence": 0.9}` | `{"probabilities": {"billing": 0.2, "technical": 0.8}, "confidence": 0.9}` |
| `Score[...]` | `{"value": 1.5, "level": 2, "probabilities": {"0": 0.1, "1": 0.3, "2": 0.6}, "confidence": 0.8}` | `{"probabilities": {"0": 0.1, "1": 0.3, "2": 0.6}, "confidence": 0.8}` |

**Inputs describe an existing decision; outputs request evidence for a new decision.**
DSPy derives output `.value`, Score `.level`, and Noul `.confidence` locally.
Existing input values pass through without recomputation; optional evidence is
omitted when absent. Both directions include the field description and any
declared outcome descriptions or rubric in the prompt. Output criteria can be
replaced by the predictor's per-field overrides.

All three types can also be inputs. For example, extend `Assess` above with a
previous assessment (the output annotations remain unchanged):

```python
class Reassess(Assess):
    """Reassess operational impact using the report and previous assessment."""

    prior_urgent: Noul = dspy.InputField(desc="Previous urgency decision.")
    prior_severity: Score["Minor", "Disruptive", "Blocking"] = dspy.InputField(desc="Previous impact assessment.")
    prior_category: Choice[("billing", "Payment issue"), ("technical", "Product malfunction")] = dspy.InputField(desc="Previous issue category.")

reassess = dspy.Predict(Reassess)
result = reassess(
    ticket="Checkout is unavailable.",
    prior_urgent=previous.urgent,
    prior_severity=previous.severity,
    prior_category=previous.category,
    lm=my_lm,
)
```

Here `previous` is an earlier rich prediction. With `ChatAdapter`, the request
contains the complete messages below, including formatting instructions and
JSON schemas. `SYSTEM` and `USER` label the message roles; the contents are
captured from the example call, with no omissions or display-only line breaks.

<details>
<summary>Full ChatAdapter request: rich inputs and evidence outputs</summary>

```text
SYSTEM
Your input fields are:
1. `ticket` (str): Customer report.
2. `prior_urgent` (Noul): Previous urgency decision.
    Type description of Noul: A Boolean decision.
3. `prior_severity` (Score['Minor', 'Disruptive', 'Blocking']): Previous impact assessment.
    Type description of Score['Minor', 'Disruptive', 'Blocking']: Continuous score from 0 to 2; intermediate values are allowed. Rubric (level index, description): [[0, "Minor"], [1, "Disruptive"], [2, "Blocking"]].
4. `prior_category` (Choice[('billing', 'Payment issue'), ('technical', 'Product malfunction')]): Previous issue category.
    Type description of Choice[('billing', 'Payment issue'), ('technical', 'Product malfunction')]: Select exactly one value. Options: [["billing", "Payment issue"], ["technical", "Product malfunction"]].
Your output fields are:
1. `urgent` (NoulEvidence): 
{
  "instructions": "Is service blocked?",
  "type": "noul",
  "criteria": {
    "true": "Service unavailable",
    "false": "Workaround available"
  }
}
2. `severity` (ScoreEvidence): 
{
  "instructions": "Rate impact.",
  "type": "score",
  "criteria": [
    "Minor",
    "Disruptive",
    "Blocking"
  ]
}
3. `category` (ChoiceEvidence): 
{
  "instructions": "Classify the issue.",
  "type": "choice",
  "criteria": {
    "billing": "Payment issue",
    "technical": "Product malfunction"
  }
}
All interactions will be structured in the following way, with the appropriate values filled in.

[[ ## ticket ## ]]
{ticket}

[[ ## prior_urgent ## ]]

[[ ## prior_severity ## ]]

[[ ## severity ## ]]
{severity}        # note: the value you produce must adhere to the JSON schema: {"type": "object", "$defs": {"ScoreProbabilities": {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": false, "properties": {"0": {"type": "number", "maximum": 1, "minimum": 0, "title": "0"}, "1": {"type": "number", "maximum": 1, "minimum": 0, "title": "1"}, "2": {"type": "number", "maximum": 1, "minimum": 0, "title": "2"}}, "required": ["0", "1", "2"], "title": "ScoreProbabilities"}}, "additionalProperties": false, "properties": {"confidence": {"type": "number", "description": "Confidence in the decision, from 0 to 1.", "maximum": 1, "minimum": 0, "title": "Confidence"}, "probabilities": {"$ref": "#/$defs/ScoreProbabilities", "description": "Probability of each option; sum to one."}}, "required": ["probabilities", "confidence"], "title": "ScoreEvidence"}

[[ ## completed ## ]]
In adhering to this structure, your objective is: 
        Reassess operational impact using the report and previous assessment.

[[ ## prior_urgent ## ]]

[[ ## prior_category ## ]]
{"confidence": 0.9, "value": "technical", "probabilities": {"billing": 0.2, "technical": 0.8}}

Respond with the corresponding output fields, starting with the field `[[ ## urgent ## ]]` (must be formatted as a valid Python NoulEvidence), then `[[ ## severity ## ]]` (must be formatted as a valid Python ScoreEvidence), then `[[ ## category ## ]]` (must be formatted as a valid Python ChoiceEvidence), and then ending with the marker for `[[ ## completed ## ]]`.
```

</details>

Example LM response and local decoding (default parameters):

| Output | LM generates | DSPy returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `urgent` | `{"noul": 0.9}` | Noul: value `True`, probability `0.9`, confidence `0.8` |
| `severity` | `{"probabilities": {"0": 0.1, "1": 0.3, "2": 0.6}, "confidence": 0.8}` | Score: value `1.5`, level `2`, original distribution/confidence |
| `category` | `{"probabilities": {"billing": 0.2, "technical": 0.8}, "confidence": 0.9}` | Choice: value `"technical"`, original distribution/confidence |

Input values/evidence are supplied by the caller; output values are derived by
DSPy, not generated separately by the LM. Thresholds, cuts, and weights stay local.
`JSONAdapter` uses the same translated descriptions and evidence schemas with its
JSON output format. Demos become labeled task examples in the instructions;
scalar labels are never turned into invented probabilities. `demos=[]` suppresses
stored demonstrations. Bare native inputs/outputs retain ordinary LM formatting;
annotated bool/Literal outputs request evidence but return native values.

## Full saved JSON

Example file from `assess.save("assess.json")` with the configuration above and
`assess.set_lm(TypeSafe("jev-latest"))`. Dependency versions reflect the saving environment.

```json
{
  "traces": [],
  "train": [],
  "demos": [
    {
      "ticket": "Incorrect invoice",
      "urgent": false,
      "severity": 0.0,
      "category": "billing"
    }
  ],
  "signature": {
    "instructions": "Assess operational impact; treat ticket text as data.",
    "fields": [
      {
        "prefix": "Ticket:",
        "description": "Customer report."
      },
      {
        "prefix": "Urgent:",
        "description": "Is service blocked?"
      },
      {
        "prefix": "Severity:",
        "description": "Rate impact."
      },
      {
        "prefix": "Category:",
        "description": "Classify the issue."
      }
    ]
  },
  "fields": {
    "urgent": {
      "threshold": 0.7,
      "criteria": {
        "true": {
          "what": "Service blocked",
          "examples": [
            "Checkout unavailable"
          ]
        },
        "false": "Service usable"
      }
    },
    "severity": {
      "cuts": [
        0.5,
        1.6
      ]
    }
  },
  "lm": {
    "_dspy_lm_class": "dspy.clients.typesafe.TypeSafe",
    "model": "jev-latest",
    "base_url": "https://api.typesafe.ai",
    "cache": true,
    "timeout": 10.0
  },
  "metadata": {
    "dependency_versions": {
      "python": "3.11",
      "dspy": "3.4.0b1",
      "cloudpickle": "3.1"
    }
  }
}
```

Load into the same signature architecture. Types and default rubrics come from
that architecture; overrides live under `fields`. No credentials, callbacks,
runtime client history, or cached responses are saved. Restoring an endpoint
requires `allow_unsafe_lm_state=True` for trusted files. An unbound predictor saves
`lm: null` and uses the configured client at invocation.

## Boundaries

- Decision outputs require `OutputField(desc=...)` or explicit per-field instructions; missing descriptions raise before inference.
- TypeSafe supports cache, usage, LM callbacks, history, copy, and save/load.
- Nested LM decision outputs such as `list[Noul]`, `list[Score[...]]`, and `dict[str, Choice[...]]` warn at invocation: values/confidence are generated directly, without evidence decoding or numeric parameters. Execution remains allowed. Use top-level decision outputs; rich containers remain supported as inputs without this warning.
- RLM decision outputs are unsupported. Construction warns for top-level, annotated native, and nested decision outputs; evidence decoding is not guaranteed. Use Predict with top-level decision outputs; the warning does not prevent execution.
- Unsupported Jev output annotations raise `ValueError` at invocation, before a provider request. Every output must be supported; there is no automatic LM fallback. Generation options and decision streaming also fail explicitly.
- Native LM output behavior is controlled by the signature and per-field configuration, independently of client binding.
- Generative optimizers and fine-tuning are unsupported with TypeSafe.
- Direct chat adapters and generation wrappers such as BestOfN and Refine are unsupported; some currently fail with attribute errors rather than capability-specific errors.

title: fix(adapters): treat Literal that includes None as allowing None
body:
### What changed

`annotation_allows_none` (added in #10148) recognises `None`, `Optional[...]`, `Union[..., None]` and
`Annotated[...]`, but not a `Literal` that includes `None`. A `Literal[...]` annotation that contains
`None` therefore still counts as not-nullable.

This adds `Literal` handling:

```python
if origin in (Union, types.UnionType, Literal):
    return any(annotation_allows_none(arg) for arg in args)
```

### Why

Output fields whose annotation allows `None` are optional: when the LM omits them, parsing falls back
to `None` instead of raising `AdapterParseError` (see #10148). With `Literal["yes", "no", None]` that
fallback never happens, because the helper returns `False`.

Reproduction on current `main`:

```python
import dspy
from typing import Literal
from dspy.adapters.utils import annotation_allows_none, apply_output_field_defaults

class S(dspy.Signature):
    question: str = dspy.InputField()
    verdict: Literal["yes", "no", None] = dspy.OutputField()

annotation_allows_none(Literal["yes", "no", None])   # False today, True after the fix
apply_output_field_defaults(S, {})                   # {} today, {"verdict": None} after the fix
dspy.JSONAdapter().parse(S, "{}")                    # raises AdapterParseError today
```

This reaches `apply_output_field_defaults` and the two callers that gate missing fields on
`annotation_allows_none` (`dspy/predict/predict.py`, `dspy/predict/flex/bridge.py`).

### How did you test it?

- `python -m pytest tests/adapters -q` -> 287 passed.
- Added `test_missing_optional_output_fields_with_literal_none_fall_back_to_none`, which asserts the
  helper returns `True` for `Literal[None]`, `Literal["yes", "no", None]` and
  `Annotated[Literal["yes", None], "meta"]`, and that a missing `Literal[..., None]` output field
  parses to `None`. Reverting the one-line fix makes the test fail.
- `ruff check` (v0.15.0, the version pinned in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`) passes on both changed files.

### Notes for the reviewer

- `Literal` is already imported in `dspy/adapters/utils.py`; the change is one line plus a regression test.
- Prepared with AI assistance.

title: fix(dspy): read an explicit temperature=0 as set when deciding the n>1 randomness bump
body:
## 📝 Changes Description

Fixes #10456

`Predict._forward_preprocess` resolved the effective temperature with

```python
temperature = config.get("temperature") or lm.kwargs.get("temperature")
```

`0.0` is falsy, so an **explicit** `temperature=0.0` was read as "unset" and the documented
"temperature is unset or `<=0.15`, and `n > 1` → `0.7`" randomness bump was decided by the *LM's*
default instead of by the value the caller passed. The same program therefore asked for
`temperature=0.0` against `dspy.LM("openai/gpt-4o-mini", temperature=0.9)` (so all `n` samples are
greedy duplicates) and `temperature=0.7` against `dspy.LM("openai/gpt-4o-mini")`.

- `dspy/predict/predict.py`: fall back to `lm.kwargs` only when the config value `is None`, so
  `0.0` counts as set. This is the "unset vs set" resolution the comment on the line above already
  describes, and it matches what `dspy.Predict(temperature=0.0, n=3)` already does for the common
  case of an LM without a temperature default — the fix aligns the other case with it rather than
  introducing new semantics.
- `tests/predict/test_predict.py`: five regression tests over `_forward_preprocess`, parametrized
  on the LM default (`None` and `0.9`) so the pair has to agree by construction, plus three controls
  that pin what must *not* change: a low non-zero temperature still bumps, `temperature=0.0` without
  `n` is forwarded untouched, and an unset temperature is still left to a high LM default.

Deliberately unchanged: `num_generations` on the next line uses the same `or` shape, but `n=0` is not
a valid request parameter (`n >= 1`), so there is no observable case where the falsy read matters —
fixing it here would only widen the diff.

## ✅ Contributor Checklist

- [x] Lint: CI's exact command (`ruff check --fix-only --diff --exit-non-zero-on-fix`, pinned `v0.15.0`
      from `.pre-commit-config.yaml`) exits 0 on both changed files. It does report 4 pre-existing
      findings in `tests/predict/test_predict.py` (`RUF012` at `:457`, `:492`, `:535`; `N815` at
      `:1313`) and `ruff format --check` would reformat pre-existing lines in both files; none of
      those hunks are in the lines added here, so I left them alone.
- [x] PR title and commit message follow `{label}(dspy): {message}`.
- [x] Behavior is covered by tests (below).

## How did you test it?

Run from the repo clone with its own interpreter (`.venv/Scripts/python.exe`, Python 3.12.11,
`dspy 3.4.0b1`), base `40a6e16`:

| run | `pytest tests/predict -m "not extra and not deno"` |
| --- | --- |
| base source + new tests | `2 failed, 299 passed, 63 skipped` — both failures are `assert 0.0 == 0.7` in `test_explicit_zero_temperature_is_bumped_for_n_gt_1[0.9]` and `..._passed_per_call_is_bumped_for_n_gt_1[0.9]` |
| fixed source + new tests | `301 passed, 63 skipped` |

**Also run** on the fixed tree: `pytest tests/primitives/test_base_module.py
tests/streaming/test_streaming.py tests/utils/test_usage_tracker.py -m "not extra and not deno"`
→ `63 passed, 7 skipped, 2 errors`. I picked these three files because each of them configures
`dspy.LM(..., temperature=0.0)`, so they are the closest neighbours to the branch this patch
changes. The 2 errors are
environment-only: the session-scoped `_litellm_test_server` fixture in `tests/conftest.py` raises
`FileNotFoundError: [WinError 2]` while spawning its subprocess on Windows, before any test body
runs.

**Not run:** the whole-repo suite. I attempted `pytest tests -m "not extra and not deno" -n 4`
twice and a narrower `pytest tests/adapters tests/primitives tests/signatures tests/core
tests/retrievers tests/utils tests/callback -m "not extra and not deno" -n 4` once; none of the
three completed on this machine (the narrow run stopped making observable progress around 90 % and
I killed it), so I have no trustworthy whole-repo number to quote here. CI is the authoritative
full-suite run for this PR — it is currently `action_required`, i.e. waiting on a maintainer to
approve workflow execution for a fork PR.

I also reproduced the inconsistency outside pytest with the snippet from #10456 (four
`temperature=0.0, n=3` results of `0.0 / 0.7 / 0.0 / 0.7` on base, `0.7` in all four cases after the
change).

Two pytest plugins the clone's venv was missing (`pytest-asyncio`, `pytest-mock`, both in the `dev`
extra) are installed locally, otherwise 35 tests in this package error at setup with
`fixture 'mocker' not found` / `async def functions are not natively supported` regardless of this
change.

## ⚠️ Warnings

- **One intentional behavior change:** `Predict(..., temperature=0.0)` (or
  `config={"temperature": 0.0}`) together with `n > 1` against an LM that has a positive temperature
  default now sends `0.7` instead of `0.0`. If the preferred resolution is the opposite — always
  respect an explicit `0.0` and never bump — then the `temperature is None or temperature <= 0.15`
  branch should be skipped for a caller-set value instead, which is a one-line variant of this patch;
  either way the LM-dependent split in #10456 goes away.
- Open PR #9434 ("Improve Predict Ergonomics", stale since 2026-03-19 with changes requested)
  rewrites `_forward_preprocess` but leaves the `temperature = ...` lookup line itself alone, so the
  two changes are logically independent; if both land there will be a textual conflict to resolve in
  `dspy/predict/predict.py` and in `tests/predict/test_predict.py`, where I append at the end.
- Same bug class as #10395 (`seed=0` being dropped by an `or` fallback), different code path.
- Attribution: this patch was written and measured by an AI agent driving the account owner's local
  clone. The RED/GREEN counts above are agent-run measurements. The account owner has not reviewed
  this diff line-by-line before submission.

title: Ship a PyInstaller hook so a frozen application collects DSPy's data files
body:
Split out of #10451 at maintainer request: this adds a packaging entry point and is reviewed on its own.

## What this adds

- `dspy/__pyinstaller/hook-dspy.py`: a PyInstaller hook that collects the files DSPy reads as **data** at run time — the Flex sandbox shim and the local-interpreter worker (both `.py` files read as text, hence `include_py_files=True`), the Deno runner, the model-metadata snapshot/provenance/LICENSE, and the vendored lm15 provenance.
- `[project.entry-points.pyinstaller40] hook-dirs = "dspy.__pyinstaller:get_hook_dirs"`: the mechanism PyInstaller documents for a package to provide its own hook, so `pyinstaller app.py` works with no flags.
- One ruff per-file ignore: PyInstaller requires the `hook-<package>.py` filename.

## Why

PyInstaller freezes modules as bytecode and ships nothing else unless named. Any DSPy feature that reads one of those files failed frozen (gauntlet 2026-09-13). #10451 fixes the import-time read so `import dspy` works; this PR makes the features that read data work.

## Verification

- Real `--onedir` build on this branch alone: `import dspy`, the Flex shim and the metadata snapshot all load; the hook is picked up automatically (`Processing standard module hook 'hook-dspy.py'`).
- `tests/utils/test_pyinstaller_hook.py` pins that the hook exists, names files that exist, and the entry point resolves.
- Matrix Python 3.10–3.14 green (offline).

## Worth attention

- The entry point makes DSPy visible to PyInstaller's plugin discovery in every install; it does nothing unless PyInstaller runs.
- `LocalInterpreter` spawns `sys.executable`, which is not a Python interpreter inside a frozen app. Its worker file is collected, but that feature is not freeze-safe; unchanged here.

title: Close the LM findings still open on main: streamify errors, dead-loop pools, strict schemas
body:
The DSPy items from the LM gauntlet (cmpnd-ai/breaka-your-lm `results/findings.md`, 2026-09-13) that were still open on `main` after #10409, #10441 and #10442. Each was reproduced against `main` before the fix.

## What changes

**1. Errors inside `dspy.streamify` are the program's own exception.** They arrived wrapped in an `ExceptionGroup` from the task group, so `except dspy.LMError` missed them. A group with one failure (even nested) is unwrapped; a group of several distinct failures stays a group.

**2. Async pools of finished event loops are released.** The LM kept one pool per finished `asyncio.run()` and `close()` only reclaimed the sync pool. Dead-loop pools are now dropped on `close()`, on `aclose()`, and when a new loop's pool is created; lm15's finalizers close the sockets. Verified with file-descriptor counts.

**3. `response_format=PydanticModel` sends a valid OpenAI strict schema.** OpenAI rejected any model with defaults or an optional submodel ("`required` must include every key"). The schema now follows the OpenAI SDK's own `to_strict_json_schema` rules. Caller-supplied raw schemas are untouched.

**4. `dspy.LM("openai/")` is refused at construction** instead of silently selecting LiteLLM and failing later.

**5. OpenAI's "use /v1/responses" refusal now says how in DSPy** — `model_type="responses"`. No endpoint is switched automatically: which models need it is OpenAI's policy, not DSPy's to guess.

## Worth attention

- (5) is a hint on the error, not a behaviour change. If maintainers prefer `openai/gpt-5*` to default to the Responses API, that's a separate decision.
- **Not changed:** an empty `choices` array still gives `['']` natively and `[]` on LiteLLM. A 200 with no choices is a malformed provider reply; the right fix is in lm15's parser (raise), then align DSPy's compatibility path after the next vendoring.
- Still open from the gauntlet and not in this PR: gevent (needs a gevent environment to reproduce), the engine-parity list and provider error classification (mostly lm15 mappings; need live provider bodies), Anthropic `CacheConfig(mode="auto")` (cause unknown, live).

## Verification

Tests live next to the code they pin (`test_streaming.py`, `test_lm_async_execution.py`, `test_lm_schema_conversion.py`, `test_lm.py`, `test_base_module.py`). Full suite 1907 passed; private matrix Python 3.10–3.14 all green, local-model live 5/5. 



**Also in this PR** (found by the failing Dependency Range check): `save(modules_to_serialize=...)` registered modules with cloudpickle by value and never unregistered — process-wide state keyed by module name. The registration is now scoped to the active saves, reference-counted under a lock so overlapping saves share it.

title: fix: preserve versioned docs trailing slashes
body:
## What changed

Replace Vercel's built-in `trailingSlash` option in the generated deployment config with explicit redirects that:

- preserve trailing slashes for exact release and minor-version roots such as `/3.3.1/` and `/3.3/`;
- retain the existing trailing-slash behavior for ordinary extensionless documentation routes;
- leave static files with extensions unchanged.

## Why

Vercel treats the final segment of `/3.3.1/` as if `.1` were a file extension. Despite `trailingSlash: true`, production therefore redirects `/3.3.1/` to `/3.3.1`. Relative CSS and JavaScript URLs then resolve from the domain root and return 404s, so exact historical-version homepages render without styling.

The explicit release redirect handles the exception while the extensionless-path redirect preserves the behavior that `trailingSlash: true` previously supplied everywhere else. No archived documentation HTML is rebuilt or modified.

## Rollout

After merge, the documentation workflow publishes the generated `vercel.json` to `krypticmouse/dspy-docs`. Vercel then deploys that repository commit. This uses the same GitHub App path that published the static-root configuration; no direct maintainer write to the deployment repository is required.

## Validation

- `PYTHONPATH=/tmp/dspy-vercel-hotfix /home/user/workspace/repo/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/docs/test_versioned_docs.py -q` — 10 passed
- `uv run ruff check docs/scripts/publish_versioned_docs.py tests/docs/test_versioned_docs.py` — passed
- Generated `vercel.json` validates against Vercel's published JSON schema.
- Both redirects compile with `@vercel/routing-utils@6.5.0` into strict, end-anchored 308 routes; assertions cover `/3.3.1`, `/3.3.1/`, `/3.4.0b1`, `/3.3`, `/current`, nested routes, and static assets.

title: fix: serve versioned docs from static root
body:
## Summary

Serve the Mike-managed documentation tree committed to the deployment repository instead of letting Vercel rebuild the legacy MkDocs source tree.

The versioned deployment PR merged successfully and Vercel deployed its merge commit, but production still returned the rebuilt legacy homepage while `/versions.json`, `/current/`, and `/3.3.1/` returned 404. The deployment repository contains all of those files. Its existing Vercel project-level build/output settings were therefore taking precedence over the checked-in static tree.

This updates the existing generated `vercel.json` source of truth to:

- replace the legacy build command with the explicit no-op command `true`;
- serve the repository root (`.`), where Mike stores the aggregate site.

Changing the publisher is necessary because it owns `vercel.json` and would overwrite a deployment-repository-only fix on the next Current or release publication.

## What happens when this merges

The existing docs workflow republishes Current to deployment `master`, including the corrected `vercel.json`. Vercel then redeploys the already-reviewed Material Current and historical snapshots. No documentation content, renderer, URL, or version policy changes in this PR.

## Validation

- `tests/docs/test_versioned_docs.py` — 10 passed
- Ruff and `git diff --check` pass
- the repository-level Mike test now asserts `framework: null`, `buildCommand: "true"`, and `outputDirectory: "."`

title: Declare HTTP providers to the native engine: one binding per LM, a fallback that keeps the connection
body:
Follows #10441 (merged). Uses lm15 `RouterConfig(providers=...)` from #10440.

## What this adds

`dspy.lm15.register_provider(...)` lets you declare an OpenAI-compatible (or Anthropic-compatible) HTTP provider that lm15 doesn't have built in — Fireworks, a company gateway — and then use it like any built-in one:

```python
dspy.lm15.register_provider(
    ProviderDefinition.chat(
        AccessPolicy(provider="fireworks", auth_modes=("bearer",), env_keys=("FIREWORKS_API_KEY",),
                     base_url="https://api.fireworks.ai/inference/v1"),
        compat=OpenAIChatCompat(max_tokens_field="max_tokens"),
        aliases=("fireworks-ai",),              # so "fireworks_ai/..." also works
    ),
    metadata_namespaces=("fireworks_ai",),      # use the fireworks_ai entries of the model-metadata snapshot for capabilities and prices
)
lm = dspy.LM("fireworks/accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4p1-flash", api_key=...)
```

`api_key`/`api_base`/`timeout` work, the env var is read if no key is given, `engine="auto"` and `"lm15"` work, saving/loading needs nothing extra (state is just the model string). This replaces writing a custom engine for such providers.

## Rules a reviewer should know

1. **Each `dspy.LM` snapshots the registry when it is constructed** and uses that snapshot for everything (routing, capabilities, pricing, sync and async engines). Registering or replacing a provider later does not affect existing LMs. Register at import time.
2. **If a call falls back to LiteLLM** (e.g. you passed `extra_headers`), it still goes to the declared URL with the declared key, via LiteLLM's generic `openai/` (or `anthropic/`) door. The alias is never given to LiteLLM as a provider prefix — LiteLLM's own `fireworks_ai/` would point at public Fireworks, not your gateway.
3. **The fallback only supports bearer auth on `openai/` and `x-api-key` on `anthropic/`.** A provider declared with another auth scheme gets an error instead of a fallback. Native calls still work for it.
4. **A refusal caused by your own compat declaration is final under `engine="auto"`** — DSPy will not "try LiteLLM anyway", because that would silently drop the setting your declaration said the server can't take.
5. **Aliases don't grant metadata.** Capabilities and prices come only from `metadata_namespaces=` (explicit) or from `supports=`/`models=` statements. Unknown stays "unsupported"; unpriced stays "unknown cost".
6. `FIREWORKS_API_BASE`-style env vars do not redirect a declared provider (they do for built-in ones).

title: Custom engines own their connection: refuse client settings at every door, save through engine state
body:
Follow-up to #10409. Fixes the custom-engine problems found in the Fireworks gauntlet (cmpnd-ai/breaka-your-lm, `CUSTOM_ENGINE_FINDINGS.md`).

**Scope.** This PR is only about custom engine objects (`dspy.LM(engine=MyEngine())`) — backends that are not an HTTP provider, like a CLI or an in-process model. If your backend *is* an OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible HTTP provider that lm15 doesn't list, don't write an engine: declare it with `dspy.lm15.register_provider(...)` instead — that's #10442 (stacked on this one), building on the lm15 `RouterConfig(providers=...)` vendored in #10440.

## What changes

**1. `api_key`, `api_base`, `timeout`, `extra_headers` etc. are now rejected when you use a custom engine.**
Before, `dspy.LM("x", engine=MyEngine(), api_key="k")` silently ignored the key: the engine used its own. Now it raises `ValueError`. Same on `lm.copy(api_key=...)` and on `lm("hi", api_key=...)`. Put those settings on the engine object instead. Built-in engines (`engine="auto"/"lm15"/"litellm"`) are unchanged.

**2. `lm.copy(engine=...)` replaces both the sync and async engine.**
Before, `copy(engine="litellm")` kept the old custom `async_engine`, so sync calls went to LiteLLM and async calls to the custom engine. Now `engine=` replaces the pair; pass `async_engine=` too if you want one. Also: the sync engine's `complete` must be a normal function, the async one's must be `async def`. Wrong kind is rejected at construction, not on the first call.

**3. Custom engines can now be saved and loaded.**
Give the engine `dump_state() -> dict` and `@classmethod load_state(state)`. `lm.dump_state()` then records the class path and that dict. Loading imports the class, so like custom LM classes it needs `allow_unsafe_lm_state=True`. `dump_state()` fails early if the class can't be imported back (e.g. defined inside a function) or the state isn't JSON. A class defined in a notebook (`__main__`) only loads in that same session — documented.

## Worth a reviewer's attention

- The refusal in (1) is a hard error with no deprecation warning. Reason: the `engine=` interface is new in 3.4 RC, nobody ships on it yet, and the old behaviour was a silent wrong-credential bug.
- Rule (1) is enforced in three places: `LM.__init__`, `LM.copy`, and `execution.prepare` (every call). If you touch call preparation, keep the third one.
- Two ReActV2-under-`streamify` tests are added. They show the streaming path works with native tool calls and fails the same way as non-streaming when the model writes the tool call as text. They do *not* explain the gauntlet's live failure.

## Tests

`tests/clients/test_custom_engine_contract.py` (33), `tests/streaming/test_react_v2_native_tool_stream.py` (2). Full suite passes; private matrix Python 3.10–3.14 green.

body:
Vendoring only: `scripts/update_vendored_lm15.py main` against `cmpnd-ai/lm15-python`, no DSPy code changes.

**lm15 change vendored** (`cd5d4d7` → `a550dab`, version still `1.0.0rc3`, contract pin unchanged at `7677980`):

- `RouterConfig(providers=(ProviderDefinition.chat(access, compat=...), ...))` declares a provider lm15's registry does not list (a gateway, a service not yet receipted) as the same pure-data triple a registry entry is. It routes by id and aliases (`id:model`, `id/model`), takes `api_keys`/`base_urls`, shares the router's pool and timeouts, plans without a key. `Resolution.declared` is true and `describe()` says "no lm15 receipts". A spelling a registry entry or litellm prefix already uses is refused at config time.
- `Resolution` carries `credential_policy` and `placeholder_key`, so `describe()` reads the resolution rather than the module tables (greptile's finding on the first revision of this PR); a declared non-hosted entry must be key-based, since the OAuth policies need their own adapter class.

Files: `dspy/_vendor/lm15/registry.py`, `dspy/_vendor/lm15/router.py`, `dspy/_vendor/lm15-provenance.txt`.

Why: the Fireworks custom-engine findings (cmpnd-ai/breaka-your-lm `CUSTOM_ENGINE_FINDINGS.md`) showed the engine rebuilding lm15's access-policy + compat-preset pair by hand to reach a provider the registry lacks, and losing `api_key`/`api_base`/`timeout` handling in the process. A follow-up DSPy PR exposes this as `dspy.lm15.register_provider(...)` and tightens the custom-engine contract; this PR only brings the dependency in.

Checks run locally: `tests/clients`, `tests/streaming`, `tests/test_vendored_lm15.py`, `tests/test_lm15_subtree_updater.py` — 673 passed, 21 skipped.

title: docs: add OrcaReplay to Providers and Integrations (record and replay a DSPy run offline)
body:
Adds one row to **Providers and Integrations** in `docs/docs/community/built-with-dspy.md`. The page says it is community-maintained and invites a PR, so here is one.

**Disclosure: I maintain OrcaReplay.** Apache-2.0, Node 20+, `npm i -g orcareplay`.

## What I measured before claiming an integration

The only thing that decides whether an external recorder works with DSPy is which base-URL variable actually redirects the call. I did not want to write "compatible" and hope, so I checked: a local HTTP server on `127.0.0.1:9971` that returns a canned chat-completion and logs the path it is asked for, then each candidate variable pointed at it.

```
dspy 3.3.1, litellm 1.101.0

OPENAI_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:9971/v1  ->  hit ['/v1/chat/completions'], program received ['ok']
OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9971/v1  ->  hit ['/v1/chat/completions'], program received ['ok']
```

**Both spellings redirect**, and the program gets the response back, so `dspy.LM('openai/…')` is capturable without changing a line of your program:

```console
orca record generic-openai -- python your_program.py
orca replay last                  # the same run, no provider contacted, nothing spent
```

That is not a given — the same probe against other frameworks found ones that honour only one of the two names, and one that ignores both because it pins the origin in its own config. For DSPy the answer happens to be the easy one, which is why it seemed worth stating in the row rather than leaving a reader to find out.

## Why it is useful here specifically

Optimizer runs make a lot of model calls and the interesting failure is usually several compile steps back. A recording lets the same run happen again offline at no cost, and `orca replay last --from N --model <other>` replays the prefix from the recording and then continues on a different model, so the model is the only variable rather than one of several.

## What I am not claiming

- **A matching replay is not a determinism result.** It proves the recorded exchange reproduces — not that your program, the optimizer, or the model is deterministic.
- **Replay blocks model-provider egress only. It is not a sandbox**; recorded tool calls still execute for real.
- **The default adapter does not capture embedding calls.** That matters more for DSPy than for most frameworks: a retriever-heavy program can replay cleanly at the LM layer and still not reproduce the behaviour you were chasing.

I put the row under *Providers and Integrations* rather than *Open-Source Projects* because OrcaReplay is not built with DSPy — it records DSPy — which is the same relationship Langfuse, Langtrace, OpenLIT and Arize have on that table.

`git diff --numstat` is `1  0` — one row appended, nothing else touched.
